Consequently we, with our said brethren and others of our council, consulted together, and by their common counsel declared to the said Sir John Oldcastle what the holy Roman Church, following the sayings of the blessed Augustine, Jerome and Ambrose and of other saints, has determined in this matter, which determinations all Catholics ought to observe. To this Sir John responded that he was willing to believe and observe whatever the holy Church determined, and whatever God wished him to believe and observe. But whether our lord the Pope, the cardinals, archbishops, bishops and other prelates of the Church had the power to determine such things, he was unwilling to affirm at that time in any way. Whence we, still feeling compassion for him, in hope of better deliberation, resolved to

units.la: Sed de scri ptura Dei nullum uer bum.
units.tr: But nothing about the Scripture of God.

units.la: Foris agni intus lupi rapaces. promisimus eidem domino Ioanni, quod certas determinationes, in materia antedicta, ac super quibus idem dominus Ioannes debuit clarius respondere, sibi ederemus in scriptis, terminis latinis, pro leuiori intellectu eiusdem, in Anglicum translatis, super quibus iubebamus eundem, ac cordialiter rogauimus, ut in die lunae proximo tunc sequente, plene & clare suum daret responsum, quas quidem determinationes eodem die transferre fecimus, ac eidem die dominica proxima sequenti realiter liberari, quarum determinationum tenor sequitur, & est talis. Fides ac determinatio sanctae ecclesiae Catholicae de sacrosancto sacramento altaris est haec, quod post consecrationem in missa a sacerdote factam, materialis panis commutetur in materiale corpus Christi. Vinumque materiale in materialem sanguinem Christi, Itaque iam nec panis, nec uini, post consecrationem ulla manet substantia, quæ prius aderat. Quid huic respondes articulo? Item sancta ecclesia determinauit quòd quemlibet oportet Christianum in terris degentę peccata sacerdoti per ecclesiam ordinato cõfiteri, fi liceat accedere, ut hūc fentis articulũ? Christus ordinauit fanctū Petrum suum uicarium in terris, cuius sedes est ec clefia Romana, concedens ac permittens eandem autoritatem, quam tribuit Petro, & omnibus Petri fucceffioribus, quæ nunc dicuntur Papæ Romani, quorum potestate in ecclesijs particularibus ordinantur ac constituuntur prælati, utpote Archiepiscopi, Episcopi, Curati, Ceterique gradus ecclesiastici, quibus Christianus populus debet obedientiam, iuxta traditiones Romanæ ecclesiæ. Hæc est determinatio sanctæ ecclesiæ, ut fentis huncarticulum? Ad hæc sacrosancta ecclesia de termi-
units.tr: Lambs without, ravening wolves within. We promised the said Sir John that we would give him in writing certain determinations in the aforesaid matter, on which the said Sir John ought to answer more clearly. These were written in Latin terms and translated into English for easier understanding. We urged him earnestly to give a full and clear answer on the Monday following. We had these determinations transcribed that same day and actually delivered to him on the next Sunday. The tenor of these determinations follows, and is as follows: "The faith and determination of the holy Catholic Church concerning the most holy sacrament of the altar is this: that after the consecration made in the mass by the priest, material bread is changed into the material body of Christ, and material wine into the material blood of Christ, so that now no substance of bread or wine remains after the consecration, which was present before. What do you answer to this article? Likewise the holy Church has determined that every Christian living on earth ought to confess his sins to a priest ordained by the Church, if it is possible to approach one: do you hold this article? Christ ordained St Peter his vicar on earth, whose seat is the Roman Church, granting and permitting the same authority which he gave to Peter and to all Peter's successors, who are now called Roman Popes, by whose power prelates are appointed and constituted in the particular churches, namely archbishops, bishops, parish priests and the other ecclesiastical grades, to whom the Christian people owe obedience according to the traditions of the Roman Church. Is this the determination of the holy Church; do you hold this article? Further, the most holy Church has determined"

units.la: terminauit, quod sit necessariū cuiuis Christiano peregrinari ad sancta loca, ibique maxime adorare sanctas reliquias apostolorum, martyrum, ac confessorum, omniumque sanctorum, quoscunq; approbauit Romana ecclesia, ut hunc sentis articulum: Quo die lunæ uidelicet 25. die dicti mensis Septembris, coram nobis, ac confratribus nostris prædictis, adiunctoque uenerabili fratre nostro Benedicto, Dei gratia Bangorensi episcopo, Iussu & mandato nostro, Consiliarij & ministri nostri, uidelicet Magister Henricus Vuare, Curię nostrę Cantuariensi officialis. Philippus Morgan, utriusque iuris Doctor, Houuelius, Kyffyn decretorum, Io. Kemp, et Vuilh, Karleton, legum doctores, ac Ioan. Vuitnam, Thom. Palmer, Rob. Vuombeuuell, Ioannes Vuithead, Rob. Chamberlayne, Ricar. Dodyngtone, & Thomas Vualde sacræ paginæ professores, necnon Iac. Cole, & Ioan. Steuyns notarij nostri in hac parte assumpti, iurati e-rant omnes, et singulí ad sancta Dei Euangelia, tacto libro, quod de & super materia prædicta, ac in tota causa huiusmodi, suum fidele con-silium, & ministerium præberent, atque toto mundo. Consequenterq; comparuit dictus dominus Roberº tus de Morlay miles, custos turris London. ac præfatum dominum Ioannem Oldcastellum secum adduxit, & coram nobis statuit. Cui nobis affabiliter & suauiter recitaui mus acta prioris diei, ac ut prius recitauimus quomodo excomunicatus fuerat, & est, idem dominus Io. acrogauimus & requisiuimus eundem, quatenus peteret & admitteret in forma debita ecclesiæ absolutionem. Cui idem dominus Ioan. expresse respondit tunc ibide, quod nullam absolutionem in hac parte peteret à nobis,sed à solo Deo.Con sequenter nos suaui & modestomo do rogauimus,& requisiuimus eun dem dominum Ioannem, quatenus de & super articulis sibi oppositis suum clarum daret responsum, & primo circa sacramentum Euchari-stiae. Ad quem articulum inter cae-tera dixit, & respondit, quod sicut Christus hic in terra degens, habuit in se diuinitatem & humanitatem, diuinitatem tamen uelatam & inui-sibilem sub humanitate, quae in eo aperta & uisibilis fuerat,sic in sacra-mento altaris est uerum corpus, & uerus panis, panis uidelicet quem uidemus, & corpus Christi sub eo-dem uelatum quod non uidemus, ac fidem circa sacramentum huius-modi in schedula praedicta, sibi per nos transmissa per sanctam Roma-nam ecclesiam, & doctores sanctos determinatā expresse negauit, de-terminatione ecclesiae fore, aut esse. Sed si est determinatio ecclesiae, dixit, quod est facta contra sacram scripturam, et postquam ecclesia fuit dotata, et venenum effusum in ecclesia, et non ante. Quo etiam ad sacrum poenitentiae, et confessionis, dixit & asseruit expresse, tunc ibidem, quod si quis in aliquo graui peccato constitutus, a quo ipse surgere nesciuit, expediret, et bonum esset sibi adire aliquem sanctum, et discretum sacerdotem, pro consilio ab eo habendo. Sed quod confiteretur peccatum suum proprio, ceu alteri presbitero, etiamsi haberet copiam eiusdem, non est necessarium ad salutem, quia sola contritione, peccatum huiusmodi deleri posset, et ipse peccator purgari. Circa adorationem sanctae crucis, dixit, et asseruit tunc ibidem, quod solum corpus Christi, quod pendebat in cruce debuit adorari, quia illud corpus solum fuit, et est cruxadoranda. Et interrogatus, quem honorem faceret imagini ipsius crucis, respondit uerbis expressis, quod illum solum honorem faceret sibi, quod bene mundaret eam, & poneret in bona custodia. Quo ad potestatem clavium, dominum nostrum Papam, archiepiscopos, episcopos, et alios prælatos: dixit quod Papa est uerus Antichristus: hoc est caput eiusdem archiepisc. & episc. necnon alij prælati membra, & fratres cauda eiusdem. Quibus Papae archiepiscopis, & prælatis non est obediendum, nisi quatenus fuerint imitatores Christi, & Petri in uita, moribus & conuersatione, et quod ipse est successor Petri, qui est in uita melior, & morib°s purior, & nullus alius. Vlterius dixit idem dominus Ioannes alta uoce, manibus expansis, alloquendo circumstantes. Isti qui iudicant, et uolunt damnare me, seducent uos omnes, & se ipsos, et uos ducet ad infernum, ideo caueatis a beis. Quibus bus sic per eum dictis nos iterum, acsepius,flebiliuultu, Dictum dominum Ioannem alloquebamur e-undem, uerbis quibus potuimus, exhortando,ut ad unitatem ecclesiae redire, crederet & teneret quod ecclesia Romana credit & tenet: qui respondebat expresse, se aliter non credere, nec tenere, quam superius expressit. Videntes ergo quod in eo, prout apparuit, proficere non potuimus, tandem cum cordis amaritudine processimus ad sententiae diffinitiue prolationem, in hunc modum, In Dei nomine Amen. Nos Thomas, permissione diuina, sanctae Cantuariensis ecclesiae archiepiscopus & minister humilis, totius Angliae primas, & Apostolicae sedis legatus. In quadam causa, siue negocio haereticae prauitatis, de & super diuersis articulis, super quibus dominus Ioannes Oldcastellus miles, dominus de Cobham, coram nobis
units.tr: It was determined that it is necessary for every Christian to make pilgrimages to holy places, and there especially to venerate the sacred relics of the apostles, martyrs and confessors, and of all the saints whom the Roman Church has approved, as your sentence holds. On Monday, the 25th day of the said month of September, before us and our aforesaid brethren, with the venerable brother Benedict, by the grace of God bishop of Bangor, joined to us, by our order and command, our counsellors and ministers, namely Master Henry Ware, official of our Court of Canterbury; Philip Morgan, Doctor of both laws; Howell and Kyffyn, Doctors of Decretals; John Kemp and William Karleton, Doctors of Laws; and John Whitnam, Thomas Palmer, Robert Wombwell, John Whithead, Robert Chamberlayne, Richard Dodyngton and Thomas Walde, professors of sacred theology; and also James Cole and John Stevens, our notaries assumed for this purpose: all of them, each one, were sworn on the holy Gospels of God, with hand on the book, that they would give their faithful counsel and service concerning the aforesaid matter and in the whole cause of this kind, and to the whole world. Next, the said Lord Robert de Morlay, knight, keeper of the Tower of London, appeared and brought the aforesaid Lord John Oldcastle with him and presented him before us. We addressed him kindly and gently, and recited to him the acts of the previous day, and as we had recited before, how he had been excommunicated, and still is; we urged and required the same Lord John that he should seek and accept, in due form of the Church, absolution. The same Lord John replied then and there expressly that he would seek no absolution from us in this matter, but from God alone. Consequently we, gently and mildly, asked and required the same Lord John that he should give his clear answer concerning the articles put to him, and first concerning the sacrament of the Eucharist. To this article, among other things, he said and replied that just as Christ, while living on earth, had in himself divinity and humanity, the divinity however veiled and invisible under the humanity, which in him was open and visible, so in the sacrament of the altar there is the true body and the true bread: the bread, namely, which we see, and the body of Christ veiled under the same, which we do not see. He expressly denied that the faith concerning this sacrament, determined by the holy Roman Church and the holy doctors, and sent to him by us in the aforesaid schedule, was or is the determination of the Church. "But if it is a determination of the Church," he said, "it is made against holy Scripture, and after the Church was endowed, and poison was poured into the Church, and not before." As to the sacrament of penance and confession, he also said and expressly asserted, then and there, that if anyone, held in some grave sin from which he did not know how to rise, it would be expedient and good for him to go to some holy and discreet priest to take counsel from him; but that to confess his sin to his own priest, or to another elder, even if he had the opportunity of doing so, is not necessary for salvation, because sin of this kind could be blotted out by contrition alone, and the sinner himself cleansed. Concerning the adoration of the holy cross, he said and asserted then and there that only the body of Christ which hung on the cross ought to be adored, because that body alone was and is the cross to be adored. And being asked what honour he paid to the image of the cross itself, he replied in express words that the only honour he paid it was to clean it well and keep it in good custody. As to the power of the keys, he said of our lord the Pope, the archbishops, bishops and other prelates: that the Pope is the true Antichrist; that the archbishops and bishops are his head, the other prelates his members, and the friars his tail. The Popes, archbishops and prelates are not to be obeyed, except insofar as they are imitators of Christ and Peter in life, manners and conduct; and that he himself is the successor of Peter, who is better in life and purer in morals, and no other. Furthermore the same Lord John said in a loud voice, with hands outstretched, addressing those standing around: "Those who judge and want to condemn me will deceive you all and themselves, and will lead you to hell; therefore beware of them." When he had said these things, we again and often, with a sorrowful face, addressed the same Lord John, exhorting him in whatever words we could to return to the unity of the Church and to believe and hold what the Roman Church believes and holds. He answered expressly that he did not believe or hold otherwise than he had declared above. Seeing therefore that, as it appeared, we could make no progress with him, at last with bitterness of heart we proceeded to the pronouncement of a definitive sentence, in this manner: In the name of God, Amen. We, Thomas, by divine permission archbishop of the holy Church of Canterbury and a humble minister, primate of all England and legate of the Apostolic See, in a certain cause or business of heretical depravity, concerning various articles on which the Lord John Oldcastle, knight, Lord of Cobham, before us,

units.la: Ridicula hypocrisis. Humiles se vocant qui Regibus imperant & orbis occupant tyrannidem. nobis in ultima conuocatione cleri, nostrae Cantuarienfis prouinciae, in ecclesia sancti Pauli, Londini celebrata, post inquisitionem diligentem ibidem,inde captam, detectus & delatus extiterat, & per nostram Cantuarienfem prouinciam notorie & publice diffamatus,ad denuncia tionem,et requifitionem totius cleri praedicti, in eadem conuocatione praedicta, inde nobis facta,fauore possibili (Deo teste) quo potuimus legitime procedentes contra eundem,ac Christi uestigijs inhærendo, qui non uult mortem peccatoris, sed ut magis conuertatur & uiuat, nitebamur eudem corrigere,ac uijs et modis, quibus potuimus atque sciuimus reducere ad ecclesiae unitatem, declarantes eidem,quod in hac parte, sancta Romana et uniuer salis ecclesia docet, tenet, determinauit et praedicat. Et quamuis eundem in fide Catholica deuium inuenerimus, nerimus, adeo duræ ceruicis, quod errorem suum noluit confiteri, aut se purgare de eodem, nec etiam detestari, eidem paterno nihilominus compatientes affectu, ac ipsius salutem cordialiter affectantes, præsiximus eidem certum terminū competentem ad deliberandum, & si uoluisset pœnitendum, et reformandum seipsum, ac demum eo quod eundem considerauerimus incorrigibilem seruatis primitus quæ in hac parte de iure requiruntur, cum dolore & amaritudine cordis ad diffinitiuæ sententiæ prolationem procedimus in hunc modum.
units.tr: Ridiculous hypocrisy! They call themselves humble, who rule over kings and seize the tyranny of the world. Was in the last convocation of the clergy of our province of Canterbury, celebrated in the church of St Paul in London, after a diligent inquiry made there, detected and denounced, and by our province of Canterbury notoriously and publicly defamed, at the denunciation and request of the whole aforesaid clergy, made to us in the same convocation; proceeding lawfully against him, with all possible favour (God is witness), and following the footsteps of Christ, who does not will the death of a sinner but rather that he be converted and live, we strove to correct him, and by whatever ways and means we could and knew, to bring him back to the unity of the Church, declaring to him that in this matter the holy Roman and universal Church teaches, holds, has determined and preaches. And although we found him straying from the Catholic faith, and so stiff-necked that he would not confess his error, nor purge himself of it, nor even detest it, yet, feeling paternal compassion for him and cordially desiring his salvation, we granted him a fixed and suitable term to deliberate, and, if he wished, to repent and reform himself; and at last, since we judged him incorrigible, having first observed what is required by law in this matter, we proceed with grief and bitterness of heart to the pronouncement of a definitive sentence in this manner.

units.la: Christi nomine inuocato, ipsumque solum habetes præ oculis, quia per acta inactitata, producta, exhibita signa, euidentias, et inditia diuersa, insuper probationum genera reperimus eundem dominum Ioannem militem, fore et esse hæreticum, hæreticisque credentem in fide, et obserobseruantia sacrosanctæ Romanæ, & universalis ecclesiæ, & præsertim circa sacramenta Eucharistiæ, & poenitentiæ. Quod tanquam iniquitatis, & tenebrarum filius, in tantum obdurauit cor suum, ut non intelligat uocem sui pastoris, nec uelit monitionibus allici, nec reduci blandiciis. Inuestigatis primitus rimatis, & diligenter pensatis meritis causæ antedictæ, ipsiusque domini Io. de meritis culpis, per ipsius damnabilem perti nacia aggrauatis. Noletes quod is, qui nequam est, fiat nequior, et alios inficiat sua labe, de consilio, & assensu magnæ discretionis, & sapientiæ uirorum uenerabilium fratrum nostrorum, dominorum Ricad. London. Henrici Vuinton. & Benedicti Bangoren. episcoporum, & aliorum nonnullorum in sacra Theologia Decretis & Iure Ciuili Doctorum, aliarumque religiosarum & peritarum personarum, nobis assi-
units.tr: Calling upon the name of Christ, and keeping him alone before our eyes, because through the acts recorded, the documents produced, the signs, evidences and indications of various kinds, and moreover the kinds of proof we have found, we find that the said Lord John, knight, is and has been a heretic, believing heretically and not observing the most holy Roman and universal Church, and especially concerning the sacraments of the Eucharist and penance. Being, as a son of iniquity and darkness, so hardened in heart that he does not understand the voice of his shepherd, nor will be drawn by admonitions, nor brought back by flattery; having first investigated and diligently weighed the merits of the aforesaid cause, and the faults of the said Lord John, aggravated by his damnable obstinacy; not willing that he who is wicked should become more wicked and infect others with his stain, by the counsel and assent of the great discretion and wisdom of our venerable brothers, the lords Richard of London, Henry of Winchester and Benedict of Bangor, bishops, and of some others, doctors in sacred theology, in the decrees and in civil law, and of other religious and experienced persons assisting us,

units.la: Qui ponunt lucem in tenebras, et tenebras in lucem.
units.tr: They put light for darkness, and darkness for light.

units.la: assistentium, prælatum dominum Ioannem Oldcastellum militem, dominum de Cobham, de et super huiusmodi detestabili reatu conuictu, et ad ecclesiæ unitatem, pœnitentia liter redire nolentem, hæreticum, ac in his, quæ tenet, docet, determinauit prædicat sacrosancta Romana et uniuersalis ecclesia, & præsertim in articulis supra scriptis errantem, iudicauimus, declarauimus, & condemnauimus sententialiter, & diffini ue in his scriptis, relinquentes eundem ex nunc tanquam hæreticum iudicio seculari. Ipsumque nihilominus hæreticum, omnesque alios & sigulos qui eundem de cætero in fui fauorem erroris receptauerit, uel receptauerint, defensauerit, seu defensauerint, sibi cosilium, auxilium seu fauorem in hac parte præbuit uel præbuerint tanquam fautores, receptatores & defensatores hæreticorum excomunicauimus, & excommuni-
units.tr: ...the assisting prelates, we, having judged, declared and condemned by sentence, and in these writings define, Sir John Oldcastle, knight, Lord of Cobham, convicted of this detestable crime and unwilling to return penitently to the unity of the Church, to be a heretic, and erring in those things which he holds, teaches, preaches and determines, especially in the articles written above, as the most holy Roman and universal Church preaches. We leave the same man from now on as a heretic to the secular judgment. Moreover, we excommunicate him as a heretic, together with all and each of those who have received, defended, or given counsel, aid or favour to him in this matter, in favour of his error, as receivers, favourers and defenders of heretics; and we also declare them excommunicated in these writings. And so that what has been set forth above may become known to all who believe in Christ, we commit and commend to your brotherhood that you declare, publish and set forth, in your church, throughout your cities and dioceses, through each of your parish priests in their own churches, when the greater crowd of people is present, in a loud and intelligible voice and in the mother tongue, as is more fully contained above in this process, that Sir John Oldcastle has been condemned by us as a heretic and schismatic, and as erring in the articles written above, and that all and each of those who have received, defended, or given counsel, aid or favour to him in this matter, in favour of his error, are excommunicated by your said definitive sentence as receivers, favourers and defenders of heretics.

units.la: Sic tradidē runt phas rifei Chri stum Pila to.
units.tr: So the Pharisees handed Christ over to Pilate.

units.la: Antiquū obtinent pharisæi. municatos denunciamus etiã in his scriptis. Et ut ista præmissa, omnibus in Christo credentibus innotescat, uestræ fraternitati committimus, & commendamus, quatenus præfatum dominum Ioannem Oldcastel lum, sicut præmittitur, per nos fuisse & esse damnatum hæreticum, schismaticum, & in articulis supra scriptis errantem, omnesque alios, & singulos, qui eundem dominum Iohannem de cetero in sui fauore erroris receptauerit, defensauerit, receptauerint uel defensauerint, aut sibi auxilium, consilium uel fauorem in hac parte præbuerit uel præbuerint, tanquam receptatores, fautores & defensatores hæreticorum, per dictam uestram sententiam diffiniti-uam excommunicatos, in ecclesia uestra, per uestras ciuitates & dioceses, per singulos subditos uestros curatos earundem, in ecclesiis suis, cum maior in eisdem affuerit popu-
units.tr: The Pharisees keep up the old custom. We also declare in these writings that they are excommunicated. And so that what has been set out above may become known to all who believe in Christ, we commit and commend it to your brotherhood, so that you may proclaim, publish and explain in your churches, throughout your cities and dioceses, through each of your parish priests in their own churches, when the greater crowd of people is present, that the aforesaid lord John Oldcastle, as has been said, has been condemned by us as a heretic, a schismatic and one who errs in the articles written above, and that all others, each and every one, who have received, defended, or given aid, counsel or favour in this matter to the same lord John, in support of his error, are excommunicated by your definitive sentence as receivers, favourers and defenders of heretics.

units.la: P li multitudo, alta & intelligibili uoce, & in lingua materna, prout supra seriosius continetur in hoc processu, declarent, publicent & exponent, ut sic opiniones erroneæ populi, qui aliter concepit forte in hac materia, quemadmodum se habet rei veritas, hac declaratione publica, rescindantur. Quod idem per uos, singulis confratribus nostris, nostrę Cantuariensis prouinciæ, suffraganeis de uerbo ad uerbum rescribi, & innotesci uolumus, & mandamus, ut ipsi omnes, & singulì per suas ciuitates & dioceceses modū & formam huius nostri processus, Dictam etiam per nos latā sententiam, & cætera omnia, & singula contenta in isdem publicent, intiment & declarēt, et consimiliter per subditos suos, et curatos faciant publicari. De die uero receptionis præsentium & quid feceritis in præmissis, & quo modo hoc nostrum mandatum fueritis. ritis, & fuerint executi, debitè & di‐stinctè certificetis, et certificet, dicto negocio expedito, literis uestris & suis patentibus, habentibus hunc tenorem. Datum in manerio de May deston 10, die mensis Octobris, Anno 1413. Et nostrę traslationis an. 18. Illud minimè silentio transigedum, qd a quibusdā fertur ab ipso dictū, se Heliæ quadā sorte defuncturum in terris, quod siue a uulgo temere natum, siue ab ipso prædictū, haud sine mente reor, aut sine numine diuum enatum esse rei exitus facile comprobat. Quemadmodum enim Helias mortalem uitam relicturus curru igneo in immortalem subuectus est, ita hanc illius decedendi figuram, & huius secuta est haud multum dissimilis moriendi necessitas. Quippe in furcam quasi in currum sublatus primum, tum circumdustus ignibus undique inflammatus, quaso quid aliud, quā Heliæ cuius damin cœlum subuolantis speciem præbuit sanctissimus Christi martyr,quippe qui ωυγοιντι πρὸς οὐρανον ἡλυθε̇ ἁιφρω. Huiusmodi sunt (pie lector) Vuicleuicæ doctrinæ fructus. Quos mundo prouentus ædit papistica sanctitas ipsi uideant. Si cuiusque drοctrinam suis fructibus metiri uelimus, hunc spectemus, quem cum infinitis aliis Vuicleui ter illa abominanda doctrina pepe rit. Sic enim ab ipso Vualdeno gra-uissimo utique aduersario accepi-mus ab ipso testatum Oldcastello, quemadmodū & supra commemo-ratum est, Haud unquam se aliter intellexisse quanta esset peccati la-bes ac uenenum, nisi ex Vuicleui audita uoce. Fertur nec sine huius consensu conclusiones has in parla-mentum adductas, quas idcirco hoc loco subnectendas curaui.
units.tr: Let them declare, publish and expound this, in a loud and intelligible voice and in the mother tongue, as is set out more fully above in this process, so that the erroneous opinions of the people, who may have formed a mistaken view on this matter, may be overturned by this public declaration, and the truth of the matter may be seen as it is. We wish and order that the same be copied word for word by you to each of our fellow bishops of our province of Canterbury and their suffragans, and made known, so that they all, and each of them, throughout their cities and dioceses, may publish, announce and declare the manner and form of this our process, the sentence pronounced by us, and all and each of the other matters contained in them, and likewise cause them to be published by their subjects and parish priests. You are to certify us duly and distinctly of the day on which you receive these presents, and of what you have done in the matters above, and in what manner this our mandate has been carried out, and when the business has been completed, by your letters and theirs under open seal, bearing this tenor. Given at the manor of Maidstone, on the 10th day of October, in the year 1413, and in the 18th year of our translation. Nor is it to be passed over in silence that it is reported by some that he said he would die on earth in the manner of Elijah. Whether this arose rashly from the common people, or was said by him, I think not without intention, nor without the will of God; the outcome of the event easily proves it. For just as Elijah, about to leave mortal life, was carried up to immortal life in a fiery chariot, so this manner of his departure, and a very similar necessity of dying, followed. For he was lifted up as if onto a chariot on the gallows, then surrounded and kindled with fire on every side, what else, I ask, did the most holy martyr of Christ present but the likeness of Elijah rising into heaven? [went up to heaven] Such are, pious reader, the fruits of Wycliffite teaching. Let the papistical holiness that produced them in the world look at them. If we wish to judge a doctrine by its fruits, let us look at this man, whom that abominable Wycliffite teaching brought forth along with countless others. For I have heard this attested by Walden himself, a most serious opponent, concerning Oldcastle, as has also been mentioned above: that he had never understood how great the stain and poison of sin was, except from hearing the voice of Wycliffe. It is reported that these conclusions, which I have taken care to append here, were brought before Parliament, not without his consent.

units.la: LIBELLVS CONCLVSIONVM exhibitus Parlamento Londini, Anno Ricardi secundi, 18. Anno Domini 1395.
units.tr: THE BOOK OF CONCLUSIONS presented to Parliament in London, in the eighteenth year of Richard II, in the year of our Lord 1395.

units.la: PRIMA CONCLVSIO. QVOD quando ecclesia Angliae incoepit delirare in temporalitate, secundum nouercam suam magnam ecclesiam Romanam, & ecclesiae fuerunt autorizatae, per appropriationem, diuersis locis fides, spes, charitas incoeperût fugere de ecclesia nostra, quia superbia cum sua dolorosa genealogia mortalium peccatorum uendicabat hoc, titulo ueritatis. Ista conclusio est generalis, & probata per experientiam, consuetudinem, ac modum sicut postea audietis.
units.tr: THE FIRST CONCLUSION. When the Church of England began to go astray in temporal matters, following its stepmother, the great Roman Church, and the churches were empowered through appropriation in various places, faith, hope and charity began to flee from our church, because pride, with its sorrowful offspring of mortal sins, claimed this under the title of truth. This conclusion is general, and is proved by experience, custom and manner, as you will hear afterwards.

units.la: Secunda. Quòd nostrum usuale sacerdotium, quod incoepit in Roma fictum, potestate Angelis altiore, non est istud sacerdotium quod Christus ordinauit suis Apostolis. Conclusio ista probatur quia sacerdotium Romanum factum est cum signis, ritibus & pontificalibus, benedictionibus, modicæ uirtutis, nullibi exemplaris in sacra scriptura, quia ordinale episcopi, & nouū Testamentum parum concordant. Et nos non uidemus, quòd spiritus sanctus, propter aliqua talia signa, consert aliquod donum, quia ipse, & omnia nobilia dona sua non possunt stare, cum mortali peccato in ulla persona. Corrollarium huius conclusionis est, quòd est dolorosum interludium hominibus sapientibus, uidere episcopos ludere cum spiritu sancto, in collatione suorum ordinum, quia ipsi dant coronas in caracteribus, loco alborum ceruorū, & hic character est Antichristi, introductus in sancta Ecclesiam ad colorandam ociositatem.
units.tr: Second: that our customary priesthood, which began in Rome as a fiction with power higher than that of the angels, is not the priesthood that Christ ordained for his apostles. This conclusion is proved because the Roman priesthood was made with signs, rites, pontifical blessings of little power, nowhere found as an example in Holy Scripture, since the ordinal of the bishops and the New Testament agree poorly. And we do not see that the Holy Spirit, on account of any such signs, bestows any gift, because he and all his noble gifts cannot dwell with mortal sin in any person. A corollary of this conclusion is that it is a sorrowful interlude for wise men to see bishops playing with the Holy Spirit in the conferring of their orders, since they give crowns in characters instead of white deer, and this character is the Antichrist's, introduced into holy Church to cover up idleness.

units.la: Tertia. Quod lex continentiae, iniun-
units.tr: Third. That the law of continence imposed on the priesthood, which was first ordained to the prejudice of women,

units.la: iniuncta sacerdotio, quae in praeiudicium mulierum prius fuit ordinata, inducit sodomiam, in totam sanctam Ecclesiam, sed nos excusamus uos per Biblia, quia suspectu decretum dicit, quod non nominaremus istud. Ratio & experientia probant istam conclusionem. Ratio, quia delicata cibaria uirorum ecclesiasticorum, uolunt habere naturalem purgationem, uel peiorem. Experientia, quia secreta probatio taliu hominum est, quod delectantur in mulieribus, & tu cum probaueris talem hominem, nota eum bene, quia ipse unus ex illis est. Corrollarium illius est, priuatae religiones et inceptores, siue origo istius peccati esset maxime digne adnullari, sed Deus de potentia sua immittet apertam uindictam.
units.tr: brings sodomy into the whole holy Church. But we excuse you by the Bible, since the decree says that we should not name it. Reason and experience prove this conclusion. Reason, because the delicate food of ecclesiastical men wants natural purging, or worse. Experience, because the secret mark of such men is that they delight in women, and when you have tested such a man, note him well, for he is one of them. A corollary of this is that private religious orders and their founders, whatever the origin of this sin, should most worthily be annulled; but God will by his power send open vengeance.

units.la: Quarta. Quod fictum miraculum sacramenti panis, inducit omnes homines, nisi sunt pauci in idololatria
units.tr: Fourth. That the fictitious miracle of the sacrament of bread leads all men, except a few, into idolatry,

units.la: Caelibatus sacerdotalis. triam, quia ipsi putant quod corpus, quod nunquam erit extra coelum, virtute verborum sacerdotis includetur essentialiter in parvo pane, quem ipsi offendunt populo. Sed utinam ipsi vellet credere, quod doctor Euangelicus dicit in suo Trialogo, quod panis altaris est habitualiter corpus Christi, quia nos suppo-nimus, quod per istum modum, potest quilibet fidelis homo, & mulier in domini lege facere sacramentum istius panis, sine aliquo tali miraculo. Corrollarium concludens est quod licet corpus Christi sit dotatum sempiterno gaudio, seruitium corporis Christi factum per fratrem Thomam non est uerum, sed pictum & plenum falsis miraculis, nec mirum, quia frater Thomas illo tempore tenens cum Papa, voluisset fecisse miraculum de ouo Gallinae, & nos cognoscimus bene quod quodlibet mendacium aperte praedicatum, uer-titad tit ad dedecus illius, qui semper ue-rax est, & sine aliquo defectu.
units.tr: (Celibacy of priests.) ...three, because they think that the body, which will never be outside heaven, is essentially enclosed by the power of the priest's words in the small bread which they offer to the people. But would that they would believe what the evangelical doctor says in his Trialogue, that the altar bread is habitually the body of Christ, since we suppose that in this way any faithful man or woman can, under the law of the Lord, make the sacrament of this bread without any such miracle. A concluding corollary is that, although the body of Christ is endowed with everlasting joy, the service of the body of Christ made by brother Thomas is not true, but painted and full of false miracles. Nor is this surprising, since brother Thomas at that time, holding with the Pope, wished to make a miracle out of a hen's egg; and we know well that every lie openly preached tends to the dishonour of him who is always truthful and without any defect.

units.la: Quinta. Quod exorcismi & be-nedictiones factae super uinum, panem, aquam & oleum, sal, incen-sum, lapidem altaris, & ecclesiae mu-ros, super uestimentum, calicem, mi-tram, crucem & baculos peregrino-rum, sunt uera practica nicromanti-ç, potius quam sacrae Theologiae. Ista conclusio probatur sic, quia per tales exorcismos, creaturae honoran-tur, esse altioris uirtutis, quam sint in natura sua propria, et nos non ui-demus aliquid mutationis in aliqua creatura, quae est sic exorcisata, nisi per falsam fidem, quod est principa-le artis diabolicae. Corrollarium, quod si liber exorcisandi aquam be-nedictam lectus in ecclesia, esset to-tus fidelis, nos cogitamus ueraciter, quod aqua benedicta usitata in sa-cra ecclesia, foret optima medicina, pro omnimodis languoribus, & ulceribus, cuius contrarium indies experimur.
units.tr: Seventh. That spiritual prayers made in our church for the souls of the dead, preferring one by name, are a false foundation of almsgiving, upon which all the almshouses of England have been wickedly founded. This conclusion is proved by two arguments. The first is that a meritorious prayer of some worth ought to be a work proceeding from high charity; and perfect charity accepts no person, since you shall love your neighbour as yourself. Wherefore it appears that the good of a temporal gift conferred on priests and on almshouses is the principal cause of a special prayer, which is not far from simony. The other argument is that a special prayer made for men condemned to eternal punishment is very displeasing to God, and although it is doubtful, it is probable to the faithful Christian people that the founders of almshouses, because of their poisonous endowment, have for the most part passed by the broad way. A corollary is that a prayer of worth, proceeding from perfect charity, would embrace in general all whom God wished to have saved, and would abandon the customary market-like way of special prayers made for beggars, landholders and other hired priests, who are a vigorous people for working and serving the whole realm, now kept idle, since it was proved in one book which the King had that a hundred almshouses suffice for the whole realm; and from this there would arise greater possible increase for the temporal part.

units.la: Sexta. Quod Rex & episcopus in una persona, praelatus & iudex in temporalibus causis, curatus & officiarius in mundano officio, facit quodlibet regnum extra bonum regimen. Ista conclusio aperte ostenditur, quia temporale & spirituale sunt duae partes totius Ecclesiae sanctae, & ideo iste, qui potuit se ad unum, non intromittat se ad alterum, quia nemo potest duobus dominis servire. Videtur quod Amphrodita vel Ambodextri essent bona nomina, pro talibus hominibus duplicis status. Corollarium est, quod inde nos procuratores Dei, in ista causa prosequimur Parlamentum, quo statuatur, ut omnes ecclesiastici, tam superiores quam inferiores sint plene excusati, & occupent se cum cura sua, & nulla alia.
units.tr: Eighth. That pilgrimages, prayers and offerings made to blind crosses, whether rood-screens or deaf images of wood and stone, are closely akin to idolatry, and far from almsgiving. And although these things are forbidden, and are imaginary, a book of error for the lay people; yet the usual image of the Trinity is most abominable. God clearly shows this conclusion, commanding that alms be given to a needy man, because he himself is the image of God, in a greater likeness than wood or stone. For God did not say, let us make a piece of wood or stone in our image and likeness, but a man. Because the supreme honour which the clergy call latria pertains to the Godhead alone, and the lesser honour, which the clergy call dulia, pertains to man and angel, and to no other inferior creature. A corollary is that the service of the cross performed twice a year in our church is full of idolatry; for if the nails and the spear must be so highly honoured, then they would be the lips of Judah, if anyone could have them, very much...

units.la: Septima. Quod spirituales orationes tiones pro animabus mortuorum factæ in ecclesia nostra præferentes unum per nomen, est falsum fundamentum eleemosynæ, super quod omnes domus eleemosynarum Anglię nequiter sunt fundatæ, ista conclusio probatur, per duas rationes. Una est, quod oratio meritoria, & alicuius valoris, deberet esse opus procedens ab alta charitate: & perfecta charitas accipit nullam personam, quia diliges proximum tuum sicut teipsum. Quapropter apparet quod bonum doni temporalis collatum sacerdotibus, & eleemosynarum domibus, est principalis causa specialis orationis, quæ non longe abest à symonia. Alia ratio est, quia speciali oratio facta pro hominibus damnatis ad sempiternam poenam, est Deo multum displicens, & quamvis sit dubium, verisimile est fideli populo Christiano, quod fundatores eleemosynarum domus, propter suam uenenofam dotationem sunt pro maiori parte pertransiti latam uiam. Corrollarium est, oratio ualoris, procedens ex charitate perfecta, complecteretur in generali, omnes quos Deus uellet habere saluatos, & dimitteret uiam usitatam nundinariam pro specialibus orationibus factam mendicantibus, poffeffionatis, & alijs sacerdotibus conductitijs, qui sunt populus strenuus ad operandum & inseruiendum toti regno, iam retentus in oo cio, quia fuit probatum in uno libro quem Rex habuit, quod centum domus eleemosynarum, sufficiunt toti regno : & ex hoc proueniret magis incrementum possibile tempórali parti.
units.tr: Seventh. That spiritual prayers made for the souls of the dead in our church, appointing each by name, are a false foundation of almsgiving, upon which all the almshouses of England have been wickedly founded. This conclusion is proved by two reasons. One is that meritorious prayer of any worth ought to be a work proceeding from high charity, and perfect charity accepts no person, since "you shall love your neighbour as yourself." Wherefore it appears that the benefit of temporal gifts conferred on priests and almshouses is the principal special cause of such prayer, which is not far from simony. The other reason is that special prayer made for men condemned to everlasting punishment is very displeasing to God; and although this is doubtful, it is probable to the faithful Christian people that the founders of almshouses, because of their poisonous endowment, have for the most part passed by the broad way. A corollary: prayer of worth, proceeding from perfect charity, would embrace in general all whom God wished to save, and would abandon the usual market-like custom of special prayers made for beggars, possessioners and other hired priests, who are a vigorous people for working and serving the whole kingdom, but now are held in idleness. For it was proved in one book which the King had that a hundred almshouses suffice for the whole kingdom, and from this there would come a greater possible increase to the temporal part.

units.la: Octaua. Quod peregrinationes, orationes, & oblationes facte caecis crucibus, siue rodis, siue surdis imaginibus de ligno et lapide, sunt pe consanguineae ad idololatriam, & lon-
units.tr: Eighth. That pilgrimages, prayers and offerings made to blind crosses, whether to rods, or to deaf images of wood and stone, are closely akin to idolatry, and far

units.la: 8 Peregrinationes et oblationes. & longe ab eleemosyna: Et quam- uis ista inhibita, & imaginaria sint, liber erroris populo laicali, attamen imago usualis de trinitate, est maxi- me abominabilis, istam conclu- sionem Deus aperte ostendit, prae- cipiens eleemosynam fieri homini indigenti, quia ipse est imago Dei, in maiore similitudine quam lignū uel lapis. Quia Deus non dixit fa- ciamus lignum uel lapidem ad ima- ginem, & similitudinem nostram, sed homine, quia supremus honor quem clerici uocant latriam, perti- net ad diuinitatem solum, & infe- rior honor, quem clerici uocant du- liam, pertinet ad hominem & ange- lum, et ad nullam aliam inferiorem creaturam. Corrollarium est, quod seruicium de cruce factum bis quo- libet anno in nostra ecclesia est ple- nū idololatria, quia si clauī, et lancea debent ita alte honorari, tunc essent labia Iudae, si quis posset habere, ualde
units.tr: 8 Pilgrimages and offerings. from almsgiving: And although these are forbidden and imaginary, a book of error for the lay people, yet the common image of the Trinity is most abominable. God openly shows this conclusion, commanding alms to be given to a needy man, because he is the image of God, in greater likeness than wood or stone. For God did not say, "Let us make a piece of wood or stone in our image and likeness," but "a man." The supreme honour which clerics call latria pertains to deity alone, and the lesser honour, which clerics call dulia, pertains to man and angel and to no other inferior creature. A corollary is that the service of the cross performed twice every year in our church is full of idolatry; for if the nails and the spear ought to be so highly honoured, then the lips of Judas, if anyone could have them, would be very

units.la: Imago trinitatis res absurdissima. ualde reliquiæ. Sed rogamus te peregrine ad narrandum nobis quando tu offers ossibus sanctorum positis in aliquo loco, utrū tu releuas sanctum, qui est in gaudio, uel illam pauperem eleemosynæ domū, ubi homines sunt canonizati, dominus scit quomodo, & ad loquendum magis plane, fidelis Christianus supponit, quod puncta illius nobilis hominis, quem homines uocant sanctum Thomam non fuerunt causa martyrij.
units.tr: The image of the Trinity is a most absurd thing; relics are absurd too. But we ask you, pilgrim, to tell us when you make offerings to the bones of saints placed in some spot, whether you are raising up the saint who is in joy, or that poor almshouse where men have been canonized. The Lord knows how. To speak more plainly, the faithful Christian supposes that the wounds of that noble man whom men call Saint Thomas were not the cause of his martyrdom.

units.la: Nona. Quod Auricularis confessio, quæ dicitur tam necessaria ad salvationem hominis, cum ficta potestate absolutionis, exaltat superbiam sacerdotum, & dat illis opportunitatem secretarum uocationum aliarum, quam nos nolumus dicere, quia domini & dominæ attestantur quod præ timore confesorum suorum non audent dicere ueritatem, & in tempore confessionis est opportuportunum tempus ad procandi & aliarum secretarum conuentionum ad mortalia peccata. Ipsi dicunt, quòd sunt commissarij Dei, ad iudicandum de omni peccato ad perdonandum, & mundandum quæcunque eis placuerint. Dicūt quòd habent claues cœli & inferni, & possunt excommunicare, & benedicere, ligare, & soluere ad voluntatem eorum, in tantum quòd pro buccelo, uel 12 denarijs uolunt uendere benedictionem cœli, per chartam, et clausulam uuarrantia sigillatam sigillo communi. Ista conclusio sic est in usu, quòd non indiget probatione aliqua. Corrollarium est, quòd Papa Ro. qui finxit se altum thesaurarium totius ecclesiæ habens illud dignum iocale, i. ἐπιμάλιον passionis Christi in custodia cum meritis omnium sanctorum, in coelo, per quod dat ficta indulgetiam, a poena, & a culpa. Est Corrollarius scriptus maximè extra cha-
units.tr: Ninth. Auricular confession, which is said to be so necessary for man's salvation, together with the feigned power of absolution, exalts the pride of priests and gives them the opportunity for secret summonses of other kinds, which we are unwilling to name, because lords and ladies testify that for fear of their confessors they do not dare to tell the truth. And at the time of confession there is an opportune moment for solicitation and other secret agreements to mortal sins. The priests say that they are God's commissaries, to judge every sin, and to forgive and cleanse whatever they please. They say that they hold the keys of heaven and hell, and that they can excommunicate, bless, bind and loose at their will, to such an extent that for a buckle or twelve pence they are willing to sell the blessing of heaven, by a charter and a clause sealed with the common seal. This conclusion is so commonly practised that it needs no proof. A corollary: the Pope of Rome, who pretends to be the high treasurer of the whole Church, holding in custody that worthy jewel, the epimalion [ἐπιμάλιον] of Christ's passion, together with the merits of all the saints, in heaven, by which he grants feigned indulgence from penalty and from guilt. This corollary is written mostly outside charity

units.la: Papa Th(e)saurarius ecclesiæ, pro thesauro carbones. tra charitatem, ex quo potest liberare omnes captiuos existentes in purgatorio, ad uoluntatem suam, & ipsos facere, nunquam uenire ibidem, sed hic quilibet fidelis Christianus potest bene uidere quod multa secreta falsitas abscondita est, in ecclesia nostra.
units.tr: The Pope, treasurer of the Church: for treasure, coals. Outside charity, by which he can free all captives who are in purgatory at his will, and make them never come there at all. But any faithful Christian can clearly see that a great deal of secret falsehood is hidden in our church.

units.la: Decima. Quod homicidium per bellum, uel praetensam legem iustitiae, pro temporali causa siue spirituali reuelatione, est expresse contra ria nouo Testamento, quod quidem est lex gratiae, & plena misericordiarum. Ista conclusio est aperte proba-
units.tr: Tenth. That homicide through war, or under the pretended law of justice, whether for a temporal cause or a spiritual revelation, is expressly contrary to the New Testament, which is indeed the law of grace and full of mercies. This conclusion is plainly proved

units.la: ta, per exempla punitionis Christi hic in terra, qui maxime docuit hominem ad diligendum inimicos, & ad miserandum eis, & non ad occidendum eos. Ratio est haec, quod pro maiore parte, ubi homines pugnant, post primum ictum, charitas rumpitur, & quisquis moritur extra charitatem, uadit recta uia ad infernum, & ultra hoc nos bene cognoscimus, quod nullus clericus scit liberare per scripturam, uel per rationem legitimam, punitionem mortis pro uno peccato mortali, & non pro alio, sed lex misericordiæ, quæ est nouum Testamentum, inhibet omnimodum homicidium, in Euägelio dictum est antiquis, Non occides. Corrollarium est facta expoliatio pauperis populi, quando demum acquirunt indulgentias à pœna & culpa, illis, qui iuuant exercitum illorum ad interficiendum populum Christianum, in longinquis terris, pro temporali lucro. Sicut nos uidimus & milites, qui currunt ad Ethnicos ad quærendum eis nomen in occasione hominum, multo magis malas grates de rege pacis, quia per humilitatem et patientiam, nostra fides fuit multiplicata, & pugnatores, ac interfectores Christus Iesus odit. Qui gladio percutit gladio peribit.
units.tr: by the examples of Christ's own punishment here on earth, who above all taught man to love his enemies, to show mercy to them, and not to kill them. The reason is this: for the most part, where men fight, after the first blow charity is broken, and whoever dies outside charity goes straight the way to hell. Beyond this we well know that no cleric knows how to free from the punishment of death by Scripture or by sound reason for one mortal sin and not for another. But the law of mercy, which is the New Testament, forbids every kind of homicide; it was said in the Gospel to the ancients, Thou shalt not kill. A corollary: the poor people are despoiled, when at last they obtain indulgences from penalty and guilt for those who help the army to kill the Christian people in distant lands, for temporal gain. As we see, and soldiers who run to the heathen to win themselves a name on the occasion of men, much more ill thanks to the King of peace; for through humility and patience our faith was multiplied, while Christ Jesus hates fighters and killers. He who strikes with the sword will perish by the sword.

units.la: Q
units.tr: Q

units.la: Vndecima. Quod uotum continentiae, factum in nostra ecclesia per mulieres, quae sunt fragiles, & imperfectae in natura, est causa indu†ctionis maximorum horribilium peccatorum possibilium humanae naturae, quia licet interfectio puerorum antequam baptizentur abortiuorum, & destructio naturae per medicinam sint turpia peccata, adhuc communicatio cum seipsis, uel irrationabilibus bestijs, uel creatura non habete uitam, transeunt in indignitate ut puniantur poenis inferni. Corrollarium est, quod uiduę & tales quae accipiunt metallum & annulum delicitate pastae, uellemus quod effent desponsatae, quia nescimus excusare eas a priuatis peccatis.
units.tr: Eleventh. That the vow of continence, made in our church by women, who are frail and imperfect in nature, is the cause of inducing the greatest and most horrible sins possible to human nature. For although the killing of infants before they are baptized, of aborted ones, and the destruction of nature by medicine are foul sins, yet communication with themselves, or with irrational beasts, or with a creature lacking life, passes into unworthiness to be punished with the pains of hell. A corollary: that widows and such women as receive metal and ring by delicate pact, we would wish that they were married, because we cannot excuse them from private sins. ## Twelfth.

units.la: Duodecima.

Quod multitudo artium non necessariarum, usitatarum in nostro regno, nutrit multum peccatum in superflua curiositate. Istud ostendit ex parte experientia & ratio tio quia natura cum paucis artibus sufficit ad necessitatem hominis &c.
units.tr: That the multitude of unnecessary arts, customary in our realm, nourishes much sin through superfluous curiosity. This is shown in part by experience and in part by reason, because nature with few arts suffices for the necessity of man, etc.

units.la: Haec est nostra legatio quā Christus praecepit nobis, prosequi isto tempore, maxime acceptabili, pro multis causis, & quamuis istae materiae sint hic breuiter notatae, sunt tamen largiter declaratae in alio libro, & multae aliae plures totaliter in nostra propria lingua, quas uellemus ut essent communes toti populo Christiano. Rogamus igitur Deum de maxima sua bonitate, ut reformet totaliter ecclesiam nostram, totaliter extra iuncturam, ad perfectionem sui primi initij.
units.tr: This is our embassy, which Christ commanded us to pursue at this most acceptable time, for many reasons. Although these matters are here briefly noted, they are nevertheless fully declared in another book, and many others at greater length in our own language, which we would wish to be common to the whole Christian people. We therefore beseech God in his great goodness to reform our church entirely, so that it is brought back from being totally out of joint to the perfection of its first beginning.

units.la: VERSVS SEQVENTES CONCLUSIONES.
units.tr: The Following Verses on the Conclusions.

units.la: Plangunt Anglorum gentes crimen Sodomorum.
units.tr: The nations of England lament the crime of Sodom.

units.la: Paulus fert, horum, sunt idola, causa malorum.
units.tr: Paul testifies that idols are the cause of these evils.

units.la: Surgunt ingrati Gyerzytae Simone nati,
units.tr: There rise up the ungrateful Gyerzytes, sons of Simon,

units.la: Nomine Prælati, hoc defensare parati
units.tr: Prelates by name, ready to defend this.

units.la: Qui Reges estis, populis quicunque praeestis
units.tr: You who are kings, and you who rule over whatever peoples,

units.la: Qualiter his gestis gladios prohibere potestis?
units.tr: By what means can you forbid these deeds with swords?

units.la: Gulielmus Sauutreus.
units.tr: William Sawtrey.

units.la: Sub idem tempus aut non multo prius, ab autore Fabiano accepimus, in persecutione Vuicleuiana pariter occubuisse Gulielmu quendam Sauutreum, de cuius innocentia, aliisque dotibus, non est quod multa predicem, quum res ipsa palam loquitur, qualis fuerit. Hic quum esset sacrificus, totusque, ut ui detur, flagrans religionis zelo, petijt se in Parlamento regio, pro totius regni audiri commodo. Honesta sane petitio, nec minus fortasse utilis futura, si audiri posset. Sed reab episcopis subodorata, ab ipsis impetratum est, ut eorum iudicio res permitteretur, a quibus demum hae refeos taxatus, pro septem articulis condemnatur, degradatusque exuritur. Anno 1400.
units.tr: At about the same time, or not long before, we have learned from the author Fabian that a certain William Sawtrey also perished in the Wycliffite persecution. There is no need for me to say much of his innocence and his other gifts, since the matter itself makes plain what sort of man he was. Being a priest, and, as it seems, wholly on fire with zeal for religion, he petitioned Parliament, asking to be heard for the good of the whole kingdom. It was an honest petition, and perhaps no less useful if it could have been granted. But the bishops, getting wind of it, obtained from Parliament that the matter be left to their judgment. By them he was at last convicted of heresy on seven articles, condemned, degraded, and burned. In 1400.

units.la: HISTORICAE LIB. I.
units.tr: BOOK I OF THE HISTORY.

units.la: NEc minus in Guliel. Thorpo sacrifico, eminuit singularis Dei virtus. Declarant id multa maximaque huius viri depugnata in ecclesia Dei stratagemata, quem nulla humana vis de fidei constantia dejicere potuit. Quoties ille ad conflictus quam acerrimos ab episcopis vocatus? Quot arietes, quot impetus sustinuit? Quot hostes unus ille perpessus est, nunc minis, & terroribus impetitus, nunc promissis iterum, blanditiisque delinitus, nunc fraude proditoria circumuentus, interdum & conviciis laedorumque plusquam scurrilibus laceratus. Quam non illi machinam adhibuerunt, ad expugnandam huius sanctissimi pectoris firmitatem: si non valuisset in illo praesentissimum Christi robur, omnibus humanis machinamentis invictum. Quorsimul doctori bus, clericis, ac legistis unus hic respondere coactus sit, sicque respondere dicitur, ut tot etiamnum antagonistas sibi uni impares esse facile declararet. Non hercules, ait proverbium, contra duos, at hic ita unus tot potuit congredientibus sufficere, ut illis potius quod objicerent, quam huic quod responderet, deesse videretur. Nonnunquam ita argumentis deiectos, ad eas usque angustias egit, ut vix saepe aliud suffugium illis, praeterquam in convitiis solum accontumeliis, suppeteret. Quod non recuso falsum videri, ni ex illius responsis, totaque causae tractatione idem facile deprehendat, quisquis modestissimam ipsius patientiam, fortissimasque rationes, cum Archiepiscopi magnificis τὰς κακολογίας, ac frigidissimis cavillis contulerit. Nec mirum, cum Christus eam pollicetur suis, spiritus energiam, cui non queat ab adversariis resisti.
units.tr: Nor was the singular power of God less evident in William Thorpe, the priest. The many great stratagems of this man, fought out in the Church of God, bear witness to it. No human force could shake him from the constancy of his faith. How often was he summoned by the bishops to the fiercest contests? How many battering rams and assaults did he withstand? That one man endured so many enemies: sometimes assailed with threats and terrors, sometimes soothed again with promises and flatteries, sometimes trapped by treacherous deceit, and at other times torn by insults and abuse more than buffoonish. What machinery did they not bring up to storm the firmness of this most holy breast? But the most present strength of Christ was in him, and it was proof against every human device. Although he alone was forced to answer doctors, clergy and lawyers together, and he answered in such a way that all those opponents, however many, were plainly no match for him alone. "Not so, by Hercules," says the proverb, "against two." Yet this one man was enough for so many who came against him, so that it seemed they lacked not so much an answer to give him as objections to bring. Sometimes he drove them, overthrown by argument, into such narrow straits that they scarcely had any refuge left except insults and abuse. I do not refuse to seem to say what is untrue if anyone, from his answers and the whole course of the case, cannot easily see the same, provided he compares his most modest patience and his most powerful reasoning with the archbishop's grand abuse [τὰς κακολογίας] and his most frigid quibbles. Nor is it any wonder, since Christ promises his people that energy of the Spirit against which the adversaries cannot resist.

units.la: Huius promissionis fidē, haud scio, an in multis, certius locupletiusque præstitit Christus, quā in hoc, quanquam non dubium, quin idem præstat in omnibus. Quoties Archiepiscopus scripturis, ut videtur, destitutus ad euanidas constitutiones, ad decretorum glossemata cōfugit? Interdum cum & hæc relinquunt, cogitur cum suis noua tentare consilia, nec raro accidit eos sic undique teneri, ut nihil sit relictum, nisi ut, ne causa deteriores uiderentur, quam ratione non possent, cum ui ac potentia opprimerent. At quæ nam hæc ratio, ut quem scripturæ absolueerent, cum humanæ traditiones hæreticum condemnarent. Atque hæc grauissima quidem est apud hos opprimendi ratio, non quia Christus id, non quia Apostoli dictant, sed quia Romana ecclesia id uult, quia sic in placitis Papalibus continetur. At quid hoc aliud est, quàm
units.tr: I do not know whether, in many cases, Christ has more surely and more abundantly kept this promise than in this one, although there is no doubt that he keeps it in all. How often has the archbishop, seemingly without Scripture, fled to vanished constitutions and to the glosses of the decrees? Sometimes, when they abandon even these, he is forced to try new plans with his men. It seldom happens that they are so hemmed in on every side that nothing is left but to oppress by force and power those whom they cannot overcome by reason, so that they may not seem worse than their cause. But what reason is this, that they should condemn as a heretic the man whom Scripture absolves, while human traditions condemn him? This is indeed the most weighty ground they have for oppressing people of this sort: not because Christ dictates it, not because the Apostles dictate it, but because the Roman Church wills it, because it is so contained in the Papal decrees. But what is this other than that the faith and rule of Christians are directed not by Christ and the Word of God, but by the Pope and his decrees?

units.la: fidem ac regulam Christianorum, non Christo, ac uerbo Dei, sed Papa eiusque decretis dirigi. Nec interim id quaeritur, an consonant illius συντάγματα omnia cum scripturae fontibus, aut secus. Verum nunquid à Papa constitutum sit, num in cano nicis decretalibus ita habeatur. Solum id ad conuincendos haereticos esse satis creditur, etiam cum nec mi ca producatur ex scripturis dei, quae legitime reuincat. Verum quum clarius haec exemplis, quàm uerbis constant, totam illius hanc congressiunculam cum Arundello archiepiscopo Cantuar. ex uerissima historicorum narratione, ut res gesta proponendam curauimus. Ex qua facile iudicium lectori fuerit, utrum uerum sit, quod apud Homerum est ἐπὶ τὰ κρείονα νικᾷ.
units.tr: Meanwhile it is not asked whether all those compositions [συντάγματα] of theirs agree with the sources of Scripture or not. Rather, the only question is whether it has been laid down by the Pope and is so found in the canon law and the decretals. That alone is thought sufficient to convict heretics, even when no proof is brought forward from the Scriptures of God that would legitimately refute them. But since these things are established more clearly by examples than by words, we have taken care to set out this whole little contest of his with Arundel, archbishop of Canterbury, as the event actually happened, from the most truthful narrative of the historians. From it the reader will easily judge whether what Homer says is true: he prevails for the better [ἐπὶ τὰ κρείονα νικᾷ].

units.la: Ex Ioan. Baleo et aliis.
units.tr: From John Bale and others.

units.la: CONFLICTATIO CONSTANTISSIMI IN CHRISTO MARTYRIS, GVILHELMI THORPI ANGLI CVM PROCERIBVS ECCLESIASTICIS, DE CAVSA RELIGIONIS EXAMINATI AC CONDEMNATI.
units.tr: THE CONFLICT OF THE MOST STEADFAST MARTYR OF CHRIST, WILLIAM THORPE, ENGLISHMAN, EXAMINED AND CONDEMNED ON THE CAUSE OF RELIGION BEFORE THE ECCLESIASTICAL NOBLES.

units.la: GVILIELMVS THORPVS, sacrificus, quo tempore sustinenda erat causae suae actio, prius ab iis, quos in Christo habebat familiares, obnixe astipulatus est, ut singula quae agerentur, diligenter annotata, literis consignarent, in communē caeterorum confirmationem. Eductus itaque e vinculis carcerariis (apud Saltuuodenses custoditus est) Anno 1407, dominica a vinculis Petri proxima, coram archiepiscopo Thoma Arundello sistitur, qui tum & Apostolicus legatus, & Regius Cancellarius summus quippe eius Insulae magistratus, erat. Hic semotis laicis, ac arbitris, solus cum Maluereno quodam Londini tum Lucem ac Parocho, aliisque duobus potificiij iuris fymmiftis in interius conclaue fe recipit: Sicque captiuum interro-gat. Guilhelme his uiginti & eo am pliusannis, peragrata Borea, uici-nisque regionibus, magnam huius regni parte pestifera doctrinae tuae aspergine uitiafti. attamen quoniam autore Paulo iubemur pacem habere in omnes, fi abdicatis errori-bus,supplex te ecclesiasticis fanxio-nibus submiseris, senties me propi-cium minimeque praedurum tibi do minum. Guilhelm. Quidnam hoc fit |modo: Archiepiscopus. Agefis demissus in genua, admotisque li-bello huic manibus, iureiurando te obstringes, dicto audientem fore mandatis & decretis nostris quae-cunque imperabimus. Guilhelmus. Domine quoniam in suspicionem me uocari uideo apud uos insimula tae haereseos,liceat quaeso fidei meae dogmata libere hic exponere. Archiepisc. Dicas liberè. Hic Guil helmus exorsus à symbolo Apostolico singula fidei Christianæ capita recesebat, adiuncta simul concinna paraphrasi, tandem quum ad articulum illum de ecclesia uentum est. Et illi, inquit, ecclesiæ membra, subiectio, quæ est in Christo Iesu tanquam os ex ossibus & caro ex carne: illis, inquam, omnibus, quos ex fidei fructibus percipio eius esse certissima membra. Huius sacrosanctæ ecclesiæ ante omnia, coram uobis quatuor, esse desiderio, quod utinam totus iam sciret mundus. Insuper utramque Dei legem ex trinitatis autoramento profectam credo ad humani generis salutem unice esse necessariam, huicque solam sufficere. In qua quicquid nobis à Deo præceptum aut promissum sit indubitata fide amplectendum censeo. Si quis huius diuinæ legis uel autoritate, uel apertis doctorum rationibus
units.tr: William Thorpe, a priest, before his case was to be heard, first earnestly asked those whom he counted as close friends in Christ to write down carefully everything that was said and done, and to record it in writing for the strengthening of others. Accordingly, he was brought out of his prison chains (he had been held at Saltwood) in the year 1407, on the Sunday next after the feast of St Peter's chains, and was presented before Archbishop Thomas Arundel, who was then both papal legate and the king's chancellor, the chief magistrate of this island. Here, with the laymen and onlookers sent away, the archbishop withdrew into an inner chamber with a certain Malverne of London, the parson of Lucy, and two other experts in papal law, and so questioned the captive: "William, for twenty years and more you have travelled through the North and the neighbouring regions and tainted a great part of this realm with the poisonous infection of your teaching. Yet since, on the authority of Paul, we are commanded to keep the peace with all men, if you renounce your errors and humbly submit yourself to the ecclesiastical sanctions, you will find me a gracious lord to you and by no means a harsh one." William: "What would that involve?" Archbishop: "You shall kneel down, and with your hands laid upon this book you shall bind yourself by oath to obey whatever our commands and decrees may enjoin." William: "Sir, since I see that I am suspected by you of heresy, may I, I beg you, be allowed to set out here freely the articles of my faith." Archbishop: "Say what you like freely." Thereupon William began with the Apostles' Creed and went through each head of the Christian faith, adding a neat paraphrase as he went, until at last he came to the article on the Church. "And as for the members of that Church," he said, "the fellowship which is in Christ Jesus, as bone of bone and flesh of flesh: all of them, I say, whom I recognise by the fruits of faith, I hold to be her most certain members. Of this most holy Church, I desire before you four, above all things, that the whole world might already know it. Moreover, I believe that both laws of God, proceeding from the authority of the Trinity, are uniquely necessary for the salvation of the human race, and that they alone are sufficient for it. In these I judge that whatever God has commanded or promised to us is to be embraced with unwavering faith.

units.la: Sola ad salutem αὐτάρκης scriptura. bus poterit mein aliquo fidei articulo coarguere, æquissimo animo cedam. Neque enim patrum aut doctorum quorumuis autoritates, temere reiecturus sum, modo quæ ab iis promuntur ad scripturæ gnomones excussa, dissentire non videantur. Sed unum hoc abs te domine Archipræsul scrire expeto. Cur manum libro apponerem? Archiepiscopus. Vt fidei iuramentum præstes. Guilhel. Reuerende, liber hic ex diuersis collatur creaturis, per quas (prohibente scriptura) nullo pacto deierare licitum est: nihilo secus, coram hisce clericis uestris attestatum uelim, si cubi, ex scripturæ autoritate, à uobis ostendi poterit, id mihi non fore illegitimum, pariterque articulos, conditiones, causasque postulati iuramenti, prius expositeris, equidem nihil detrectabo quicquid æquum fit me facere. Archipræsul, iurabis te non solum deserturum turum omnes opiniones lollardi-cas, sed & summa ui posthac relu-ctaturum sanctæ Ecclesiæ pertur-batoribus. Quisi præfractiores uidebuntur in susceptis opinioni-bus, autorum nomina pariter cum erroribus, dioecesanis, aut eorum ministris traduces. Postremo ab o-mni predicandi functione, interim temperabis, quoad nobis de resipi-scentia tua, ac correctis erroribus, certius pleniusque constet. Guil-helmus ad hæc obstupefactus, ac ueluti cum Susanna in lacrum et sa-xum redactus, silurit. Tum archiepi-scopus: Respondé, inquit, unum uel alterum. Guilhel. Domine, his si acquiescam, ac nomina uirorum ac mulierum coram episcopis, ac im-pissimis eorū ministris, tanta mali-tia publicem, merito totius Angliæ explorator, proditorque uideri pos-sem, quouis Iuda sceleratior. fieret enim, ut qui hodie in uia Dei salu-tifera tifera perstēt, metu supplicij, ac per- secutionis (sicut expertus noui) im pulsi, à ueritate semel suscepta resili rent. Neque uero in tota scriptura reperio, qua ratione officium huiuf- modi competat in Christianum. Ex quo & illis pernitiem et conscientiæ meæ onus non ferendum contrahe- rem; Dignusque essem qui non so- lum malam, in hac uita, fortunā, sed & æternam posthac damnationem feram, quod pīssimus auertat Do- minus. Archiepiscopus. Instar Pha- raonis induratum habes animum. Diabolus sic sensus tuos excæcauit & illusit, ut nec ueritatem scire, nec oblatam à nobis gratiam agnoscere poteris. Ex friuolis tuis responsio- nibus intelligo, quod pristinos ad- huc errores non excutis. Sed hoc tibi persuasissimum habeto (nequis sime hæretice) uel cito nostris de- cretis acordinationibus accedes, uel publicè degradatus, socium sequeris in foro ferrario exurendus. Ad hanc uocem steti cogitabundus aliquandiu Guilhelmus, nihil impotentius secum optans apud Deum, quàm tam sancto honorari martyrio. Vidensque archiepiscopum nihil ingemiscere, quòd Guilhelmum Sautreum innocentissimum uirum incenderit, Anno 1400, at magis adhuc magisque sanguinem innocuum sitire, minus coepit illius tyrannidem formidare, iamque pro confesso dei aduersario ducere. Sed hoc illi molestum erat, quod extra publicam frequentiam Christianorum fratrum, ac testium, res, priuata paucorum tractatione, ageretur. Interim precibus quàm obnixissimè egit apud dominum, ut spiritu potentiae suae, ipsum armaret aduersus horum conspirationem. Hæc, atque alia, tacita secum cogitatione uoluntanti, ex clericis mastiga quispiam obgannit. Quid tuτèiam tecum cogitas,
units.tr: Scripture alone, self-sufficient for salvation [αὐτάρκης]. If anyone can convict me of error in any article of faith, either by the authority of this divine law or by clear reasons drawn from the teachers, I will yield with the utmost equanimity. For I am not going to rashly reject the authorities of the Fathers or of any teachers, provided that what they put forward, when tested by the rules of Scripture, does not appear to disagree. But this one thing, my lord archbishop, I ask you to tell me: why should I lay my hand on the book?" Archbishop: "So that you may make the oath of fidelity." William: "Reverend sir, this book is made up of various creatures, and by Scripture's prohibition it is in no way lawful to swear by them. Nevertheless, I would be willing to have it attested here before these clerics of yours, if you can show from the authority of Scripture that it would not be unlawful for me, and if you will first set out the articles, the conditions and the grounds of the oath you demand; I for my part will refuse nothing that it is right for me to do." Archbishop: "You shall swear that you will not only abandon all Lollard opinions, but will also hereafter vigorously resist the disturbers of the holy Church. And if they seem more stubborn in the opinions they have adopted, you will report the names of their authors, along with their errors, to the diocesans or their ministers. Finally, you will refrain from all function of preaching in the meantime, until it is more certainly and fully established to us that you have repented and corrected your errors." William, astonished at this, and like Susanna's accusers turned to stone, fell silent. Then the archbishop said: "Answer, say one thing or another." William: "My lord, if I were to agree to these terms, and to betray the names of men and women before the bishops and their most impious ministers with such malice, I might rightly be seen as an informer and traitor to all England, more wicked than Judas. For it would come about that those who today remain in the saving way of God, driven by fear of punishment and persecution (as I know from experience), would fall back from the truth once they had embraced it. Nor indeed can I find anywhere in the whole of Scripture by what reasoning a duty of this kind belongs to a Christian. From this I would bring ruin upon them and a burden upon my own conscience, which must not be borne; and I would deserve to suffer not only a wretched fortune in this life but also eternal damnation hereafter, which may the most merciful Lord forbid." Archbishop: "You have a heart hardened like Pharaoh's. The devil has so blinded and deceived your senses that you can neither know the truth nor recognise the grace we offer. From your frivolous answers I understand that you have not yet shaken off your former errors. But be fully persuaded of this, you most wretched heretic: either you will soon accede to our decrees and ordinances, or you will be publicly degraded and, with your fellow, will be burned at the Smithfield."

units.la: Guilhelmus Sautreus gitas, facut dominus archiepiscopus hictibi demandarit. Adhuc meditabundus ille, nihil respondes, tacuit. Tunc archiepiscopus: Nondum satis apud te deliberatum est in animo, quid acturus sis. Guliel. Domine, cum olim parentum meorum (quorum misereatur dominus) impensis, perfuasionibus ac minis adductus sum, ut primum in presbiterij gradum initiarer, petij ab ipsis, ut edoceri liceret prius ab aliis, qui sanctiores, doctioresque uiderentur, quid ad tam sanctum officium spectaret. Quod illi nec inuite concesserunt, & pro conficiendo itinere uiatitum insuper addiderunt. Tum ego ad eos me contuli, quos sanctimoniae pariter ac doctrinae commendatione spectatissimos probatissimosque audirem. Cum ijs tam diu assueui, donec ex sanctissimis eorum exercitijs, ac morum integritate non nihil uiderer mihi profecisse. His Itaque doctrinę pietatis ac innocen- tię exemplis pertractus, sacrosanctæ scripturæ studio, animum adiunxi huc omnibus uotis modisque ad- nitens, ut uitam ad huius præscri- ptum quam maxime componerem. In hac tam diu me exercui, in hac me oblectaui. Nunc si persua- sionibus, ac minis uestris, à pristino uitæ ac studiorum instituto, auelli me patiar, quæ uiginti & amplius annis coluerim, merito is essem, qui reprehensioni omnibus, multis scan dalo uideri queam. Sicque non ædificator, sed destructor ecclesiæ, non fidus uerbi minister, sed inutile membrum, merito abscindendum appaream. Satis me exempla imbe- cillium quorundam docent, præci- pue N. Herfordi, I. Puruei. Tho. Britouelli, ac huius potissimum Re- pingtoni, quid mihi hic, multisque aliis, sit metuendum. Videmus enim quam periculose isti, tam turpi sua palinodia, in cruce Pauli, ecclesiam dei distrahant, ac miserè perturbent. Repingtonus uero non solum Christianam plebeculam pharisaicis technis, & palleatis fraudibus seducit, sed etiam pie credentes, ad mortem usque, persequitur. Hęc carnis prudentia, qua nunc huius mundi amatoribus blandiuntur, & adulantur in concionibus, non erit à Deo impunita. Veritatem olim edocebant isti, maximo ecclesiae bono, pro qua nunc uix unguium segmina exponerent. Archiepiscop. Illi quos hic commemoras, olim impru dentes erant, & haeretici, quos iam cōstat apprimè sapientes uiros esse, licet tibi similibusque haereticis secus uideantur. Nunquam equidem peritum quenquam uidi, uestra imposterice hac doctrina diu immoratum. Guliel. Mundo quidem sapientes hos esse, non nego. Verumtamen diuinae sapientiae arra bonem fursceperant, ad suam atque aliorum salutem si fide sic perstitissent, in spi-ritus paupertate, ac uitae Christianae simplicitate. Sed uae funestis consi-liis, saeuae tyrannidi, ac cupiditati terrenae, quę orbem fere uniuersum in omnium malorum colluuiem se-cum pertrahit. Archiepiscop. Ne-quissime haeretice, tu, atque tui simi-les, barbas ad intimam usque cutem raderetis pro consequendis eccle-siarum prouentibus. Per Iesum Christum non noui magis auaros nebulones, quam de uestra secta, Sacerdotium aliquando Ioan. Pur-ueo contuleram, uix mille passibus ab hoc castro dissitum, nec quisquam est in tota dioecesi eo ipso in cumu-landis oblationibus & decimis audi-dior. Guliel. Purueus neque adeo uobiscum iam sentit pro munera-rio hoc sacerdotio, neque fidem ser-uat doctrinae, quam antea scriptis uerbisque profitebatur. At quia se
units.tr: At these words William stood for some time in thought, wishing for nothing more powerful with God than to be honoured with so holy a martyrdom. And seeing that the archbishop showed no sorrow that he had burned William Sawtrey, a most innocent man, in the year 1400, but thirsted more and more for innocent blood, he began to fear his tyranny less and to regard him now as an open enemy of God. Yet what troubled him was that the matter was being handled in private, among a few, and not in the public assembly of Christian brethren and witnesses. Meanwhile, he prayed to the Lord as earnestly as he could that He would arm him with the Spirit of His power against this conspiracy. While he was turning these things over in silent thought, one of the clerics, a sly fellow, muttered to him: "What are you thinking about, what the lord archbishop has commanded you here?" Still pondering, he said nothing and kept silent. Then the archbishop said: "You have not yet sufficiently deliberated in your mind what you are going to do."
