William: "My lord, when I was once persuaded and pressed by my parents (may the Lord have mercy on them), with their expense, persuasions and threats, to be initiated into the first grade of the priesthood, I asked of them that I might be taught first by others who seemed holier and more learned, what such a holy office required. They granted this not unwillingly, and even added provision of travelling money for the journey. Then I went to those whom I could hear, men most conspicuous and most approved both for holiness and for teaching. I lived with them for so long that from their most holy exercises and integrity of life I seemed to myself to have made some progress. Drawn in by these examples of the teaching, piety and innocence, I applied myself to the study of holy Scripture, striving with every wish and effort to shape my life as far as possible to its precepts. In this I have exercised myself for so long, and in this I have taken my delight. Now, if I were to allow myself to be torn away by your persuasions and threats from the former course of life and study which I have cultivated for twenty years and more, I would rightly be one who could seem to all men a reproach and a scandal. And so I would appear to be not a builder but a destroyer of the Church, not a faithful minister of the Word but a useless member, rightly to be cut off. The examples of certain weaklings teach me enough what I have to fear here, and what many others have to fear: especially N. Herford, J. Purvey, Thomas Bredwell, and above all this Repton. For we see how dangerously these men, by their shameful recantation, tear apart and miserably disturb the Church of God, as on a cross of Paul. Repton not only leads the Christian common folk astray with Pharisaical tricks and cloaked deceits, but also persecutes to death the godly believers. This worldly prudence, with which he now flatters and fawns upon the lovers of this world in his sermons, will not go unpunished by God. These men once taught the truth, to the great good of the Church, for which they now would hardly risk the cutting of their fingernails." Archbishop: "Those whom you mention here were once imprudent and heretical; yet it is now plain that they are very wise men, however it may seem otherwise to you and to heretics like you. Indeed, I have never seen anyone skilled in your imposture linger long in this doctrine." William: "I do not deny that these men are wise in the eyes of the world. But they had received a foretaste of divine wisdom, for their own salvation and that of others, if they had persisted in faith in this way, in poverty of spirit and in the simplicity of Christian life. But woe to their deadly counsels, to savage tyranny and to earthly greed, which drags almost the whole world along with it into a deluge of all evils." Archbishop: "Most wicked heretic, you and those like you would shave your beards down to the very skin for the sake of gaining the revenues of the churches. By Jesus Christ, I have never known greedier scoundrels than your sect. Once I had appointed John Purvey to a priesthood, not a thousand paces from this castle, and there is no one in the whole diocese more eager than he for gathering offerings and tithes." William: "Purvey does not now think with you about this ministry of pay, nor does he keep the faith of the teaching which he professed before in his writings and words. But because he has shown himself neither hot nor cold..."

units.la: Nescit iu} rare simpli citas papi stica. ostendit modò neque calidum esse neque frigidum, timendum est illi suisque sodalibus, ne electorum excidant numero ni resipuerint. Archiepiscop. Si Purueus uersipellis, ac callidus fuerit, suo id damno fecerit. Si denuo tamen pro huiusmo di negocijs huc redierit, dilucide se nobis ante discessum aperiet, cuias sit. Age sed qui tandem illi sapien- tes sunt, a quibus institutionem tam sanctam te imbibisse prædicas? Gu- lielmus, Dom. Ioannes Vuicleuus à multis habebatur omnium, ætate sua, uiuentium laudatissimus: idem- que porro corpore macilentus, exte- nuatus, ac uiribus pene exhaustus fuit, conuersationeque innocentissi- mus, propterea complures huius re- gni proceres cum eo sæpius conse- rentes, homine summo studio com- plectebantur, colebant, dicta per- scribebant, uitæque exempla tan- quam pro regula assectabantur.
units.tr: The papistical simplicity does not know how to swear. He has just shown that he is neither hot nor cold, and he and his companions must fear that they will fall out of the number of the elect unless they repent. Archbishop: If Purvey is a slippery and crafty fellow, he has brought the loss on himself. If he returns here again on such business, he will make clear to us before he leaves whose side he is on. But come now, who are those wise men from whom you claim to have absorbed so holy a teaching? Thorpe: Master John Wycliffe was held by many, in his own time, to be the most praiseworthy of all the living. He was also thin of body, worn down, and nearly drained of strength, and he was most innocent in his conduct. For this reason many of the nobles of this realm often associated with him, embraced and cherished him with the greatest zeal, wrote down his sayings, and followed the examples of his life as if they were a rule.

units.la: Vuiclcui laus. huius Vuicleui doctrina talis etiam num à plerisque creditur, utpote quæ Apostolicæ primæque ecclesiæ puritatem quàm maximè redoleat ac referat. Eaque ratio est, quur hodie à tam multis tum uiris, tum fœminis tanto in precio, studioque habeatur. Deinde Magister Aistonus hanc ipsam doctrinam, ab eo susceptam, scriptis, uoceque, quanta uí poterat ac diligentia, disseminauit, uixitque secundum eandem inculpatissimè usq; ad exitus sui diè.
units.tr: Praise of Wycliffe. Even now his teaching is believed by many, since it is thought to breathe and reflect the purity of the apostolic and earliest Church most fully. This is why it is held in such high esteem and zeal today by so many men and women. Then Master Aston spread this same teaching, which he had received from him, by writing and by speech, with all the power and diligence he had, and he lived most blamelessly according to it until the day of his death.

units.la: Similiter Philippus Repingtonus, dum esset adhuc Canonicus Licestriæ. Nicolaus Herfordus, Dauid Gottreus, & Pakryngus, monachus Bylandensis, ac Theologiæ candi- datus, Item Ioannes Purueus, cum aliis quàm plurimis, habebantur id temporis conspicui nominis, & auctoritatis uiri, qui in eisdem studijs ac ueritatis professione, ingenti labore se exercuerunt, uitamque quàm san stissime instituerunt. His ego omni bus multum diuq; familiariter memet adiunxi, ac discipulum tradidi sanctissimis illorum institutis, ac præceptis excolendum, at nulli addi ctior quàm ipsi Ioanni Vuicleuo uiro tum omnium, quos mundus habebat, sanctissimo atque integerrimo. Ab his inquam uitæ & doctrinæ methodum hausi quam usque ad extremum uitæ exitum non sum deserturus. Et quamuis horum nonnulli, modò secum ipsi pugnantes uideantur, attamen doctrina, quam è cathedra non Moysi, sed Christi diuulgabant, uerissimæ est ubique certitudinis. Nam & hi ipsi etiam ob negatam dei uirtutem, iam nūc increpati, haud negant se tum errasse, sed quòd supplicijs perterriti sententiam dissimularint. Qui priùs ducebant, uidelicet sub uerbo rum fuco se occultare, quàm cum suo Christo persecutionis subire incommodo commoda. Archiep. Doctrina illa, quam veritatẽ uocas, ecclesiam Romanam scandalizat, id quod, ab eadem sacrosancta ecclesia, saepius est probatum. Et licet autor vester Vuicleuus multorum elogio eruditissimus ac perfectus habeatur, doctrina eius, per ecclesiam approbata non est, sed in multis sententiis, prout meruit, condemnatur. Philippo Repyngtono Licestriae olim canonico, & abbati, accessit dies ille festiuus, cuius tam diu ieiunauit uigiliam. Episcopus enim Lincolniensis effectus nec uobis, nec vestris deinceps fauet, adeo ut caeteris praelatis quibusque, multo sit in hac uia persequenda, ac punienda, uehementior. Guiliel. Quàm plurima mala de hoc uiro referuntur, habeturq; à multis pro maximo veritatis inimico. Archiep. Quare his nugis tam diu nos detines? Vin' tu nostris decretis nomen dare, an non? Guilhel.
units.tr: Likewise Philip Repton, while he was still a canon of Leicester; Nicholas Hereford, David Gotrey, and Pakryngus, a monk of Bylands and a candidate in theology; and also John Purvey, with very many others, were at that time men of distinguished name and authority. They devoted themselves with great labour to these studies and to the profession of the truth, and they ordered their lives most holily. I attached myself to all of these men, intimately and for a long time, and I gave myself as a pupil to be formed by their most holy institutions and precepts. But I was more devoted to none than to John Wycliffe himself, the most holy and upright man of all whom the world then had. From these men, I say, I drew the method of life and of teaching which I shall not abandon until the end of my life. And although some of them now seem to contradict themselves, the doctrine they proclaimed, not from the chair of Moses but of Christ, is everywhere most certainly true. For these same men, now rebuked for having denied God's power, do not deny that they erred at that time, but say that, terrified by punishments, they concealed their opinion. They preferred, that is, to hide under the disguise of words, rather than to suffer the inconvenience of persecution with their Christ. Archbishop: That teaching which you call the truth scandalizes the Roman Church, and this has been proved often by that same holy Church. And although your author Wycliffe is considered by many, in the judgement of many, the most learned and perfect man, his teaching has not been approved by the Church, but in many opinions it is condemned, as it deserves. For Philip Repington, once a canon of Leicester and also an abbot, that festive day has arrived for which he fasted so long in vigil. For having been made Bishop of Lincoln, he no longer favours you or your followers, so that he is more vehement than all the other prelates in pursuing and punishing this way. Thorpe: Very many evils are reported about this man, and he is held by many to be the greatest enemy of the truth. Archbishop: Why do you keep us so long with these trifles? Will you give your name to our decrees or not? Thorpe:

units.la: Quemadmodum supra responsum est, propter timorem Dei non audeo. Tunc commotior archiponti-sex, unicuique am exclericis illis martyromastigis subinnuens. Affer, inquit, syngraphā testimonialem, e Salopia nuper ad me adductam sub sigillo Balyui, aduersus haereses istic ab hoc lofello (ut ipsius utar E-pitheto) disseminatas. Quam ille mox allatam, in hanc fere sententiam legit.
units.tr: As has been answered above, I do not dare, for the fear of God. Then the archbishop, more agitated, nodding to each of those clerical scourgers of martyrs, said: Bring forward the testimonial document recently brought to me from Shrewsbury under the seal of the bailiffs, against the heresies spread there by this fellow (to use his own epithet). He at once read out the document, which was brought forward, to about this effect.

units.la: Tertia Dominica post festum paſchae An.1407. Guilhelmus Thorpus Salopiam accessit, qui concionandi nactus facultatem, in ecclesia Diui Ceddae publice edisserebat, quod in sacramento altaris, post consecrationem remanet materialis panis. Quod imagines non sunt adorandae. Quod homines no debeant peregrinari ad Diuos. Quod sacer-dotibus nullum ius sit uendicandi decimas. Quod licitum non sit iura re. Haec
units.tr: The third Sunday after Easter, in the year 1407. William Thorpe came to Shrewsbury, and having obtained the opportunity to preach, he publicly expounded in the church of St Chad that in the sacrament of the altar, after consecration, material bread remains; that images are not to be worshipped; that men ought not to make pilgrimages to the saints; that priests have no right to claim tithes; that it is not lawful to swear an oath.

units.la: Balyui as pud Anglos dicuntur, ediles curules, si inferiores magistratus, ad res populi curandas constituti.
units.tr: Among the English, bailiffs are called aediles, or, if they are lower magistrates, officials appointed to attend to the affairs of the people.

units.la: Literae Salopensium ad archiepiscopum. Missae contra Thorpum. re. Hæc ubi lecta sunt, conuoluta demum schedula, martyromastix episcopus, crispata fronte toruũ quiddam & uultuosum spectãs ὅτως ἐπιφωνεῖ. Quid inquiens, Instructione hæc populo salubris? Guliel. Malignantium hominum sunt hæ men dacissimæ calumniæ, quippe à me nec publicè, nec priuatim hæc ita dicta sunt. Archiep. Facilius credo hæc referentibus quàm tibi. Tu sceleste, usque adeo Salopensium permouisti rempublicam, ut scriptis ad me literis, qui iam archiepiscopus sum Cantuariæ, Angliæ primas, ac totius regni Cancellarius, id egerūt sedulò, ut te illuc, in aliorum terrorem, uel πρὸς τὸ παλινῳδῆσαι, uel ad supplicia sumenda remitterem. Demum pro Colophone addit, Enimuero, inquit, nec in obliuionem ueniet, quod tam honestè ac fideliter petitum est. Quanquam uerò parum hæc claudiana tonitrua Guilhelmum nostrum territabant. Sed quemadmodum palmae arboris mira acinuicta natura, nulla unquam quantalibet ponderis grauitate decutitur, sed presla ualentior insurgit, sefeqp contra onus erigit, obnixius. Sic huius diuina quadam magnitudine ac uti suffulta mens, haud quicquam his fracta tragicis furoribus, κχι ἀταξτηφοῖς ἐπῆτοσιν, minitantis archiepiscopi, sed multo animata magis, audacter liberaque uoce respondit. Equidem si uerum mihi fatendum sit. Qui Salopiae, aut alibi tantopere fidei Christianae nego cio officere existimatur, eos ego potissimum prodesse statuo. Contra qui fideles cefentur, uere sit ut nihil sint minus quam quod titulo praeferunt, quod facile eorum declarat supercilium intolerabile, liuor, cupiditas, libido, cum consimilibus carnis fructibus. Neque enim de Ecclesia Christi censendi sunt, qui uerba Dei ba Dei contemptui habent, quod maiori horum parti hodie usu uenire cernimus. Hiq; sunt, qui si quos uere Deũ timentes uideat, protinus pro hæreticis ducunt. Nec mirum si de me scelerato homuncione maligne sentiat Salopensis plebecula, ecclesiasticorum, sat scio, calumniis ac clamoribus instigata, quum eadem hæc Iesus Dei filius passus sit à Hierosolimitanis sapientibus. Sic & Synagogæ Nazarænæ primores Christum ob conciones ciuitate eiecerunt, præcipitium illi e montis supercilio molientes. Nec aliter per Moysen promisit Dominus, reliquturum se cultoribus suis gentem aduersariam, cuius quotidiana uexatione exerceantur. Quis tandem diuini uerbi legationem apud incredulos geret, ut non indidem certissimam sibi crucem accersat, iuxta Christi ac Prophetarum exempla & uaticinia. Archiep. Tunc ergo Christi
units.tr: Letters of the Shrewsbury men to the archbishop, sent against Thorpe, etc. When these were read, the archbishop, having finally rolled up the schedule, the scourger of martyrs, with a wrinkled brow, looked at me with a kind of grim and angry face and exclaimed thus he cries out [ὅτως ἐπιφωνεῖ]. What, he said, is this instruction wholesome for the people? Thorpe: These are most lying calumnies of malicious men, since these things were not said by me in public or in private. Archbishop: I more readily believe those who report these things than you. You wicked fellow, you have so stirred up the commonwealth of Shrewsbury that they have diligently written to me, who am now archbishop of Canterbury, primate of England, and chancellor of the whole realm, asking that I send you back there, to terrify others, either to recant [πρὸς τὸ παλινῳδῆσαι], or to undergo punishment. At last, as a conclusion, he added: Indeed, he said, what has been asked so honourably and faithfully will not come into oblivion. Yet these thunderings in the manner of Claudian did little to frighten our William. But as the palm tree has a wonderful and unconquered nature, and is never struck down by any weight, however heavy, but rises the stronger under the pressure and pushes back against the burden the more stubbornly, so his mind, sustained by a certain divine greatness, was not broken at all by these tragic rages not with abject threats [κχι ἀταξτηφοῖς ἐπῆτοσιν] of the threatening archbishop, but, animated all the more, answered boldly and with a free voice. Indeed, if I must confess the truth: those who are thought in Shrewsbury, or elsewhere, to be such great obstacles to the Christian faith, I judge to be especially useful. On the contrary, those who are counted faithful, truly they are nothing less than what their title suggests, as their intolerable arrogance, envy, lust, and sensuality, with similar fruits of the flesh, readily show. For those who hold the word of God in contempt are not to be counted in the Church of Christ, which we see happening to most of them today. These are the men who, if they see any who truly fear God, at once regard them as heretics. Nor is it surprising if the Shrewsbury rabble think badly of me, a wicked little man, being stirred up, I am well aware, by the slanders and clamours of churchmen, since Jesus, the Son of God, suffered these same things from the wise men of Jerusalem. So too the leaders of the synagogue of Nazareth cast Christ out of the city because of his sermons, plotting to throw him down from the brow of the mountain. Nor did the Lord promise otherwise through Moses, that he would leave to his worshippers an adversary people, by whose daily vexation they would be exercised. Who, finally, would carry out the embassy of the divine word among unbelievers without thereby procuring for himself the surest cross, according to the examples and prophecies of Christ and the prophets. Archbishop: Then do you believe you are a follower of Christ, and so you can preach without the authority of any prelate?

units.la: Crux sem- per uerita- tis comer.
units.tr: The cross always accompanies the truth.

units.la: Christi te sequacem credis, sicque sine cuiusque praelai autoritate pof se concionari? Guihel. Certe hunc in modo à Christo institutum est, praecipuum esse illud Christiani sacerdotis officium, Euangelicam praedicationem liberè ac ubilibet circumferre. Nec alios ad hanc functionem admisit summus ille pastorum princeps, quàm qui populo Domino operam darent instituendo. Nos nulla iactatione huiusmodi esse ostentamus, caeterum ut uerè simus, à Domino efflagitamus. Archiep. Malefurcifer, quorsum haec nobis producis phantasmata? Nonne Paulus hoc quaerit? Quomodo praedicabunt nisi mittantur. Nunquam ego te misi ad praedicandum. Adeo enim per Angliam innotuit pestifera doctrina tua, ut haud quisquam episcoporum licentiarias tibi literas communicet. Cur igitur, pestime idiota, haec facere praesumis, quum fis à nullo prælato huc admissus. Nunquid & idem Paulus admonet, præpositis parendum esse, non modestis modo, sed et uitiosis tyrannis? Guilhel. Literas uestras nec moramur, nec recipimus, Continet enim præceptiunculas prorsus cum Euangelij puritate ac spiritu Christi pugnantes. Has sibi τωλοκοπλάστοι illi fraterculi comparent, qui mendacijs acimposturis uicitant. Literæ nostræ hi sunt, quos instituimus & firmum testimonium, æterna Dei ueritas. Neque enim atramentaria scripta, nec humanum testimonium quærimus, qui diuinos sermones simpliciter gratisq; mortalibus annunciamus, qua in re astipulatorem habemus Paulum. Non egemus, inquit, literis commendaticijs. Epistola nostra, Vos estis in Domino, non atramento inscripta, sed spiritu Dei uiui. Pono quod ad præpositorum obedientiam attinet. Eam minime negamus, saltem iis, qui praesunt uerbo & exemplo. Contra in his, quae a tyrannis aduersus Euangelij uerbum, praecipiuntur, moriendu magis, quam obediendum ceseo. Archiepiscop. Si quid perpetram praecipiant hi, qui praefecturam gerunt, sibi id in damnu cedet: Caeterum obedienti, idipsum tamen erit meritorium, quum sit omnibus uictimis obedientia melior. Guilh. Obedientia quam a Saule in hoc loco exigebat Samuel, Dei erat praecipientis, non hominis. Dicunt Paulus & Dauid, quibus insuper suffragatur Gregorius, hos damnatione dignos esse, non solum qui iniqua perpatrant, sed & qui patrantibus consenserint. Praeterea huc consonant ecclesiae Decreta, quibus affirmatur, quod nec seruus Domino, nec filius patri, necmulier marito, nec monachus praesidenti, obedien diiure astringatur, praeterquam in honeste. honestis & licitis. Archiep. Satis tu quidem arroganter hæc, ratus te ac tui similes solos esse iustos, itaque Pauli doctrinam respuentes, putatis licere quod libet. Guilhel. Obsecro quos tu potissimum Apostolorum munus nobis in ecclesia referre iudicas, an non sacerdotes? Archie. Maxime quidē. Guilhel. Primum ergo de Apostolorum officio, abun deliquet, Matthei 10. & Marci ultimo: Christus misit prædicare Apostolos. Præterea Lucæ 10. ubi legimus à Christo 72 discipulos, ad confirmandum ablegatos in omnem ciuitatem, & locum quo fuerat ipse uenturus. Quemadmodum nec Gregorius dissimulat, in decretis scribes, prædicationis officium cum sacerdotio esse commune. Presbiter, inquit ille, ad iracundiam dominum prouocat, cuius in Euangelij prædicatione, uocem populus non audit. Et Glossa in Ezechielem. Sacerdos cerdos qui non prædicat, sit damnationis eorum omnium particeps, qui ex hoc pereunt. Qui populo præsunt, & Euangelium non docent, sunt homicidæ coram Deo, uitæ uiaticum subtrahentes. Isidorus quoque. Sacerdotes, inquit, ex plebis iniquitate damnabūtur, si ignorantes nō doceant, & delinquentes non arguant. Ad hoc sum natus, inquit Christus, ut ueritati testimoniū perhibeam. Et qui ex ueritate est, audit uocem meam. Itaque Christi præcepto, & exemplo, sacerdotū est posthabitis rebus omnibus, uacare propagando Euangelio Dei. Quia teste Gregorio, quicquid facit homo, ingratum est spiritui sancto, si quod ex debito fit, id negligens præterit. Quin & huic concinit perpulchre Lincolniensis. Sacerdos, inquit, qui uerbum Dei nō prædicat, quamuis alium non habuerit defectum, Antichristus est, Satanas est, fur nocturnus la-
units.tr: Do you believe you are a follower of Christ, and so you preach without the authority of any prelate? William: Certainly it has been instituted by Christ that the chief duty of a Christian priest is to spread the Gospel preaching freely and wherever he may be. That supreme prince of pastors admitted to this office none but those who would labour to instruct the people of the Lord. We do not display any such boasting; but we ask the Lord that we may truly be such. Archbishop: Malefurcifer, why do you bring these fancies before us? Does not Paul ask, "How shall they preach unless they are sent?" I never sent you to preach. Your pernicious doctrine has become so well known throughout England that not one of the bishops will grant you a licence. Why then, you pestilent idiot, do you presume to do these things, when no prelate has admitted you here? Does not the same Paul also teach that we must obey those who are set over us, not only the gentle ones but also the wicked tyrants? William: We neither delay over your letters nor accept them, for they contain little precepts utterly at odds with the purity of the Gospel and the spirit of Christ. Such letters are fashioned by those word-mongers [λογοπλάστοι], those little brothers who thrive on lies and deceits. Our letters are those whom we have instituted, and the eternal truth of God is our firm witness. For we seek neither written documents made with ink nor human testimony, since we announce the divine words simply and freely to mortals; and in this we have Paul as our fellow-supporter. "We have no need," he says, "of letters of commendation. You are our letter, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God." As for obedience to those set over us, we by no means deny it, at least to those who rule by word and example. But against those things that tyrants command against the word of the Gospel, I judge that one ought rather to die than obey. Archbishop: If those who hold office command anything wrong, the harm will fall on them. Yet to the one who obeys, the obedience will still be meritorious, since obedience is better than all sacrifices. William: The obedience which Samuel in that passage demanded of Saul was the obedience owed to God commanding, not to man. Paul and David say, and Gregory agrees, that those are worthy of condemnation who not only commit wicked deeds but also consent to those who commit them. Moreover, the decrees of the Church agree, which affirm that neither a servant to his lord, nor a son to his father, nor a wife to her husband, nor a monk to his superior, is bound to obey except in honest and lawful things. Archbishop: You speak quite arrogantly, supposing that you and those like you alone are just, and so, rejecting Paul's teaching, you think it lawful to do whatever you like. William: I beg you, whom do you judge should principally bear the office of the apostles in the Church? Are they not priests? Archbishop: Certainly, most of all. William: Then first, concerning the office of the apostles, which is abundantly clear from Matthew 10 and the last chapter of Mark: Christ sent the apostles to preach. Also Luke 10, where we read that Christ sent seventy-two disciples to confirm the people, into every city and place to which he himself was about to come. Nor does Gregory conceal, as he writes in the Decretals, that the office of preaching is common to the priesthood. "A priest," he says, "provokes the Lord to anger when the people do not hear his voice in the preaching of the Gospel." And the Gloss on Ezekiel: "A priest who does not preach shares the damnation of all those who perish through this." Those who preside over the people and do not teach the Gospel are murderers before God, withdrawing the viaticum of life. Isidore also: "Priests," he says, "will be condemned for the wickedness of the people if, being ignorant, they do not teach, and, when they fail, do not rebuke." "For this I was born," says Christ, "that I should bear witness to the truth; and whoever is of the truth hears my voice." Therefore, by the precept and example of Christ, it is the duty of priests, setting aside all other concerns, to devote themselves to spreading the Gospel of God. For, as Gregory witnesses, whatever a man does is unpleasing to the Holy Spirit if he neglects what he owes and passes it by. Indeed the Lincolnshire writer agrees most beautifully with this: "A priest who does not preach the word of God, although he may have no other defect, is Antichrist, is Satan, is a thief by night, a la-

units.la: Quid hic respondeat muti cācelarij et epi scopi no⁠ stri. nus, latro diurnus, animarum carni sex, & angelus lucis, in tenebras uer sus. Ex his autoritatibus perspicu-um fit, illos esse maledictos sacerdo-tes, qui populo Euangelium synce-re non enunciant. Tunc archiepi-scopus, ad tres clericos conuersus, subinquit. Perpetuum est his hæreti-cis, si qua grauiora sint, scripturæ, aut sanctorum dicta, quæ in os im-pingant, in nos, & ecclesiæ ordi-nationes distorquere, quorum ob-tentu, se sectamque tueantur, eoque pessimeolosellè (his enim rosis abun-dabat hic Satrapas) Psalterium il-lud, quo te priuaram aliquado Can-tuariæ, recuperare cupis, unde sem-per excerpas aliquid, quod in nos obgannias. Sed mihi crede, Psalteri-um illud, haud unquam extorseris, nec ullum scripturæ librum, quoad te perfensero, & corde & ore, ma-gis ecclesiæ conciliatum. Gulielmi Spero me de sacrosancta ecclesia,
units.tr: What would our dumb chancellor and bishop answer here? "nus, a robber by day, a butcher of souls, and an angel of light turned into darkness." From these authorities it is made clear that those are cursed priests who do not sincerely set forth the Gospel to the people. Then the archbishop, turning to three clerks, said in an undertone: "It is always the way with these heretics, if there are any weightier texts of Scripture or sayings of the saints that strike them in the face, that they twist them against us and against the ordinances of the Church, under the cover of which they defend themselves and their sect. And so most wickedly, for this Satrap abounds in such roses, you wish to recover that Psalter by which you were once deprived at Canterbury, from which you always pick out something to bark against us. But believe me, you will never wrest that Psalter, nor any book of Scripture, from me, as long as I live, which is more reconciled to the Church both in heart and mouth." William: I hope I am judging the holy Church no differently than becomes a servant of Christ.

units.la: haud aliter sentire, quàm decet Christi seruulum. Interrogantique Archiepiscopo, quid esset ecclesia, respondit ille: Ecclesiam hanc, quam sacrosanctam appello, credo esse Christum & sanctos. Archiep. Fateor uidelicet in coelo. Sed in terris ecclesia quid est? Gulielm. Ea bifariam distributa est. Cuius altera, ac potior pars hostibus deuictis cum Christo laeta triumphat. Altera adhuc in terris, aduersus Satanae, carnis, & mundi huius irrequietas impressiones gladiatoria fide dimicat. hos nulla tanta uis est, nec aura superbiae, nec afflictionum aestus, nec tyrannorum saeuitia aut discordantes doctorum rationes, quae a recto fidei gradu ac scripturarum, queat deiicere. Quia per uerbum Dei, in Christo, ceu supra firmissimam petram constabiliti sunt. Tunc clericos compellas suos: Videte, inquit, quàm obfirmatus sit hic nebulo, quomodo diabolus eum agitat, ad confirmandos errores. his, totum hunc diem, nos detineret, si permitteremus. Tum è clericis quispiam eum adorsus. Quoniam, inquit, iam dudum quaestus est, malitiose confictū esse aduersus se testimonium, quod à Salopiensibus mittebatur: Interrogetur itaque quid de obiectis articulis sentiat, ut ex ore proprio habeamus quod testificemur. Moxq; reuocata schedula, Archiepiscopus sic inquit. Principio hic tibi obiectū est, quòd apud Salopienses, in templo diui Ceddæ, publicè prædicaueris, manere panem in altaris sacramento post consecrationem. Quid huic respondeas? Guilhelm. Nihil ibi agitabatur de hoc sacramento, nisi sub hac forma. Siquidem cum illic è suggesto, diuina praecepta pertractarem, euenit ex missa priuata, ad hostiae elevationem tinnitum fieri. Sequutus est ilico, ut fit, populi concursus ac strepitus, iamque relicta concione, cunctiali alio auerteban tur. Quamobrem ita eos allocutus sum, Christiani fratres, multo efficacior est, uiua huius sacramenti uirtus in fide, quam in aliquo exteriori sensu. Standum igitur esset ad salutiferam uerbi auscultationem potius, quam prodigiose sic cocitari ad spectacula sacramentorum, quum recta fides hinc magis adaugeatur. Haecque fere erant, quae de sacramento id temporis commemini me prolocutum. Archiepiscop. Magis hic testibus idoneis fido, quam tibi. Sed age quoniam ad inficialem statum praesidii causa confugis, dic tandem quid tute hac de re sentias. Man neatne in consecrata hostia materialis panis an non? Guilielmus. In scriptu ris nusquam hoc (materialis) uocabulum reperire est. Mihi igitur quoties de Eucharistia sermo incidit, de pane materiali nihil fit mentionis. tionis. Archiepiscop. Quo pacto igitur plebem, de sacramento hoc, instituis? Guliel. Vt ipsemet credo. Archiepisc. Edicas tuum credere. Guliel. Credo, quòd dominus Iesus, ipsa qua tradebatur nocte, accepit panem, & gratias agens, benedixit, fregit, deditƅ discipulis, dicens: Accipite & comedite ex hoc omnes, hoc est corpus meum, quod pro uobis datur. Hanc omnium debere esse fidem, testatur Mattheus, Marcus, Lucas & Paulus. Aliam ego fidem nec agnosco, nec doceo, quam sufficere iudico. In hac sola uiuere, & mori constitui. Archiep. Certissimum est sacramentum hoc Christi corpus esse, sub forma panis. Sed tu tuiq; similes panem permanere astruitis. Guliel. Nec ego, nec mei similes, quos pro hæreticis exploditis, secus sentimus, quàm dixi. Nihilominus doceri à uobis expeto, quo pacto hoc intelligatur ex Paulo:Id sentite in uobis,quod et in Christo Iesu,qui cum in forma Dei esset &c. Nōne Paulus hic pro sub-stantia utitur? Quid quod, ecclesia in quotidianis diuae uirginis ho-ris,huic concordat,dicens. Memen to saluti s autor, quod nostri quon-dam corporis,ex illibata uirgine,na scendo formam sumps… Id mo-do,<bl>ὑπὲ τὰς χάριτας</bl>,respondeas,si corporis nostri forma, substantia di-ci non possit? Archiep. Proposito tuo non satisfaciam ,postquam ec-clesia aliter determinauerit. Credis illius determinationi uel non? Gu-ilielmus. Quicquid praepositi,e suo cere-bro protulerint,fides certe manet in-tegra. Ante hac nō audiui humanas traditiones sub fidei uocabulo ue-nire. Arch. Si haec prius non audiue-ris rectam ecclesiae fidem non sapis. Sed quid de hac re dicūt doctores? Guilihel. Magnus ecclesiae doctor diuus Paulus integra docens huius sacrasacramẽti fidem, panem quem frangimus id uocat. In canonæ missæ post consecrationem dicitur etiā panis. Præterea quilibet huius regni sacerdos, post eucharistię susceptionẽ, hoc dicit. Quod ore sumpsimus Domine, pura mente capiamus, i. fide, ut mihi uidetur. Augustinus etiam fateturid forepanem, quod oculus uidet, & quod creditur esse uerum Christi corpus. Et huius opinionis est Fulgentius quoq; ecclesiæ doctor nō aspernandus. In secreto missæ Christi natiuitatis in aurora, sicetiam habetur. Idem refulsit Deus, sic terrena substantia nobis conferat quod diuinum est. Quam sententiam cum secreto quartæ feriæ, quatuor temporum in Septembri à uobis enodari cupio. Archiep. Iam demum intelligo quid quæras, & quo Diabolus te agat, ne ecclesiæ sanxionibus te dedas. Sed age modo, citius respondeas an credas post consecra
units.tr: Being asked by the archbishop what the Church was, he replied: "This Church, which I call holy, I believe to be Christ and the saints." Archbishop: "I grant, of course, in heaven. But what is the Church on earth?" William: It is divided into two parts. One part, the chief one, rejoices in triumph with Christ, its enemies having been conquered. The other, still on earth, fights with sword-like faith against the restless assaults of Satan, the flesh and this world. Neither the great force of these, nor the breath of pride, nor the heat of afflictions, nor the savagery of tyrants, nor the conflicting arguments of teachers, can cast them down from the right step of faith and of the Scriptures, because they are established through the word of God in Christ, as upon a most firm rock. Then he addressed his clerks: "See," he said, "how hardened this scoundrel is, and how the devil drives him on to confirm his errors. He would keep us the whole day with these matters, if we allowed it." Then one of the clerks, approaching him, said: "Since it was complained a long while ago that a testimony sent from the people of Shrewsbury was maliciously fabricated against him, let him be asked what he thinks about the articles brought against him, so that we may have from his own mouth what we can bear witness to." And immediately, recalling the schedule, the archbishop spoke thus: "First, it is charged against you that at Shrewsbury, in the church of St Chad, you publicly preached that the bread remains in the sacrament of the altar after consecration. What do you answer to this?" William: "Nothing was being discussed there about this sacrament, except in this way. For while I was treating the divine precepts from the pulpit, it happened that, at the elevation of the host in a private Mass, a bell rang out. Immediately, as usually happens, there was a rush and uproar of the people, and now, the sermon abandoned, they were all turning their attention elsewhere. Therefore I addressed them thus: 'Christian brothers, the living power of this sacrament is far more effective in faith than in any outward sense. We ought therefore to stand by the saving hearing of the word rather than be stirred up so wonderfully to gaze at sacraments, since right faith is increased more by this.' And these were almost the things I recall saying about the sacrament at that time." Archbishop: "I trust witnesses who are fit more than you. But come, since you take refuge in an evasive position for the sake of protection, tell me at last what you yourself think about this matter. Do you hold that in the consecrated host there is material bread or not?" William: "The word 'material' cannot be found anywhere in the Scriptures. Therefore, whenever talk of the Eucharist arises, no mention is made by me of material bread." Archbishop: "In what way then do you instruct the people about this sacrament?" William: "As I myself believe." Archbishop: "Declare that you believe it." William: "I believe that the Lord Jesus, on the very night in which he was betrayed, took bread, and giving thanks, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to his disciples, saying: 'Take and eat of this, all of you; this is my body, which is given for you.' That this must be the faith of all, Matthew, Mark, Luke and Paul bear witness. I neither acknowledge nor teach any other faith than this, which I judge sufficient. In this alone I have resolved to live and to die." Archbishop: "It is most certain that this sacrament is the body of Christ under the form of bread. But you and those like you assert that the bread remains." William: "Neither I nor those like me, whom you cast out as heretics, think otherwise than I have said. Nevertheless I desire to be taught by you how that passage of Paul is to be understood: 'Let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus, who, being in the form of God, etc.' Does not Paul here use 'form' for 'substance'? What of the fact that the Church, in its daily hours of the blessed Virgin, agrees with this, saying: 'Remember, Saviour, that you were once formed from our body, born of the undefiled Virgin'? Could you answer this, if the form of our body cannot be called its substance? [ὑπὲρ τὰς χάριτας]" Archbishop: "I shall not satisfy your proposal until the Church has determined otherwise. Do you believe that determination or not?" William: "Whatever the prelates may bring forth from their own brain, faith certainly remains whole. Until now I have not heard that human traditions come under the name of faith." Archbishop: "If you have not heard this before, you do not savour of the true faith of the Church. But what do the teachers say about this matter?" William: "The great teacher of the Church, the blessed Paul, teaching the whole faith of this sacrament, calls the bread which we break by that name. In the canon of the Mass, after consecration, it is also called bread. Moreover, every priest of this kingdom, after receiving the Eucharist, says this: 'What we have taken with our mouth, Lord, may we receive with a pure mind,' that is, by faith, as it seems to me. Augustine also confesses that the outward thing which the eye sees is bread, and what is believed to be the true body of Christ. Fulgentius also, a Church teacher not to be despised, is of this opinion. In the secret prayer of the Mass of Christ's nativity at dawn, it is likewise found: 'God shone forth, so that earthly substance may bring to us what is divine.' I wish you to explain this opinion to me together with the secret prayer of the Wednesday of the Ember days in September." Archbishop: "Now at last I understand what you are seeking, and to what the devil is driving you, so that you do not surrender yourself to the ordinances of the Church. But come, answer quickly: do you believe that after consecration in the sacrament the substance of bread remains, or not?"

units.la: Fulgentius tionem in sacramento manere sub‐stantiam panis, an secus. Guilielm. Quod accidens sit sine subiecto, ut fatetur hodie de hoc sacramento ec‐clesia, nec affirmare, nec negare au‐deo, cum res spinosa multisq; argu‐mentationibus obnoxia sit, captumq; in‐genioli mei longe superet, hoc discu‐tiendum λορομαχοις istis ac subtilibus sophistis relinquo, simplici fide mea contentus. His enim consuetum est, nodosas huiusmodi difficultates in utramque partem, ultro citro ar‐gumentis tractare, donec se mutuo non intelligant, dumq; tantum sibi tribuant, stultissimi reddunturapud Deum. Archiep. Non est animus modo te subtilibus scholasticorum argutijs inuoluere, cum sciam imperitum. Sed cogam te ecclesiae obsequi decretis. Guiliel. Mille post Christi incarnationem annis, sufficiebat ad hominum salutem, ecclesiae, quam dixi, determinatio. Quaeuero
units.tr: Whether, after the consecration, the substance of bread remains in the sacrament or not. Thorpe: That an accident can exist without a subject, as the Church today teaches about this sacrament, I neither dare to affirm nor to deny. The matter is thorny and open to many arguments, and it far exceeds the capacity of my small wit. I leave this to be debated by those word-battlers [λογομάχοις] and subtle sophists, being content with my simple faith. For it is their habit to handle such knotty difficulties back and forth with arguments on both sides until they no longer understand one another, and while they claim so much for themselves, they become most foolish before God. Archbishop: I have no wish to entangle you in the subtle quibbles of the schoolmen, since I know you are unlearned. But I will compel you to obey the decrees of the Church.

units.la: Determinatio Romanae ecclesiae post mille annos non valet. uerò deinceps post Satanam ab angelo solutum, per fratrem Thomâ, eiusq; farinæ sophistas, inuenta sunt in Ecclesiâ (ueluti Accidens sine sub iecto atque id genus nugæ) his ego neutiquam assentiendum arbitror: Ex huius fratris emendicata aliunde sententia, fidei articulum non constituam, De me uideat, agatq; Dominus, pro sancto arbitratu suo. Archiepiscopus. Has manus non effugies hodie, ni sententiam in diuersum flexeris.
units.tr: The determination of the Roman Church after a thousand years is not valid. Thorpe: But whatever was afterwards brought into the Church, after Satan was loosed by the angel, through Brother Thomas and sophists of his kind (such as "accident without subject" and that sort of trifle), I judge that I must by no means assent to. I will not establish an article of faith on this brother's opinion, borrowed from elsewhere. Let the Lord see to me and deal with me as he pleases. Archbishop: You will not escape these hands today unless you change your opinion.

units.la: Iam ad secundum articulum, de imaginibus, quid dicis? Guilielm. Autore Mose traditum legimus, quod cuncta quæ fecerit Deus fuerint ualde bona. Quapropter in suo quæq; genere, & ad finem à Domino præscriptum, honore sunt prosequenda: præsertim homo, quē Deus ad suam similitudinem creauit, præ cæteris animantibus colendus. Imò Christianos homines ob insignes
units.tr: Now to the second article, concerning images: what do you say? Thorpe: We read, as handed down by Moses, that all the things God made were very good. Therefore each thing, in its own kind and for the end prescribed by the Lord, is to be honoured, especially man, whom God created in his own likeness and who ought to be cherished above other living creatures. Indeed, it is fitting that Christians, out of love, should honour one another for the outstanding gifts of God.

units.la: Dei dotes, honore inuicem præue-nire, ex amore decet. Lignum, lapi-des, stannum, æs, ferrum, argentum, & aurum ex quibus imagines fiunt, etiam sunt in suo genere bona. Sculpturæ tamen, conflaturæ, pictVRÆ aut huiusmodi aliæ artificum inuen-tiones non sunt à fidelibus adoran-dæ, quamtumlibet à magistratibus approbatæ, & ordinatæ ut sint eorū calendaria, qui nec Deum in uerbo, nec in creaturis laudant, nec ex mi-randis eius operibus glorificant in forma, quam homo creaturis infert, horum, inquam, nihil potest absque idolomania adorari, cum res sint ita expertes formarum, quas Deus im-presserit. Archiepiscopus. Assenti-or imagines propter se non colen-das, sed propter figuras impressas, uel propter id, quod foris exprimūt, puta, crucifixum propter Christi pas-sionem, & imaginē Trinitatis, diuæ Mariæ, ac sanctorum propter eos quos referunt. Nam & terrenorum regum diplomata, insignis ornata, utique à subditis sine magnis honoribus minime suscipiuntur, quanto igitur magis Dei & sanctorum imagines? Guiliel. Haec humana est similitudo, nec appositè quadrans cum rebus diuinis, quum Moses, Dauid, Salomon, Esaias, Baruch caeterique bibliographi ferè omnes disertissimis verbis, nec sine minis imagines statuarias quibuslibet interdicunt. Archiep. Obstinate loselle, quamuis ante natum seruatore nulla erat trinitatis expressio, est tamen nunc ex illius relatione manifesta. Licetque ex doctis plusculi opinentur, errorem esse trinitatem depingere, ego tamen vehementer id necessarium statuo, quum plaebanos ad deuocionis ardorem non uulgariter sollicitat. Tunc suos allocutus haec uerba habuit. In partibus, ait, transmarinis praestantissimi sunt artifices, qui istiusmodi morem rem habent, quem laudo, ut si quod simulachrum, pictura, plastica, aut sculptura ijs ѓedenda sit, apud sacerdotem primum scelerum conscientia se exonerant, uotisque obstringunt, uel ad ieiunandum, uel orandum, aut peregrinandum, astipulates interim a sacerdote, ut precibus artem iuuet apud Dominum, quo deuotam imaginem queant elicere. Guiliel. Non dubium, quin hos satis poenitet artifices facti sui, si Mosi, Dauidis, Salomonis, Esaiae, Baruch, similiumque scripta intelligeret, mallentque quiduis perpeti prius, quam ad tam blasphemas & insanas artes recurrere. Et sceleratius adhuc ipsis peccant sacerdotes, qui malesuadis consilijs ijs animum suggerunt, ad id quod ex ore Dei impium est, ac maledictu. Quod si Christum ac Apostolos imitati, sacerdotes rite fungerentur officio suo, haud magnopere opus esset, opinor, mutis imaginum calenlendariis,ad cognoscendum Deum. Sed inexplebilis ecclefiastarum auaricia,his atqz aliis dæmonum imposturis,credulam multitudinem nunquam cessat ad damnationem pertrahere. Archiep. Te maledictum sentio, & omnes tuæ sectæ sacerdotes, qui populi destruitis deuotionem. Quid, pulchrumne id tibi uidetur esse, miserrime carnifex, Ecclesiam sic cernere imaginibus uacuã? Guiliel. Nulli salubrius orant quam qui occlusis sensibus, mente sola, in spiritu & ueritate subuolãt ad Deũ. Christus namqz beatos hos prædicat qui crediderunt, & non uiderunt. Quamobrem nobis soloDei uerbo, sine imaginibus innitendum est. Archiepiscopus hic irritatior, subdit. Quicquid in contrariũ obieceris,nequa hæretice, religiosum affirmo trinitatis imaginem colere. Quid & tu super hoc dicis? Nõne motiuum est animæ, talia contemplari? Guiliel. PercuPercuperem scrupulo conscientiae quodam per uos liberari: Cum Pater, Filius, & Spiritus sanctus idem semper sit Deus, & eiusdem aeternitatis in utroque testamento, multiqp extiterint inter Prophetas et Patres, tum confessores, tum martyres, cur non perinde in ueteri lege, huiusmodi permissa sunt simulachra pro laicorum calendariis: Archiep. Sinagoga Iudaeorum eandem non posside-bat autoritatem quam nunc habet Ecclesia. Guiliel. Diuus Gregorius uir percelebris, magniqp erat nominis, qui(ut proditum est)plurimum commendabat impium quendam, Serenum nomine, quod imagines adorari prohibuerit. Archiep. Os impudens, medius fidius, ueritati non magis caniculo, fauces. Londini apud Diuum Paulum, ad ualuas aquilonares, tot habentur miracula, de diua uirgine parathalassia, & frequenter alibi per Angliam, Annon ergo haec
units.tr: Wood, stones, tin, bronze, iron, silver and gold, from which images are made, are also good in their own kind. Yet sculptures, castings, paintings, or other such inventions of craftsmen are not to be adored by the faithful, however much they are approved and ordained by magistrates as the calendars of those who praise God neither in his Word nor in creatures, nor glorify him from his wonderful works, in the form which man gives to creatures. None of these, I say, can be adored without idolatry, since such things are devoid of the forms which God has impressed. Archbishop: I agree that images are not to be honoured for their own sake, but for the figures impressed on them, or for what they express externally: for example, the crucifix for the passion of Christ, and the image of the Trinity, of the blessed Mary, and of the saints, for the sake of those they represent. For the decrees of earthly kings, adorned with their seals, are certainly not received by subjects without great honour; how much more, then, the images of God and the saints? Thorpe: This is a human likeness, and it does not fit well with divine things, since Moses, David, Solomon, Isaiah, Baruch and almost all the other writers forbid statues of any kind in the most explicit words, and not without threats. Archbishop: Obstinate fellow, although before the Saviour was born there was no expression of the Trinity, there is now a clear one from his revelation. And although many learned men think it an error to depict the Trinity, I hold it to be altogether necessary, since it stirs the common people powerfully to the ardour of devotion. Then, addressing his people, he spoke these words: "In the lands beyond the sea," he said, "there are most excellent craftsmen who have this custom, which I commend: whenever an image, painting, figure or sculpture is to be made, they first unburden their consciences of sins before a priest and bind themselves by vows, either to fasting, prayer or pilgrimage, while meanwhile the priest supports them, that by his prayers he may help the craft before the Lord, so that they may bring forth a devout image." Thorpe: There is no doubt that these craftsmen would be sorry enough for what they do if they understood the writings of Moses, David, Solomon, Isaiah, Baruch and the like, and they would rather suffer anything than resort to such blasphemous and insane arts. The priests sin even more wickedly, who with evil counsel put such thoughts into their minds, toward what is impious and cursed by the mouth of God. If priests, imitating Christ and the Apostles, duly performed their office, I think there would hardly be any need for dumb calendars of images in order to know God. But the insatiable greed of the clergy never ceases to draw the credulous multitude to damnation by these and other deceits of demons. Archbishop: I perceive that you are a cursed man, and all the priests of your sect, who destroy the devotion of the people. What, do you think it is a fine thing, most wretched executioner, to see the Church thus emptied of images?

units.la: Serenus laudatus a Gregorio quod imagines prohibuerit. hæc loca, maiori plebis deuotione, aliis impensius sunt frequentanda: Guiliel. Certus sum, à Deo nullum fieri prodigium, quo imagines attolli antur. Nec est in illis uirtus ulla, (ut Salopiæ prædicaram) quamobrem ab hominibus quærantur, aut genuū inflexionibus, munusculis, uotis, aut honore aliquo afficiantur. Nam serpentem æneum, Dei præcepto per Mosen erectū, ob idololatriæ periculum aboleuit pius rex Ezechias. Referunt sancti Doctores Augustinus, Gregorius, I. Chrysostomus, & plærique alij, quod Dæmones portentis huiusmodi incredulorum animos ob infidelitatem deludunt. Multo enim his diebus propensiores sunt ad prodigia quærenda, quàm ad salutiferum Dei uerbum rite uel audiendum, uel credendum. Prædixit itaque seruator, magno eorum pudore, quòd generatio adultera portentuosa signa semper quærat, contra uero Euangelium recta fide semper suscipiendum est. Sufficere nobis debet uerbum Dei, sine simulachrorum prodigijs. Sed quum Deus pater Spiritus sit, nec formam habeat nobis explicabilem, non satis admiror, quam poteris ei affingere similitudinem. Archiep. Sufficit Ecclesiae filijs ea trinitatis figura, quā ei, totannis, permiserit eadem mater, Verū quum tu impie putridum fis, atque ab eius gremio resectum membrum, sacras illius ordinationes uilipendis.
units.tr: Serenus, praised by Gregory because he forbade images. Thorpe: No one prays more profitably than those who, with their senses shut, fly up to God in mind alone, in spirit and in truth. For Christ pronounces blessed those who have believed and not seen. Therefore we must rely on the Word of God alone, without images. The archbishop, growing more angry, adds: "Whatever you object to the contrary, you heretic, I affirm that it is a religious act to honour an image of the Trinity. What do you say to this? Is it not a stimulus to the soul to contemplate such things?" Thorpe: I would gladly be freed from a scruple of conscience by you. Since the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are always the same God, and of the same eternity in both testaments, and since many confessors and martyrs have arisen among the Prophets and Fathers, why, under the old law, were such images not similarly permitted for the calendars of the laity? Archbishop: The synagogue of the Jews did not possess the same authority that the Church now has. Thorpe: The blessed Gregory, a very famous man of great name, as is reported, greatly commended a certain impious man named Serenus, because he forbade the worship of images. Archbishop: Shameless mouth! By my faith, your throat is no more fitting for truth than a dog's in the dog-days. At London, at St Paul's, at the north doors, there are so many miracles of the Virgin Mary "by the sea" [παραθαλάσσια], and frequently elsewhere throughout England. Should not these places therefore be visited more often, with greater devotion of the people? Thorpe: I am certain that no prodigy is wrought by God through which images are exalted. Nor is there any power in them (as I preached at Shrewsbury), so they should not be sought by men, nor honoured with bended knees, little gifts, vows or any other reverence. For the bronze serpent, which God commanded to be raised by Moses, the pious king Hezekiah abolished because of the danger of idolatry. The holy doctors Augustine, Gregory, Chrysostom and many others report that demons deceive the minds of unbelievers by such portents, because of their unbelief. For in these days men are far more inclined to seek out prodigies than to hear or believe the saving Word of God rightly. Therefore the Saviour foretold, to their great shame, that "an adulterous generation seeks a sign" [Matth. 12.]; on the contrary, the Gospel must always be received with true faith. The Word of God should be enough for us, without the prodigies of images. But since God is Spirit and has no form that we can explain, I do not much wonder what likeness you could attribute to him. Archbishop: The sons of the Church are content with that figure of the Trinity which their mother has allowed them every year. But since you, impious man, are rotten, and a limb cut off from her bosom, you despise her sacred ordinances.

units.la: Iam labete die, ad tertium articulum de peregrinatione respondeas,
units.tr: Now, as the day wears on, answer concerning the third article, on pilgrimage.

units.la: Dicebas (ut a dignis fide accipimus) stupidos esse, ac sine sensu illos, profugos, maledictos, & miseros, qui ex uotis peregrinetur, seu Cantuariam, seu Beuerlacum, seu Carlingtonum, seu Vualsingamiam, aut alia sanctae peregrinationis loca. Guiliel. Quicquid retulerint aemuli, duas, Salopię praedicaram, Deo placere peregrinationum nationum species. Archiep. Quos opinaris ergo iniustos fore peregrinos: Guiliel. Qui Deum spiritu quaerunt, & qui summis viribus scelera fastidientes, domini praecepta serua re laborant, hi non aliter credunt, quam Christus in Euangelio docuerit, aut ex Apostolorum symbolo haut serunt, hi charitatis operibus inhaerent & invicem pro sua quisque portione subveniunt, nihil inde sperantes, nisi iusta Dei promissa, isti saepissime conscientias domino aperiunt, illius quotidie timetes offensam, hi peregrini delectantur maxime, cum viderint dominum quaerentes proximos, mundi prospera aspernantes, grinatio* carnis desideria abdicates, in adversis patientes, in consiliis prudentes * virtuti addictos, omni tyrannorum seuitia superiores, pauperibus σνμ- πάσχοντας, oratione frequentissimos aliaque Christi exempla pie sectantes. Has videlicet divinas notas ac
units.tr: You said (as we have received from trustworthy persons) that those who go on pilgrimage out of vows, whether to Canterbury, Beverley, Carlton, Walsingham or other places of holy pilgrimage, are stupid and senseless, fugitives, cursed and wretched. Thorpe: Whatever my rivals have reported, I preached at Shrewsbury that there are two kinds of pilgrimage that please God. Archbishop: Whom, then, do you think will be unjust pilgrims? Thorpe: Those who seek God in spirit, and who, hating sins with all their strength, labour to keep the Lord's commandments. These believe no otherwise than Christ taught in the Gospel, or than the Apostles' Creed sets forth. They cling to works of charity and help one another, each according to his portion, hoping for nothing from it except the righteous promises of God. These very often lay open their consciences to the Lord, fearing daily to offend him. These pilgrims take the greatest delight when they have seen the Lord seeking their neighbours; despising the world's prosperity, denying the desires of the flesh; patient in adversity, prudent in counsel, devoted to virtue, superior to all the cruelty of tyrants; sharing the sufferings of the poor [συμπάσχοντας]; most constant in prayer; and piously following the other examples of Christ. These, of course, carry about these divine marks and conditions, and these are the people whose pilgrimage God approves. But your pilgrims nowhere show these conditions of piety, for I have had enough and more than enough experience of them. Out of six hundred you can scarcely produce one who knows the commandments of God, who recites the Lord's Prayer or the creed correctly:

units.la: T conditiones circumferunt hi, quorum peregrinationem comprobat Deus. At uestri peregrini has pietatis conditiones nusquam ostendunt, expertus enim satis satisque no ui. E fexcentis uix unum proferas, qui Dei mandata calleat, qui oratio nem Dominicam aut fidei symbolu recte pronunciet: plus quam friuola sunt quae plurimos ad peregrinatio nem adducunt, ueluti corporis salu britas, carnalis amicitia, prosperitas, luxus, petulantia, prodigalitas, et le nones, at quid tandem hi post tam gra ues impensas, & membra defatiga ta reperiunt, nisi offa mortuorum, ac mutas imagines? Haec uanissima esse quis non uidet, qui ullum diuini spiritus gustu sapit? Quod si quid hinc lucelli prouenit, (prouenit autem permultum) id uniuersum, uel in au uaros sacerdotes, uel in meretrices deciditur, ut sileamus interim neglectas domi familias, quibus necessaria ria cura cuiq; Christiano debeba-tur. Itaq; quod ex Dei præcepto proximis ac propinquis impendēdum fuerat, id in profanos usus profun-dunt miseri. Sunt præterea ex his multi qui partim mutuato, partim furto iter peragunt, nunquam resti-tutis precijs. Sambucis utuntur & fi-stulis, nonnunquā & obscœnis car-minibus, quo magis carni adlube-scant. Demum reuersi, nihil referūt proximis præter hypocritas blasphe-mias, & maledicta mendacia. Ar-chiepiscopus. Nequissime uerbe-ro, quod in hoc negocio præcipu-um est non uides, uidelicet itineran-tium labores & pœnas. Quod tu po-tissimum uitio uertis, id premio, lau-de-q; amplissima dignum uidetur. Nec peregrinationi quicquam ossi-cit, quod tubicines, ac histriones se-cum ducunt, quibus pedum læsio-nes, aut itineris tædium, uel fallant, uel mulceant. Guilielmus. Paulus
units.tr: These are the conditions that those whose pilgrimage God approves carry with them. But your pilgrims nowhere show these conditions of piety, for I have known enough and more than enough of them. Out of six hundred you can hardly name one who knows God's commandments or recites the Lord's Prayer or the creed correctly. The things that draw most people to pilgrimage are more than trivial: bodily health, carnal friendship, prosperity, luxury, wantonness, extravagance, and the like. But what do these men find after such heavy expenses and wearied limbs, except the bones of the dead and dumb images? Who that has tasted anything of the divine Spirit does not see that these things are utterly vain? And if any small gain comes from it (and a great deal does), it is all handed over either to greedy priests or to prostitutes. I say nothing of the families neglected at home, to whom every Christian owes necessary care. So what should have been spent on neighbours and kinsfolk by God's command, these wretches pour out on profane uses. Moreover, many of them travel partly on borrowed money and partly by theft, never making restitution. They use sambucas and pipes, and sometimes obscene songs, the more to indulge the flesh. And when they return, they report nothing to their neighbours except hypocritical blasphemies and lying slanders. Archbishop: Wicked fellow, you do not see what is chief in this matter, namely the labours and sufferings of travellers. What you find most fault with, that seems worthy of reward and the highest praise. Nor does it hinder the pilgrimage in any way that trumpeters and actors go with them, whose injuries to the feet or the tedium of the road either distract or soothe them. William: Paul teaches us to weep rather with those who weep.

units.la: docet, cum flentibus flendum potius. Archiepiscopus. Quicquid in hos deblateras, censeo peregrinationes adminicula esse quædam ad maiorem gratiam, cuius te prorsus expertem iudico. Adeo nullam non tentas machinam, quo populi devotionem tollas e medio. Sed hoc ultimo nihil proficis, cum dicat regius vates omnigenis laudari Deum multis instrumentis. Guilielmus. Iuxta Doctorum interpretamenta, hæc nobis modo ad spiritum flectenda sunt, nec admodum diuaricat Pauli interpretatio, innuentis hæc, olim in figura contigisse: nobis proinde cauendum, ne frigidæ literæ a scopo aberrantes inhæreamus. Christus non antea Iairi filiam suscitarat, quam tubicines e foribus eiecti essent, ceu inutiles, ad fidei negocia, remoras. Archiepiscopus. Itane ais, scelus, quod Ecclesiis non liceat ad Dei cultum, organis uti? Guilielmus. Secundum cundum humanam quidem constitutionem fateor. Sed ex Christi institutione multis nominibus Deo gratior foret, simul ac plebi maiori commodo, organorum vice, euangelica concio. Archiepiscopus. Organa modulato concentu, ac dulcisonis cantibus admista vulgi animos plus mille concionibus afficiunt. Guiliel-mus. Mundi huius amatores fortasse, istiusmodi sensuum oblectamentis capiuntur. At longe diuersa ratione Christi despectis hic tyronibus accidit, quibus solo animae cibo saturari, id unice cordi est. Hos enim Dei timor, & amor ad rerum caelestium desideria a fluxis huius mundi, & carnis delitiis auocant. Quemadmodum praeclare a Hieronymo dictum est, Neminem posse simul cum mundo gaudere, & cum Christo regnare. Quo responso in bilem efferatus Archiepiscopus. Quid, inquit, idiotam hunc timere putatis, quum in mea praesentia tam libere loquatur. Per Deum uiuum, aliter adhuc tibi uidebitur.
units.tr: Archbishop: Whatever you babble against these people, I think pilgrimages are certain aids to greater grace, and of this I judge you wholly ignorant. Thus you try every contrivance to remove the devotion of the people from the midst. But you achieve nothing by this last, since the royal prophet says that God is praised with instruments of every kind. William: According to the interpretations of the doctors, these things are for us now to be turned to the spirit, nor does Paul's interpretation greatly differ from this, indicating that these things once happened in a figure. Therefore we must take care not to cling to cold letters and stray from the goal. Christ did not raise Jairus's daughter until the trumpeters, as useless hindrances to the business of faith, had been thrown out of the doors. Archbishop: So you say, villain, that it is not lawful for churches to use organs in the worship of God? William: I admit it according to human ordinance. But according to Christ's institution, in many ways the preaching of the gospel would be more pleasing to God, and at the same time of greater benefit to the people, in place of organs. Archbishop: Organs, with their modulated harmony and sweet-sounding songs mixed in, move the minds of the crowd more than a thousand sermons. William: Perhaps lovers of this world are captured by such delights of the senses. But by a far different reasoning it happens to these novices, despised by Christ, for whom it is their sole concern to be filled with the food of the soul alone. For the fear and love of God draw them away from the fleeting things of this world and the pleasures of the flesh toward longing for heavenly things. As Jerome nobly said, no one can rejoice with the world and reign with Christ at the same time. At this answer the archbishop, enraged to bile, said: "What do you think this idiot fears, since he speaks so freely in my presence? By the living God, he will see things differently yet."

units.la: Sed ad quartum articulum, quid dicis? An licite possint sacerdotes a suis exigere decimas? Guiliel. Nihil illic a me de decimis attactum est. Sed post menstruam inclusionem in carcere, adierat me ignotus quispiam, qui de decimis plura percontabatur. Cui nec uolebam, nec si uellem, ausus sum efflagitata denegare, quum a Petro admonemur cuilibet fidem petenti modeste esse respondendu. Dicebam igitur sub umbra ueteris instrumenti decimas olim deberi Leuitis, quas suis Christus nusquam in nouo concedit. Praecipit enim ille, solis misericordiae operibus incumbendum, sicubi usu uteniat, ut superfluis nostris, aliorum necessitas indigeat. Non ex oblationibus, aut decimis, sed ex charitate eorum, quibus praedicarat, eleemosinatia, uixit ille cum discipulis. Post eius uero Ascensionem, suscepto Spiritu sancto, manibus operabantur apostoli, pro victu necessario, quod nō semel ex Paulo uidere est. Necesse tamen est ut de Euangelio viuant, qui euangelij ministeriū exercent, quod & idem affirmat Paulus. Sed cautio hic adhibeatur, ne in de grauetur populus. Apud historicos quosdam proditum legimus, Gregorium papam decimum, anno Christi 1271 decimas primum Ecclesijs cōcessisse. Christi sacerdos non est, qui eius, ac apostolorum ue-stigijs non respondeat, quamuis mil-le unctionibus, rasurisq; commen-detur populo, ut piè probat Augu-stinus, Gregorius, Chrysostomus, & Lincolniensis. Archiepiscopus. Credis hanc populo salubrem esse doctrinam? Plane repugnant hæc sanctorum patrū sanxionibus, qui sacerdotibus, nec decimas inuidet, nec oblationes auferunt, nec ullas plebis deuotiones prohibet. Guil. Si presbiterorū numerus imminutus esset, nec alij in hoc albo censerentur, nisi qui Christi & apostolorum exemplo, administrando verbo syncere inuigilaret, abunde pro facto ex plebis Christianæ largitate suppeteret, quod cuique ad sobrium uictum satis foret. Ad quam uocē lacessītus ex clericis quispiam respondit. Belle & suauiter profecto abs te dictum, ut uulgi liberalitatem expectemus, cum uixiuris stricti rigore id faciant. Guil. Nec mirum adeo, si clero populus tantopere obnitatur, cum eorum conuersatio sit à Christi institutis quàm diuersissima. Decimæ, fundationes, & legata, cum aliis populi eleemosinis, post mediocria sacerdotū salaria, olim habebantur pro bonis pauperum, communi iuris decreto. Quorum ipsi postea dispensatores effecti, in proprios usus,
units.tr: "But on the fourth article, what do you say? Can priests lawfully demand tithes from their people?" William: "Nothing about tithes was touched on by me there. But after a month's confinement in prison, some unknown man came to me and asked at length about tithes. I neither wished to deny what he demanded, nor, even had I wished, would I have dared, since Peter admonishes us to answer modestly anyone who asks for an account of our faith. So I said that under the shadow of the old covenant, tithes were once owed to the Levites, which Christ nowhere grants to his own in the new. For he enjoins that we should devote ourselves only to works of mercy, wherever use requires, so that our superfluities may supply the needs of others. He lived with his disciples not on offerings or tithes, but on the alms of those to whom he preached. After his Ascension, however, once the Holy Spirit had been received, the apostles worked with their hands for necessary sustenance, as we see more than once from Paul. Yet it is necessary that those who exercise the ministry of the gospel live by the gospel, which Paul also affirms. But caution must be applied here, lest the people be burdened. We read in certain historians that Pope Gregory the Tenth first granted tithes to churches in the year of Christ 1271. He is not a priest of Christ who does not answer to the footsteps of Christ and the apostles, however much he is commended to the people with a thousand anointings and tonsures, as Augustine, Gregory, Chrysostom and the Lincolnian rightly prove." Archbishop: "Do you believe this doctrine is wholesome for the people? These things plainly contradict the decrees of the holy fathers, who neither grudge priests their tithes, nor take away their offerings, nor forbid any devotion of the people." William: "If the number of presbyters were diminished, and no others were counted on this roll except those who, after the example of Christ and the apostles, watch diligently over the sincere administration of the word, there would be enough and to spare from the generosity of the Christian people, enough for each to live soberly." Provoked by this word, one of the clergy replied: "Certainly you have spoken well and sweetly, that we should wait for the liberality of the common people, when they do this under the strict rigour of those who are about to live." William: "It is no wonder that the people so strongly resist the clergy, since their way of life is most unlike Christ's institutions. Tithes, endowments and legacies, along with the other alms of the people, beyond modest stipends for the priests, were once held to be the goods of the poor, by the common law of the decree. Having become their dispensers, they have turned all of it to their own uses,

units.la: & et (quod hoc foedius) luxum omnia, publici muneris obliti, detorserunt.
units.tr: and (what is more shameful) to luxury, forgetting their public duty."

units.la: Et quid miremur igitur, si homines haec illis detrahant, praesertim cum participes se quodammodo scelerum eorum videant, quorum largitionibus ipsi abutantur ad omne nequitiam. Archiepiscopus. Nunquam rem facies scelus, qui matrem spiritualem ita despicias. Qua frote haec te, non pudet, coram imperita plebecula sermocinari? An non decimae sunt quaesso, sacerdotibus ad victum necessariae? Guilielm. Ut idoneus autor est Paulus, solis leuitici generis sacerdotibus decimae debebantur, in veteri lege. At Christi sacerdotes cum de genere Iuda sunt, non Leui, nequaquam igitur ex Dei promissione ad illos decimae spectant. Cum ergo mutatu sit sacerdotium, necesse est mutari & legem, ut iam non Mosen sed Christum, & Apostolos, sacerdotes nostros imitari co tenit. Porro nec par est, ut sit discipulus domino suo superior, sed ut se simplicem, modestum, mansuetum, ac patientem gerat, magistri utique exemplo. Archiepiscopus hic tamen bile lymphatus. Quoniam, inquit, plus tribuis veteri, quam novae legi, Leuitis, quam nostris sacerdotibus, nostra atque Dei sit super te maledictio. Guilielmus. Demiror vos non rectius Paulum intelligere. Multo liberiores atque perfectiores erant Christus & Apostoli, quam erant Leuitici generis sacerdotes. Hieronimus ait (quod idem hausit ex Paulo) quod nostri temporis sacerdotes, vel iterum iudaizant, vel iniuste decimas exigunt: his Mosaicae legis umbris, quid aliud quam Filii Dei negant cum Iudaeis in carne venisse. Archiep. Audistis unquam schisma sicut loqui? Horum haec omnia communis doctrina est. His malitiae suae iaculis, ecclesiae libertatem ubique pessundant. Guiliel. Qualem quaeso, libertatem, ex his, Ecclesiae afstruere poteritis, cum nec Christus, nec Apostoli decimas suscepe-rint? Imo magnum Ecclesiae scandalum haec inurunt potius, & libertatem obruunt, ex nimia adeo sacerdotum auaricia. Archiep. Cur tu, cum confoederatis commilitonibus, tam strictas scripturae & doctorum sententias, perinde aduersus laicos, atque sacerdotes non adducis? Guiliel. In sacris concionibus nullus est penes nos personarum respectus, sed suum cuique officium demonstramus vitaeque vitia conuellimus. Incipimus tamen a sacerdotibus, quos uulgi stomachum Chrisostomus appellat cum in illis maiora vitia dominari coperimus. Quippe ambitione, auaritia, voluptate, liuore, atque id genus vitiis nullum non populi statum, ac ordinem depurant, quin & iustam super omnes Dei vindictam provocant, dum
units.tr: "And so why should we wonder if men detract these things from them, especially since they see that they are in some way sharers in the crimes of those whose largesse they abuse for every wickedness?" Archbishop: "You will never make a crime of it, you who despise your spiritual mother in this way. With what shame are you not ashamed to speak like this before the untaught common folk? Are not tithes, I ask you, necessary for priests' sustenance?" William: "As Paul is a trustworthy authority, in the old law tithes were owed only to the priests of the Levitical tribe. But Christ's priests, since they are of the tribe of Judah and not of Levi, tithes by no means pertain to them by God's promise. Therefore, since the priesthood has been changed, the law must necessarily be changed as well, so that we ought now to imitate not Moses but Christ and the apostles, our priests. Nor is it fitting for the disciple to be superior to his lord, but rather he should conduct himself as simple, modest, gentle and patient, following the teacher's example." The archbishop, however, frenzied with bile, said: "Since you grant more to the old law, to the Levites, than to the new law, to our priests, may the curse of God and of us be upon you." William: "I marvel that you do not understand Paul more rightly. Christ and the apostles were far freer and more perfect than the priests of Levitical stock. Jerome says (which he also drew from Paul) that the priests of our time either judaize again or unjustly exact tithes. By these shadows of the Mosaic law, what else do they deny but that the Son of God came in the flesh together with the Jews?" Archbishop: "Have you ever heard a schismatic speak like this? All these things are the common teaching of these men. With these darts of their malice they everywhere overthrow the liberty of the Church." William: "What kind of liberty, I ask, can you claim for the Church from these things, since neither Christ nor the apostles received tithes? Rather these men inflict a great scandal on the Church and crush its liberty, out of the excessive avarice of the priests." Archbishop: "Why do you not, with your confederate fellow soldiers, bring forward such strict sayings of Scripture and the doctors as much against laymen as against priests?" William: "In our sacred sermons there is no respect of persons among us; we set out to each his own duty and uproot the vices of life. Yet we begin with the priests, whom Chrysostom calls the stomach of the people, since we have begun to see greater vices ruling in them. For indeed by ambition, avarice, pleasure, envy and vices of that kind they corrupt the whole condition and order of the people, and even provoke God's just vengeance upon all, while"

units.la: Sacerdotes uulgi stomachus ... nunc uetus ... sed {d}dum talia passi mapud eos designa-ri impune sustinent. Archiep. Su-perbos illos iudicas, qui tibi dissimi-les, honestis incedunt indumentis. Profecto longe teipso attrito, & sor-dido, mitiores sunt, qui cocco pur-purati, ac holosericí, bombycinis a-miculis obambulant, sed age modo quibus tandem iudiciis sacerdotem nosti superbum? Guliel. Ex Christi & Apostolorum suorum contem-ptu. Hi enim abdicatis mundi, car-nisq; illecebris, spiritu pauperes e-rant. Isti honores, diuitias, & uolu-ptates omni uel ambitione cõsectan-tur, uel contentione etiam quadoq; extorquent: Ad hæc spiritualia uen-dentes, & nundinantes, cum Iuda & Simone cuncta in tēplis propha-nant. Archiep. Si scires sacerdotem omnibus his deditum uiciis, aut ui-deres cum meretricula consuetudi-nem habere, iudicares eum ex hoc damnatum? Dico tibi quod in ui-ctu cuoculi posit talis iuste poenitere. Guiliel. Neminem damno, uerun-tamen malum uidetur resipiscentiae signum, ubi sic peccans praesbiter nullam publice quoque poenitudinem praeseferat. Sed maior illorum pars non semel atque iterum, sed ad mortem usque flagitia flagitiis cumulant. Tales arbitror peccare peccatum ad mortem, pro quibus non est orandum censet Ioannes. Tum assurgens clericus in hunc modum Archiepiscopum affatus est. Domine cum eo reticendum censeo, quia quo magis interrogas, hoc uidetur praefractior, magisque nidum proprium conspurcans. Rursusque clerico Archiepiscopus. Quiesce paululum, quippe unum quiddam adhuc superest interrogandum.
units.tr: The priests are the stomach of the common people... now old... but while they suffer such things to be marked out among them with impunity. Archbishop: You judge those proud men who go about in honest clothing, unlike you? Surely those who strut in scarlet and silk, clad in cotton, are far milder than you, worn and shabby as you are. But tell me, by what judgements do you know a priest to be proud? William: By his contempt for Christ and his apostles. For they, having renounced the world and the allurements of the flesh, were poor in spirit. These men pursue honours, riches and pleasures, either with every kind of ambition or sometimes by extorting them through contention. Moreover, selling and trading in spiritual things, they profane everything in the temples, like Judas and Simon. Archbishop: If you knew that a priest was given over to all these vices, or saw him keeping company with a little harlot, would you judge him condemned for this? I tell you, such a man can justly be punished in the cook's own kitchen. William: I condemn no one, but it seems a sign of repentance when a priest who sins in this way shows no public penitence either. Yet most of them do not sin once or twice, but heap crime upon crime even to death. I judge such men to commit the sin unto death, for which John says we should not pray. Then a clerk rose and addressed the Archbishop in this manner: "My lord, I think it best to keep silent about him, for the more you question him, the more stubborn he seems, and the more he fouls his own nest." And again the Archbishop said to the clerk: "Be quiet a little, for one thing still remains to be asked."

units.la: Postremo, inquit, hic aduersum te relatum est, Quod Salopiae praedicaueris, nullo pacto iurare licitum esse. Guil. Istuc nunquam ego uel sensi, uel dia-
units.tr: Lastly, he said, it has been reported against you that at Shrewsbury you preached that it is in no way lawful to swear. William: I never either thought or said that...

units.la: An iurare licitum sit Christiano dixi, Sed autoritate adductus tum Euangelij, tum Diui Iacobi, pariterq; illustribus Doctorum testimonijs, id dixi non licere per creaturas (ut solent) iurare. praedicabam quoque ijsdem aliisq; munitus testibus, nequaquam omnino iurandum, si exposita apud legitimum iudicem veritas aliter possit enodari. Sin minus licebit, docui testificādam fideli iuramento veritatem, sub Dei solius nomine, quū ipse sit solus perpetua veritas. Clericus. Quid ais, An subdito licitum sit, ad praelati sui iussio-nem reductis poplitibus, tactoque Euangelico libro, in hanc sententiam codicem exosculari? Ita me iuuet Deus, & hoc sacrosanctum eius Euangelium, &c. Quoniam qui fideli-is est subditus, ultro praestabit, quic-quid praelatus iusserit. Guiliel.
