If any ecclesiastical controversy arises anywhere, or a question is raised about the doubtful sense of Scripture, the matter in dispute is at once turned into a court. Minds have lost their freedom. The schools are changed in a second way, where it is not looked at which side wins, but which side lives. The lictor sits in place of the opponent, and the sword is drawn in place of the pen, which often falls not on the worse man but on the weaker. But what freedom can there be in stating opinions here, when the death of the other party hangs before the eyes of one, and when, though a man is conquered by reason, power still conquers? We Christians of these times have departed immeasurably far from the footprints of the ancient Church. What age was ever more fertile of heresies than the one in which Jerome lived, not to mention here how gravely the Church laboured over weightier doctrines! Yet men were not driven to such severity of judgement if they dissented from the rest, and indeed there was no need. By books, errors were brought forth and tested, and in them the silent reader might pass judgement on what was consistent on each side and what was otherwise. How often does Jerome, in his writings, his letters and his apologies, challenge his opponents as if to the arena, on fair and open ground, neither robbing himself of freedom nor taking it from others? "I do not want," he says, "that man or this man to answer me, who can overwhelm me by power but cannot teach." And he prevailed no less by this method in exposing the dangers of opinions, indeed far more happily, both satisfying those who were contending and strengthening the others if they wavered. How little did Helvidius, Jovinian and Pelagius achieve with their opinions, once Jerome's books, polished with such brilliance, had come forth and been read! When a heresy had spread so widely, did it not at once fall silent, as if its voice had been taken away, once Augustine had come forward on the stage or Jerome had thundered in the churches, in books no less formidable than any judge in the forum? But now we have lost these literary contests, or, to speak more truly, we have lost among the Church's leaders men like Augustine and Jerome, who know how to contend with style and eloquence. In their place has followed a posterity of such a kind that it mostly defends what it cannot judge, and, since it may not deal with books, attacks the matter with bare power. Yet we must speak in the unlearned law of these men, whether the learned wish it or not, or else learn to be silent at the risk of Pecock. For how do they attack him? Do they overcome him with books, after the example of their elders? Do they confound him with eloquence, pierce him with style, prick him with arguments, and [ἐπισομίζωσι] overwhelm him with wit and judgement? Do they, as Jerome says, bring the hiding places of error into the open, foot to foot, and, once they are brought out, refute them, and wrest victory from a man however much he resists? Finally, do they impose silence upon him, or rather a blush, binding him so tightly on every side with the reins of argument that he not only dares not gasp against them but cannot do so even if he most wishes to? Yet with such weapons one ought to proceed in a case like this, if they were learned men. If they are not learned, why are they put in charge of handling the controversies of the Church, why is judgement on colours committed to the blind? If what Pecock maintained was false, there was no danger that he could not easily be driven from the stage, if some learned craftsman had met him with suitable arguments, one who could have made the goodness of the cause superior through the skill of learning and the force of the Scriptures, as the errors of earlier times were usually plucked up. But now one can only conclude the following. Either these men lacked learned and capable champions of the truth, who could match them in the conduct of the business, or they thought their own cause weak and suspect, one in which they did not dare to risk themselves in a fair freedom of combat, but fled to judgements as to a single citadel, where it is easy, not by sharpness, not by books, but by fear and authority, to crush even the most learned and eloquent men in a little dust. Pecock, therefore, dragged before judges and presidents, though he labours to no avail, nevertheless does many things worthy of an outstanding theologian, and arms himself with every weapon to defend his cause and his life alike. On the other side, his opponents strive with equal sweat, according to their dignity and gain, and do so more eagerly now that a new adversary has been set against them, whose authority, the higher it stood in the Church, the more it seemed destined to bring a heavier collapse of their tyranny before the people. Fearing this, they, as if reduced to the last line of veterans, thought that every kind of equipment must be used and that their strength must be deployed to the utmost. Exquisite wits are summoned, sophists, philosophers, theologians, orators. Nor are the lawyers and the centurions of the decretists lacking, whose use in such matters is very great. The matter is first tried in private conversations; then the frightening form of a judgement is set up, and they threaten the man, present before them, with death in every form. To these terrors are added threats of words, exhortations and remonstrances. Frequently there are also the enticing flatteries of promises, like poisoned cups smeared with Circe's witchcraft. In short, no stone is left unturned. They beg, move, wear down, demand, entreat, threaten, promise, flatter, and in addition they grant time for deliberation and for returning to their senses, in which a delay of death might make life sweeter. They bid him consult his own interest in good time, and assure him that there is still plenty of hope of life and of dignity too, if he will renounce these opinions. In a word, the bewitching tongues never cease to push, persuade and beg, until at last Pecock, overcome by the bishops, gives way, and the bishops' spirit is satisfied. At once a palinode, forced upon him by the bishops, is prepared for him to sing to the people; yet even in singing it, he was nevertheless led back into prison, from which he could not be released except by a final death.

units.la: EXEMPLAR EPISTOLAE CITATORIAE, ab Archiepiscopo Cantaur. ad provinciales ministros conscriptae, in qua Episcopum Pecokum, & aduersarios provocat ad comparendum.
units.tr: Copy of the Letter of Citation, drawn up by the Archbishop of Canterbury for the provincial ministers, in which he summons Bishop Pecock and his opponents to appear.

units.la: THOMAS, PERMISSIONE DIVINA, Cantuariensis Archiepiscopus, totius Angliae primas, & Apostolicae sedis legatus, universis & singulis rectoribus, vicariis, capellanis, curatis, & non curatis, clericis, ac litteratis quibuscunque per nostram provinciam Cantuariensem ubilibet constitutis, Salutem, gratiam, & benedictionem. Querelam, venerabilis confratris nostri Reginaldi, Dei gratia, Cicestrensis episcopi, grauem recepimus continentem, quod licet idem venerabilis confrater noster episcopus, quosdam libros in anglicis, per ipsum nuperscriptos, nobis exhibuerit, per nos & nostra autoritate examinandos, corrigedos, reformandos, & approbandos: Nonnulli tamen (huiusmodi negotio examinationis & reformationis, librorum praedictorum, coram nobis pendente in discussio) apud crucem sancti Pauli Londini, & in aliis diversis, nostrae provinciae Cantuariensis, publice assferuerunt, & publicaverunt, quod idem confrater noster episcopus dicta dixit, fecit, & scripsit, seu scribi fecit in libris praedictis, quasdam conclusiones orthodoxae fidei repugnantes, et contrarias, ac pertinaciter tenuit, & defendebat. Quarum assertionis, & praedicationis praetextu status, & bona fama, eiusdem Domini Reginal di episcopi, enormiter laeduntur, ac ipse, & eius opinio grauantur in immensum. Vobis igitur communiter & diuisim committimus, & mandamus firmiter iniungentes, publice, & in genere moueatis, seu moueri faciatis omnes, & singulos qui quicquam contra conclusiones praedicti reuerendi confratris nostri episcopi, in ipsius libris, huiusmodi, ceu scriptu-ris habitas, ceu contentas, opponere uoluerint uicesimo die, post monitionem huiusmodi, eis in hac parte, factam, libere copareant coram nobis, aut nostris, in hac parte, commissariis, ubicunque in nostris, ciuitate dioecesi, aut prouincia Catuariensi, tunc fuerimus, quicquid hereticum ceu erroneum contra conclusiones huiusmodi, in libris praedictis, dicere, proponere, ceu opponere uoluerint in scriptis sufficienter, & plene proposituri, dicturi, & allegaturi, facturi & recepturi quod est iustum, & sacris in hac parte, conuenit institutis. Et quia, negotio hoc pendente indeterminato, & indiscusso, nihil debet attentari, ceu innouari: uobis mandamus quatenus uniuersis, & singulis sic praedicantibus & assereti-bus autoritate nostra inhibeatis. Quibus nos etiam tenore praesentium, sic inhibemus, ne (pendentia
units.tr: THOMAS, by divine permission Archbishop of Canterbury, primate of all England and legate of the Apostolic See, to all and each of the rectors, vicars, chaplains, curates and non-curates, clerks and literate persons of whatever kind, established anywhere in our province of Canterbury, greeting, grace and blessing. We have received a grave complaint from our venerable brother Reginald, by the grace of God bishop of Chichester, that although the same venerable brother, our bishop, has submitted to us certain books in English, recently written by him, to be examined, corrected, reformed and approved by us and under our authority, nevertheless some persons, while the examination and reform of the aforesaid books is pending before us, have publicly asserted and published at St Paul's Cross in London and in various other places of our province of Canterbury that our said brother the bishop said, did and wrote, or caused to be written, in the aforesaid books certain conclusions repugnant and contrary to the orthodox faith, and that he obstinately held and defended them. By the pretext of these assertions and preaching, the status and good name of the said Lord Reginald, bishop, are grievously harmed, and he and his opinion are burdened beyond measure. We therefore commit to you, jointly and severally, and firmly enjoin and command you to publicly and generally move, or cause to be moved, all and each of those who wish to oppose anything against the conclusions of our aforesaid reverend brother the bishop, as they are held and contained in his books of this kind, that within twenty days after the monition made to them in this matter, they freely appear before us, or our commissaries in this matter, wherever we shall be in our city, diocese or province of Canterbury, to propose, state and allege in writing, fully and sufficiently, whatever they wish to say, propose or oppose as heretical or erroneous against the conclusions in the aforesaid books, and to do and receive what is just and agreeable to the sacred institutions in this matter. And because, while this business is undetermined and undiscussed, nothing ought to be attempted or innovated, we command you to inhibit, on our authority, all and each of those who so preach and assert. We also by the tenor of these presents so inhibit them, that they presume in no way to assert, judge or preach outside of judgment anything to the prejudice or scandal of the aforesaid Lord Reginald, bishop, while the commission of examination and discussion of the books of this kind is pending before us or our commissaries.

units.la: Z te examinationis, & discussionis commissione dominus librorum huiusmodi negotio coram nobis, aut commissa rijs nostris in discusso) quicquam in præiudicium seu scandalum prædicti domini Reginaldi episcopi, extra iudicium afferere, iudicare, seu prædicare, præsumant aliquo modo. Et si quos in hac parte contradictores, reclamantes, seu inhibitionis nostræ non parentes, inuenetitis, citetis, ceu citari faciatis peremptorie eosdem, quod compareant coram nobis, aut nostris in hac parte commissariis, decimo die post citationem, eis, in hac parte factam, si iuridicus fuerit, alioqui proximo die iuridico sequente, ubicunque in nostra ciuitate, dioecesi, aut provincia Cantuariensi tunc fuerimus, causam contradictionis, ceu reclamationis huiusmodi, in forma iuris, proposituri, facturi ulterius, & recepturi quod iustitia in hac parte te suadebit. Et quid feceritis in praemissis, nos aut commissarios nostros (dictis die & loco) debite certificetis per uestras, seu sic certificet ille, qui nostrum mandatum fuerit executus per suas literas. Datum in manerio nostro Lambeth, uicesimo secundo die mensis Octobris, Anno Domini 1457 & nostrae translationis anno quarto.
units.tr: And if you find any contradictors, objectors, or those not obeying our inhibition in this matter, you shall peremptorily cite them, or cause them to be cited, that they appear before us, or our commissaries in this matter, on the tenth day after the citation made to them in this matter, if that day be a juridical day, otherwise on the next juridical day following, wherever we shall then be in our city, diocese or province of Canterbury, to propose the cause of their contradiction or objection of this kind in due form of law, and to do further and receive what justice in this matter shall suggest. And what you have done in the premises you shall duly certify to us or our commissaries, on the said day and at the said place, by your letters; or let him who has executed our mandate certify it by his letters. Given at our manor of Lambeth, on the twenty-second day of October, in the year of the Lord 1457 and the fourth year of our translation.

units.la: FORMVLA RETRACTATIONIS Pecoki episcopi Cistrensis, illi ab episcopis & tyrannis papisticis praescripta, & obstrusa.
units.tr: FORMULA OF RETRACTATION of Reginald Pecock, bishop of Chichester, prescribed and forced upon him by the bishops and papist tyrants.

units.la: IN DEI NOMINE AMEN. CO-ram uobis reuerendissimo, in Christo patre ac D. domino Thoma, Dei gratia, Cantuariae Archiepiscopo, totius Angliae primate, & apostolicae sedis legato. Ego Reginaldus Pecokus indignus Ecclesiae Cistrensis episcopus, pure, sponte, simpliciter, & absolute confiteor, & recognosco, quòd ego retrò actis temporibus, uidelicet per 20 annos proximè præteritos, & amplius, de ecclesiasticis sacramentis, de fidei articulis aliter sensi, tenui, docui, scripsi & dogmatizaui, quàm sacrosancta Romana, & uniuersalis Ecclesia docet, prædicat & obseruat: Necnò contra ueram, catholicam, ac apostolicam fidem, multa & diuersa perniciosa dogmata, libros, codices, opuscula, & scripta, hæreses, & errores, fidei catholicæ, & bonis moribus contrarios, in se continentia, feci, scripsi, ædidi, & publicaui, & præcipuè hæses et errores infra scriptos uidelicet,
units.tr: IN THE NAME OF GOD, AMEN. Before you, the most reverend father in Christ and lord, Thomas, by the grace of God Archbishop of Canterbury, primate of all England, and legate of the apostolic see: I, Reginald Pecock, unworthy bishop of the Church of Chichester, purely, willingly, simply and unconditionally confess and acknowledge that in past times, namely for the last twenty years and more, I have thought, held, taught, written and propagated views on the sacraments of the Church and on the articles of faith that differ from what the most holy Roman and universal Church teaches, preaches and observes. Moreover, against the true, catholic and apostolic faith, I have made, written, published and issued many and various pernicious doctrines, books, codices, pamphlets and writings containing heresies and errors contrary to the catholic faith and to good morals; and especially the heresies and errors written below, namely:

units.la: Inprimis, quòd nò est de necessitate fidei, credere, quòd Dominus noster Iesus Christus, post mortem descendit ad inferos.
units.tr: First, that it is not necessary to faith to believe that our Lord Jesus Christ descended into hell after his death.

units.la: Item quòd non est de necessitate salutis, credere in sanctam Ecclesiam catholicam.
units.tr: Likewise, that it is not necessary to salvation to believe in the holy catholic Church.

units.la: Item quòd non est de necessitate salutis, credere in sanctorum communionem.
units.tr: Likewise, that it is not necessary to salvation to believe in the communion of saints.

units.la: Item quod non est necessarium, ponere corpus materialiter in sacramento.
units.tr: Likewise, that it is not necessary to posit the body materially in the sacrament.

units.la: Ite quòd Ecclesia uniuersalis potest errare in iis, quae sunt fidei.
units.tr: Likewise, that the universal Church can err in those things which belong to faith.

units.la: Item quòd non est de necessitate salutis, credere quod id, quod consilium generale uniuersaliter statuit, approbat, seu determinat in fauorem fidei, & ad salutem animarum, sit ab uniuersis Christi fidelibus approbandum, & tenendum: & contra.
units.tr: Likewise, that it is not necessary to salvation to believe that what a general council universally decrees, approves or determines in favour of the faith and for the salvation of souls must be approved and held by all the faithful of Christ; and the contrary.

units.la: Vnde ego idem Reginaldus miserabilis peccator, qui diu in tenebris ambulaui, nunc ad lucem & semitam ueritatis, Deo misericorditer disponente, reductus, & ad unitatem sanctae matris Ecclesiae rediens, haereses & errores supradictos, &c.
units.tr: Therefore I, the same Reginald, a wretched sinner, who walked for a long time in darkness, now led back by God's merciful disposition to the light and the path of truth, and returning to the unity of our holy mother the Church, renounce the aforesaid heresies and errors, etc.

units.la: Non est, pie lector, quòd credas haec à Pecoko profecta esse, utcunque secus uerba recantationis præsefe-rant. Vetus est artificium, & ludus episcoporum, si quem sibi subegerunt, tanquam bubalum naribus quocunque pertrahunt, uerba tanquam psitaco præformant, quæ loquatur populo non ex uoluntate ipsius, sed ex eorum libidine. Nec dubium est quin huius recantationis episcopum hunc postea pœnitudo cœperit, quod uel hinc facilis æstimandi copia est, quando carcere iterum multatus, ac captiuus detinebatur, in quo, nec scio an occulta tyrannide abipsis oppressus martyrij τῷ ἀπολογισμῷ assecutus sit.
units.tr: Do not believe, kind reader, that these things came from Pecock, however much the words of the recantation may appear otherwise. It is an old trick and game of bishops: whomever they have subdued, like an ox they lead wherever they wish by the nose, and they shape his words like a parrot, so that he speaks to the people not by his own will but by their lust. Nor is there doubt that this bishop later repented of his recantation, which can easily be gathered from this, that when he was again punished and held captive in prison, I do not know whether he was, by some hidden tyranny of theirs, oppressed and obtained the crown of martyrdom [τῷ ἀπολογισμῷ] by his apology.

units.la: DE QVODAM CANDENSI exustō, ex Fauentino.
units.tr: OF A CERTAIN MAN OF CANDIA, burnt, from Faventinus.

units.la: FAuentinus capite decimo mentionem reliquit cuiusdam, qui uxoris, ducis Candiæ cognatus fuerat. Is per Petrum Thomasium, Romanæ sedis legatus, condemnatur hæreseos, flammisque exponitur, abiuraniurantibus suis complicibus. Idem Thomasius in Candia, ossa iam tumulata, alterius ob haeresim exhumari praecepit, ac amburi. O fortunatam, natam hoc iudice Romam.
units.tr: FAVENTINUS, in chapter ten, left a record of a certain man who was a kinsman of the wife of the duke of Candia. He was condemned for heresy by Peter Thomas, legate of the Roman see, and was given to the flames, his accomplices abjuring under oath. The same Thomas, in Candia, ordered the bones of another man, already buried, to be dug up for heresy and burnt. O fortunate Rome, born under such a judge!

units.la: PETRVS IOANNES Aquitanus.
units.tr: PETER JOHN OF AQUITAINE.

units.la: MEminit etiā Guido Perpinianensis, cuiusdam Petri Ioannis Aquitani, ac Franciscani, in cuius cadauer, iā diu demortui, similiter desaeuitum est per Clementē quartū, ann. 1260 quod in eius scriptis, nescio quid siniστri uaticinij repertum sit, futuram Romanā ecclesiam magnam meretricem, Babylonem, bestiam carnalem, papam mysticū futurum Antichristum, quodcp nouissimis temporibus, lex appareret libertatis. Nō ita opinor Dauid conuiciatorē suū uindicabat in scriptu-ris, quo tempore nimis petulanter a maledico Semei impetitus, lōgē for tasse iustiorē habebat ulciscē di causam. Nihil enim in hoc fuerat, nisi spiritus malitię mendax. Vtinam perinde fuisset alter uanus. Non seruamus hic annorum seriem, sed quia uir bonus hic erat, & utilis Ecclesię monendæ minister, non putaui nomen illius obliuione prætereundum in Ecclesia Dei. Plurimum enim referre arbitror, ut fideles intelligant in densissimis his temporum & errorum tenebris, ubi uera illa series, & occultæ quasi uenæ, dominici templi, delitescât. Nihil enim magis fallit Christianos, quam quod externa specie seducti plurimi, uerâ Ecclesiæ imaginem ac serie non considerant, nec intelligunt. Semper enim uulgus multitudinem fere sequitur, & externam hanc uocationem. Internam Dei uoluntatem, & occultam Ecclesiæ conseruationem in mundo, perpauci animaduertunt. Quo fit ut facillimus sit erroris lapsus, ni maior in iudicando diligentia adhibeatur.
units.tr: Guy of Perpignan also mentions a certain Peter John of Aquitaine, a Franciscan, on whose corpse, long since dead, cruelty was likewise inflicted by Clement IV in the year 1260, because in his writings some sinister prophecy was found, I know not what, that the future Roman church would be the great harlot, Babylon, the carnal beast; that the pope would be the future mystical Antichrist; and that in the last times the law of liberty would appear. I do not think David, in the Scriptures, avenged his reviler in this way, when he was too insolently assailed by the cursing Shimei, although he perhaps had a far juster cause for vengeance. For there was nothing in this but a lying spirit of malice. Would that the other had been as empty! I do not keep here the sequence of years, but because this man was a good one, and a useful minister for admonishing the Church, I did not think his name should be passed over in oblivion in the Church of God. For I judge it matters greatly that the faithful understand, in these very dense darkness of times and errors, where that true succession lies hidden, as if in secret veins of the Lord's temple. For nothing deceives Christians more than that most people, seduced by an external appearance, do not consider or understand the true image and succession of the Church. The crowd almost always follows the multitude and this outward calling; very few notice the inner will of God and the hidden preservation of the Church in the world. Hence it comes that the fall into error is very easy, unless greater diligence is applied in judging.

units.la: Petrus
units.tr: Peter

units.la: SVbit hic memoria Petri Olerij, cuius aetas ad superiora tempora pertinebat, Quanquam neutiquam hic a nobis praeterietur. Is (ut ferunt annales,) in ciuitate Barchinona cum Durando Gundensi, Guilielmo Gilberto, & Valentino, tempore Ioannis 22. hoc est, an. 1336. condemnatis eius articulis, ipse quoq; condemnatus est. Bernard. lib. 5.
units.tr: Here the memory of Peter Olerius comes to mind, whose age belonged to earlier times; yet by no means shall he be passed over by us here. He (as the annals report) was condemned in the city of Barcelona together with Durandus of Girona, William Gilbert and Valentinus, when his articles were condemned in the time of John XXII, that is, in the year 1336; he too was condemned. Bernard, book 5.

units.la: DVO MINORITAE.
units.tr: Two Minorites.

units.la: ADhęc tempora accedunt etiam duo Minoritae in quos ignis supplicio animaduersum est. anno 1354. feria 5. in hebdomada Pentecostes, apud Curiam Aniuionensem pro opinionibus nescio quibus, certe ut Papae ac Cardinalibus uidebatur haereticis. Ranulph. Cestrensis.
units.tr: Next to these times belong also two Minorite friars, who were burned at the stake in the year 1354, on the Thursday of Pentecost week, at the papal court at Avignon, for I know not what opinions, certainly heretical as the Pope and the cardinals judged them. Ranulph of Chester.

units.la: IOANNES DE VVESALIA.
units.tr: JOHN OF WESEL.

units.la: ANno 1479. Ioannes de Vue- ZV falia superiori, Germanus doctor, & ecclesiastes Vuormacensis, uir singulari eruditionis commendatione celebris, nec tam ingenio excultus, quàm uita undiquaque integer, nō paucas exagitationes Christi nomine à sophistis sustinuit, tandē è Gerardo Elteno, Iacobo Sprenger, cæterisq; Dominicanæ factionis doctorculis, hæresεos insimulatus, condemnationis censuræ, ac supplicio succumbit uenerandus se nex, quòd opinor, diceret Papam, episcopos, & sacerdotes haud quicquam ad salutem conferre. Cuius libri Moguntiæ in foro publico concremati sunt.
units.tr: In the year 1479 John of Wesel, the Upper, a German teacher and preacher at Worms, a man famous for his singular commendation of learning, and polished not so much in talent as wholly upright in life, endured no small harassment for Christ's name from the sophists. At length, accused of heresy by Gerard Elten, Jacob Sprenger and the other little teachers of the Dominican faction, he succumbed to the censure of condemnation and to punishment, the venerable man dying; because, I suppose, he said that the Pope, bishops and priests contributed nothing whatever to salvation. His books were burned in the public square at Mainz.

units.la: MATER DOMINAE YONGE.
units.tr: MOTHER OF LADY YONGE.

units.la: ATque ne non omnes pāriter sexum inuolueret hæc persequendi rabies, neu omnes crudelitatis numeros satis absoluueret, quasi parum hactenus effet tantam uirorum rum cędem edidisse, in mulieres iam grassari ceptum est, quarum cum aliae complures extiterūt, Christum sponsum per crucem, ac mortem sequutae, tum una commemoratur, uirtute, ac cōstantia cum primis laudata mulier, quę mater est dicta Dominę cuiusdam cognomēto Yong. Ea propter hæresim apud Anglos exusta est, Anno 1490.
units.tr: And lest this rage of persecution should not equally embrace both sexes, nor sufficiently complete the full tally of cruelty, as if it had hitherto been too little to have carried out so great a slaughter of men, it began to rage against women as well. Of these, while many others appeared who followed Christ their spouse through the cross and death, one is recorded who was praised above all for her virtue and constancy: a woman who is called the mother of a certain lady surnamed Yonge. For this reason she was burned for heresy among the English, in the year 1490.

units.la: IOANNES BALLVS SACERDOS.
units.tr: JOHN BALL, PRIEST.

units.la: IOannes Ballus sacerdos ob Euangelij prędicationem Londini incarceratus, per Symonem Archiepiscopum Cantuariensem, et Guilielmū episcopū Londinensem, anno 1381. à communi plebe liberatur à vinculis, interfecto Archiepiscopo, cum duobus aliis sacerdotū principibus. Deinceps per Angliā peragratus, & uaticinia ædens, per Robertum Treuilianum Couentrię captus adiucatur suspendio, anno
units.tr: John Ball, a priest, was imprisoned in London for preaching the Gospel by Simon, Archbishop of Canterbury, and William, Bishop of London. In 1381 the common people freed him from his chains, and the archbishop was killed along with two other chief priests. Afterwards Ball travelled through England, uttering prophecies. He was captured at Coventry by Robert Tresilian and condemned to hanging in

units.la: 1382 1582. apud S. Albanum. Moxque idem Treuilianus summus iusticiarius eadem pertulit tiburno suspensus iusta Dei retaliatione.
units.tr: 1382, at St Albans. Soon afterwards the same Tresilian, the chief justiciar, suffered the same fate, hanged at Tyburn, by the just retribution of God.

units.la: NICOLAUS QVIDAM ITALVS.
units.tr: NICHOLAS, A CERTAIN ITALIAN.

units.la: AD haec tempora pertinet & Nicolaus quidam de Luca Doctor Italus, Carmelita, de quo apud Theodoricum de schismate lib.3. sic accipimus, quod in vincula, ob veritatis enarrationem coiectus sit per Gregorium 12. ac perpetua predicatione interdictus. Quae criminis illius actio fuerit certum non succurrit, uerum id unum certissimum est, non posse malum esse illum, quisquis Romano pontifici displiceat. Etsi non eiusdem temporis, eiusdem tamen supplicij particeps erat Thomas quidam Dominicanus Anglus, de quo ita proditum est apud Masseum, Quod papae Ioanni resti terit, eoque carceribus intrusus, satis acer-
units.tr: To this period also belongs Nicholas of Lucca, an Italian teacher and Carmelite, of whom we learn from Theodoric's On the Schism, book 3, that he was cast into chains by Gregory XII for proclaiming the truth, and was forbidden to preach for the rest of his life. I do not clearly recall what the nature of his offence was. The one thing most certain is that whoever displeases the Roman pontiff cannot be in the right. Although not from the same time, a certain English Dominican, Thomas, shared the same kind of punishment. Massaeus reports of him that, because he had reviled Pope John, he was thrown into prison and afflicted with rather severe

units.la: Ann. 1408. acerbis supplicijs plectitur. Causam ita exprimit Masseus, quod assereret animas separatas Deum non uidere in perfecta gloria, ante diem iudicij, fortassis uisum est hoc pontifici, derogare nescio quid adorationi Sanctorum. Huc etiam referendum est quod apud Antoninum legimus de compluribus discipulis Almerici Lutetiae degradatis & exustis, partim quod coniugati essent, partim quod Sacramenta signa esse diceret, haec ex Antonino.
units.tr: In 1408 he was punished with harsh torments. Massaeus gives the cause: he asserted that the souls of the departed do not see God in perfect glory before the day of judgement. Perhaps this seemed to the pontiff to detract somewhat from the worship of the saints. To this should also be referred what we read in Antoninus about several disciples of Amalric who were degraded and burned at Paris, partly because they were married and partly because they said that the sacraments are mere signs. So far Antoninus.

units.la: Posset huic farragini attexere mentionem Philippi Noris Hybernini, cuius supra nomen perfunctorie attigimus. Hic etsi exustus non est, tamen papistarum rabiem maiorem in modum sustinuit, quippe qui me dicantibus infestissimus hostis, ubique in concionibus, lectionibus, (erat enim Oxoniae professor artium) eos uoraces, porcos, fures, lupos, tyrannos, haereticos, antichristos, ac diabolos diabolo peiores appellare consue-uit,item Gabionitas hypocritas,qui Iosue dederunt uerba. Qua de causa accusatus, prouocans ad consilium generale,noluit Rom. Pontificis iudicio stare. Postea diu multumqʒ uexatus,tandem excommunicatus, & suspensus est ab omni gradu, quoad ingenti pecuniarum summa papae ministris persoluta, sese in libertatem asseruit.
units.tr: I could add to this medley a mention of Philip Norris of Ireland, whose name I touched on briefly above. Although he was not burned, he endured the rage of the Papists to an extraordinary degree. He was a most hostile enemy of those who were called Wycliffites, and everywhere in his sermons and lectures (for he was a professor of arts at Oxford) he was accustomed to call them gluttons, swine, thieves, wolves, tyrants, heretics, antichrists, and devils worse than the devil, and likewise Gibeonite hypocrites who deceived Joshua. For this he was accused. Appealing to a general council, he refused to abide by the judgement of the Roman pontiff. Afterwards, long and much harassed, he was at last excommunicated and suspended from every rank, until, after a huge sum of money had been paid to the pope's ministers, he won his liberty.

units.la: ROGERVS ACTONVS MILES.
units.tr: Roger Acton, Knight.

units.la: S Ancto huic martyrum innocentissimorum catalogo accedit Rogerus Actonus miles, qui in capo di ui Aegidij Lodini exustus est, cum triginta octo aliis, an. 1413 mense Ian. Autore Fabiano in cronicis. Quae fuerat illius causa, aut illorum nomina, fusiori fortassis tractatione explicare, nisi calamitosum hoc exilium nostrum, procul a patria semotos, ab omni librorum copia, ac pera peruestigandi facultate excluderet; Quod si (comiserante Christi gratia) posthac contingat eo reducinos ubi certa istarum rerum notitia recolligi poterit, non senties, lector amice, officium nostrum ac inuestigandi laborem defuturum.
units.tr: To this holy catalogue of the most innocent martyrs is added Sir Roger Acton, who was burned in the field of St Giles at Lodini, together with thirty-eight others, in January 1413, as Fabian reports in his chronicles. I might perhaps explain the cause of his case, or the names of the others, in a fuller treatment, if this wretched exile of ours, kept far from my country and cut off from every supply of books and from any means of thorough investigation, did not prevent it. But if, by the merciful grace of Christ, I should later come to a place where certain knowledge of these matters can be gathered, you will not, friendly reader, find my diligence and labour in searching them out lacking.

units.la: ROGERVS ONLAEVS MILES.
units.tr: Roger Oldcastle, Knight.

units.la: DE Rogero Onleo traditum a quibusdam, hoc tantum accepimus pro veritate hunc strangulatum esse, anno Domini 1441. Nec praeteriemus Aleonoram Cobhamam, etsi nihil aliud compertum de illa ad nos peruenit quam haereseos causa, i. ueritatis studio, a papistis in Monam esse relegatam, iuxta Hardyngum & Fabianum.
units.tr: Of Roger Oldcastle, what some have related we have received only as this for certain: that he was strangled in the year of the Lord 1441. Nor shall we pass over Eleanor Cobham, although nothing else concerning her has come down to us except that, for the cause of heresy, that is, for the pursuit of the truth, she was banished to the Isle of Man by the Papists, according to Hardyng and Fabian.

units.la: HIERONYMVS SAVONAROLA Italus.
units.tr: Hieronymus Savonarola, an Italian.

units.la: ANno 1499. iij. calendas Iunij, Hieronymus Savonarola,
units.tr: In the year 1499, on the third day before the Kalends of June (29 May), Hieronymus Savonarola,

units.la: Italus natione ex sodalitio Dominicanorum, cum quaedam pertentasset, aduersus suae professionis primores, non modicum schisma aduersus eum suscitabant in Italia. Quod non potuit, nisi sua suorumque morte, sedari. A Romano ergo pontifice Alexandro. 6. ut populi concitator, seditiosus, ac potificiae dignitatis conceptor, ad flammas cum duobus sociis adiudicatus, primum laqueo suffocatus, deinde in Florenti no foro comburitur. ex Io. Balaeo.
units.tr: an Italian by birth, of the fellowship of the Dominicans, after he had attempted certain things against the leaders of his own profession, stirred up no small schism against himself in Italy. This could not be calmed except by his death and that of his followers. Therefore by Pope Alexander VI, as a stirrer-up of the people, a seditious man, and a conceiver of an attack on papal dignity, he was condemned to the flames with two companions. He was first strangled with a noose and then burned in the square at Florence. From John Bale.

units.la: ARTICVLI, SIVE APHORISMI aliquot I. Vuicleui sparsim ex uariis illius opusculis excerpti per aduersarios papicolas, ac Concilio Constantiensi exhibiti.
units.tr: Several articles, or aphorisms, of John Wycliffe, scattered through various of his little works, excerpted by the adversaries, the papist worshippers, and presented to the Council of Constance.

units.la: PAPA EST HAERESIARCHA, fundans & autorisans nouos ordines contra Christum. Et mirum foret quod Dominus cooperaretur cum talibus, in dispensationibus friuolis, quas intendunt.
units.tr: The pope is a heresiarch, founding and authorizing new orders against Christ. And it would be a marvel if the Lord cooperated with such men in the frivolous dispensations they intend.

units.la: Papa non dispensat cum symonia, uel uoto temere. temerario, cum ipse sit capitalis symoniacus, uo uens temerarie seruare statum summe damnabi- lem hic in uia.
units.tr: The pope does not dispense with simony or with a rash vow, since he himself is a chief simoniac, rashly vowing to keep here on the way a most damnable state.

units.la: Papa qui se falsè nominat seruum seruorum Dei: sub nullo gradu est in opere Euangelij mun- dano. Et si sit in ordine aliquo, est in ordine dæ- monum, Deo plus culpabiliter seruientium.
units.tr: The pope, who falsely calls himself servant of the servants of God, holds no rank in the worldly work of the Gospel. And if he is in any order, he is in the order of demons, serving God more culpably.

units.la: Papa est ille Antichristus qui in scriptura ex primitur, cum sit specialis procurator Diaboli, procurans per mendacia perditionem animæ con- tra Christum, & sic est patulus Antichristus.
units.tr: The pope is that Antichrist who is depicted in Scripture, since he is a special procurator of the devil, procuring by lies the perdition of souls against Christ; and so he is the manifest Antichrist.

units.la: Papa est patulus Antichristus, non solum il- la simplex persona, sed multitudo paparum, à tempore dotationis Ecclesiæ, cardinalium, epi- scoporum, & suorum complicium aliorum est persona Antichristi compositi monstrosa, non tamen repugno quin Gregorius & alij Papæ qui in uita fecerūt multa bona de genere fructuo- sè finaliter pœnitebant.
units.tr: The pope is the manifest Antichrist. Not only that single person, but the multitude of popes from the time of the endowment of the Church, together with the cardinals, bishops and their other accomplices, is a monstrous composite person of Antichrist. Yet I do not deny that Gregory and other popes, who did many good deeds in their lives, repented at the end of the fruitless kind of works.

units.la: Genus humanum specialiter in Europa per- sunditur, in isto, hæresi nimis cæca, quod opor- tet totam militantem ecclesiam duci per regime Antichristi. De sermone Domini in monte tra- ctatu sec u do cap.38.
units.tr: The human race is especially deluded in Europe, in this heresy, too blind, that the whole militant Church must be led by the rule of Antichrist. From Wycliffe's treatise on the Sermon on the Mount, second treatise, chapter 38.

units.la: Si sit expediens Ecclesiæ militanti quod ca- reret corporali præsentia capitis Iesu Christi, si- in monte,
units.tr: Whether it is expedient for the militant Church to lack the bodily presence of its head, Jesus Christ, on the mount.

units.la: Libellus Vuicleui de sermone Domini in monte cut cōtigit quando Ecclesia post Ascensionē Domini, secundum illud Ioannis. Expedit uobis ut ego uadā, quanto magis prodesset Ecclesiæ quod careret Papa capitaneo, qui nō æquiparatur in uirtutibus Iesu christi. Tunc enim descenderet gratia perpendiculariter in homines ut sunt digni.
units.tr: Wycliffe's booklet on the Sermon on the Mount, which happened when the Church after the Lord's Ascension, according to that passage of John, "It is expedient for you that I go away." How much more would it profit the Church to lack a pope as captain, who is not equal in virtues to Jesus Christ. For then grace would descend perpendicularly upon men, as they are worthy.

units.la: Papa est abhominatio desolationis in abstra-cto, cum ex sua antiqua malicia sit in peruersita te diaboli induratus.
units.tr: The pope is the abomination of desolation in the abstract, since from his ancient malice he is hardened in the perversity of the devil.

units.la: Papa est immediatus uicarius principis huius mundi. Ruinam scelerum ex sua fallacia merito patiatur secundum illud, inimici uero Domini mox ut honorificati, &c.
units.tr: The pope is the immediate vicar of the prince of this world. Let him justly suffer the ruin of his crimes from his own deceit, according to that: "But the enemies of the Lord, as soon as they are exalted," etc.

units.la: Ex isto textu, Expedit uobis ut ego uadā, etc. eliciunt fideles, quod Christus qui promisit fidelibus quod maneret cum ipsis usq; consummatione nem seculi, uoluit perpetuo sine tali uicario in cœlestibus residere, ut couersatione atq; affectione aspirando ad cœlestia colligant suam affectionem in Domino Iesu Christo. De sermone Domini in monte, tractatu secundo capitulo 5i.
units.tr: From this text, "It is expedient for you that I go away," etc., the faithful deduce that Christ, who promised the faithful that he would remain with them until the consummation of the age, willed to dwell perpetually in heaven without such a vicar, so that by conversation and by affection aspiring to heavenly things they might gather their affection in the Lord Jesus Christ. From the Sermon on the Mount, second treatise, chapter 51.

units.la: Petrus & Clemens cum cæteris adiutoribus in fide, nō fuerunt papæ, sed Dei adiutores ad æ-dificandam Ecclesiā Domini nostri Iesu Christi. De sermone Domini in monte tractatu 2. cap. 5i. quæst. secunda.
units.tr: Peter and Clement, with the other helpers in the faith, were not popes, but helpers of God in building the Church of our Lord Jesus Christ. From the Sermon on the Mount, treatise 2, chapter 51, second question.

units.la: Papa et cardinales fuerāt non ordinati à Domino, sed per Diabolū introducti, in cuius signū nome papæ uel cardinalium non inseritur in scri ptura, sed (ut communicantes referunt) quando uenenum effusum est in ecclesia, inuentū est. De ferm. Domini in monte tract. 2. cap. 51. quæst. 2.
units.tr: The popes and cardinals were not ordained by the Lord but introduced by the devil. As a sign of this, the name of pope or cardinal is not inserted in Scripture, but (as informants report) it was discovered when poison was poured out into the Church. From the Sermon on the Mount, treatise 2, chapter 51, question 2.

units.la: Rationi consonat & scripturæ, quod non existente papa aliquo uel cardinali, uel persona aliqua de quatuor sectis, non minus sed (probatur) magis staret Ecclesia militans in fide & uir tutibus quàm stat modo. De sermone Domini in monte tractatu 2. cap. 51. quæst. 3.
units.tr: It agrees with reason and Scripture that, if there were no pope or cardinal, or any person of the four sects, the militant Church would stand no less, indeed (it is proved) more, in faith and virtues than it stands now. From the Sermon on the Mount, treatise 2, chapter 51, question 3.

units.la: Electiones cardinalium cum cæteris humanis traditionibus non sunt dignæ memoria, cum nō sit maior color, quod Deus ipsas conficit, quam sequitur, quod ex sua uesania Deus papam statu⸗ it socium Iesu Christi.
units.tr: The elections of cardinals, like other human traditions, are not worthy of mention, since there is no greater plausibility in saying that God makes them than the consequence that, by his own folly, God appointed the pope as companion of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Licet Papa præcipiat in bullis quod nulli ho minum liceat paginam illam infringere, sed eo ipso quod præsumunt incurrant & c. fideles au⸗ dacter exponunt igni bullas tales tanquam hære ticas contra fidem.
units.tr: Although the pope commands in his bulls that no one of men be permitted to break that page, yet by the very fact that they presume to do so they incur (the penalty), etc. The faithful boldly expose such bulls to the fire as heretical and contrary to the faith.

units.la: Est contra æternum iudicium sanctisanctoⁿ rum, quod talis inhibet refuga. i. papa, taliter po pulo præfiguratur, secundum illud, Quod si sal euanuerit, etc. & multo minus ualet tales bullæ hereticæ quas asportant discoli de nido illo.
units.tr: It is against the eternal judgment of the Holy of Holies that such a refuge, that is, the pope, should forbid it. He is thus prefigured to the people, according to that: "But if the salt have lost its savour," etc. And much less are such heretical bulls worth anything, which the rascals carry away from that nest.

units.la: Consulendum est fidelibus quod nõ petant cu riam Romanam, uel ad Papales indulgetias, uel absolutiones àpœna & à culpa sibi & alijs im-petrandas, quia Dominus totius mundi non uult in tali breui loco et angulo coarctari, sed in cœlo existens perpendiculariter cuilibet uigilanti est paratus, ad lumen suæ gratiæ influendum.
units.tr: The faithful should be advised not to seek the Roman curia, either for papal indulgences or for absolutions from punishment and guilt to be obtained for themselves and others, because the Lord of the whole world does not wish to be confined in such a narrow place and corner. Existing in heaven, he is ready to pour the light of his grace perpendicularly upon anyone who is watchful.

units.la: Ne seducētus populus pedibus talis hypocritæ appropinquet, si enim petitio sua sit rationabilis. Dominus domi infra conscientiā hanc cõcedit. Si autē petitio sit irrationabilis: soret summa de mentia credere quod talis refuga hanc cõcedit.
units.tr: Lest the deceived people approach the feet of such a hypocrite. For if his request is reasonable, the Lord grants it at home, within the conscience. If, however, the request is unreasonable, it would be the height of madness to believe that such a refuge grants it.

units.la: Non est alius locus, quare Roma sit locus aptus ut Papa ibi resideat, nisi ex altera infami starum causarum, primo quod Papa ibi infideliter perdit uitas animarum, sicut Cæsar prius infideliter perdidit uitas ibi corporum, & martyrum Iesu Christi. Secundo quia Cæsar residet in illa uilla qui dotauit Papam contra legē quam Christus suis apostolis ordinauit.
units.tr: There is no other reason why Rome should be a suitable place for the pope to reside, except one of two infamous causes. First, because the pope there faithlessly destroys the lives of souls, just as Caesar earlier faithlessly destroyed there the bodily lives of the martyrs of Jesus Christ. Second, because the emperor, who endowed the pope, resides in that town, contrary to the law which Christ ordained for his apostles.

units.la: Potestates quæ finguntur à Papa & alijs quatuor nouis sectis, sunt ficte, & ad seducendū subditos diabolice introductæ, ut prælatorū Cæsariorum excommunicatio, citatio, incarceratio, & redditus pecuniarum uendicatio.
units.tr: The powers which are feigned by the pope and the other four new sects are fictitious, and diabolically introduced to seduce subjects: such as the excommunication, citation and imprisonment of the prelates of Caesar, and the claiming of money revenues.

units.la: Superiores istarum sectarum fingunt se habere re potestate à Domino, ad subditos taliter puniendos, ut papa fingit se habere potestate ad excö municandum, quà tamè potestate nō plus habet, q diabolus ad maledicendū populo Christiano.
units.tr: The superiors of these sects pretend to have power from the Lord to punish subjects in this way, just as the pope pretends to have power to excommunicate. Yet by that power he has no more than the devil has to curse the Christian people.

units.la: Videtur fidelibus, quod talis ficta potestas prælatorum simul creuit cum haeresi de hostia cō secrata, nam moderni prælati sunt de numero illorum, de quibus dicitur per Prophetam, Maledicam benedictionibus uestris.
units.tr: It seems to the faithful that such feigned power of prelates grew together with the heresy about the consecrated host, for the present prelates are of the number of those of whom the Prophet says, "I will curse your blessings."

units.la: Intendat fidelis rationem scripturæ & fidei, & nō credat talibus extrauagantibus fabulis in fundabilibus de potestate prælatorū, quia benedictio ipsorum est similis benedictioni qua benedicunt hostiæ, & maledictio e contra in benedictionem Domini conuersa est.
units.tr: Let the faithful attend to the reason of Scripture and of faith, and not believe such extravagant fables, founded on nothing, about the power of prelates. Their blessing is like the blessing by which they bless the host, and their curse, on the contrary, has been turned into a blessing of the Lord.

units.la: Priuilegia & libertates quas papa concedit hominibus sunt deliramenta à fidelibus deridenda. In cuius signum populus cui isti maledicunt, benedicitur à Deo, & e contra.
units.tr: The privileges and liberties which the pope grants to men are delusions to be mocked by the faithful. As a sign of this, the people whom these men curse are blessed by God, and conversely.

units.la: Ex dissensione pontificum de Papatu, magnū bonum proueuit, quia iam uisa debilitate Antichristi confortantur fideles publicare sententias multas euangelicas, quas, stante ipso in suo robo Schisma re, differere non auderent. Et si placet Domino seu diuisio iam mouere brachium seculare, ut tepore huius in papatu debilitati Antichristi, nitatur efficaciter redu tere Ecclesia ad ordinatione Domini nostri Iesu Christi, fructus valde notabilis proveniret ex di uisione huius capitis antichristi.
units.tr: From the dissension of the pontiffs over the papacy great good has come forth, because now that the weakness of Antichrist is seen, the faithful are strengthened to publish many evangelical sentences which, while he stood in his full strength, they did not dare to put forth. And if it pleases the Lord that division now stir the secular arm, so that, with the papacy weakened at this time, Antichrist might be effectively struggled against, and the Church brought back to the ordinance of our Lord Jesus Christ, a very notable fruit would come from the division of this head of Antichrist.

units.la: Papa & sui complices sunt scribae et pharisaei, claudentes regnum coelorum, & nec ipsi intrant, nec alios intrare permittunt, et principalis ratio huius est, traditionum, quas edidit Antichristus.
units.tr: The Pope and his accomplices are the scribes and Pharisees, who shut the kingdom of heaven: they do not enter in themselves, and they do not allow others to enter. The chief reason for this is the traditions which Antichrist has put forth.

units.la: Si non in isto textu evangelico. Nemo accendit lucernam &c. non reperi ibi quod anachoritae inclusi in lapidibus vel claustrales, in lege Domini fundarentur, & cum hic non fundatur talis religio, patenter eius oppositu patet, quod non est Christi religio, quam describit Iacobus, sed religio diabolica vel hypocritica, quae ab ipso vana religio nuncupatur.
units.tr: If it is not in this gospel text, "No one lights a lamp, etc.", I have not found there that enclosed anchorites in their cells or cloistered monks are founded in the law of the Lord. And since such a religion is not founded there, its opposite makes it plain that it is not the religion of Christ, which James describes, but a diabolical or hypocritical religion, which James himself calls "vain religion".

units.la: Cum no tantum istae religiones sanctae matris ecclesiae prosunt, quantu prodest casus diaboli, sicut diabolus no debet taliter peccare, sed a peccato huiusmodi continere: sic ordines isti priuati qui non sunt autorizati a Domino non se debent introducere in Ecclesiam militantem.
units.tr: Since these religious orders do no more good to holy mother Church than the fall of the devil did, and the devil ought not to sin in this way but to refrain from such sin, so these private orders, which have not been authorised by the Lord, must not introduce themselves into the militant Church.

units.la: Sicut quaecunque discrasiae in humano corpore prosunt, sic sanctae matris ecclesiae & istae quattuor sectae per diabolum introductae.
units.tr: Just as any dyscrasias in the human body may be of benefit, so these four sects, introduced by the devil, are of benefit to holy mother Church.

units.la: Cum maior malicia in sectis q personis singularibus iudicatur, uidetur Christianu quod secta illæ sunt plus q; personæ simplices reprobandæ, et ideò reprobationes sectales exerceri deberent.
units.tr: Since a greater wickedness is judged in sects than in single persons, it seems to me as a Christian that these sects are more to be condemned than simple persons, and therefore sectarian condemnations ought to be carried out.

units.la: Si per impossibile doceri posset, quod aliquæ illarum quatuor sectarum à Deo sumpserunt originem, tunc de tanto foret color fidelibus sectis de conditione laudabili approbandis, cum autem non sic à Domino sumpserunt originem: christia nis licet ipsas redarguere, quia qui nõ intrat per ostium, fur est & latro.
units.tr: If it could be shown, though it is impossible, that some of those four sects took their origin from God, then there would be some colour for approving those sects of praiseworthy condition. But since they did not take their origin from the Lord, Christians may refute them, because whoever does not enter by the door is a thief and a robber.

units.la: Omnes religiosi moderni seipsos necessitant ut hypocrisi maculentur, ad hoc enim sonat sua perfectio, ut si ieiunent, ut sic se induent, ut sic faciant quicquid differenter ab aliis observant.
units.tr: All modern religious bind themselves to be stained with hypocrisy. For their perfection tends to this: that if they fast, if they clothe themselves in such a way, if they do whatever they observe differently from others.

units.la: Cum fideles debeant ex mandato Dei honora re corpus sanctæ matris ecclesiæ, & istæ quatuor sectæ tanquam quatuor humores inficiunt & mortificant ipsam ecclesiam, omnes fideles debent ipsam ab ipsis humoribus expugnare.
units.tr: Since the faithful ought, by God's command, to honour the body of holy mother Church, and these four sects infect and mortify the Church itself like four humours, all the faithful ought to drive these humours out of her.

units.la: Causa totius mali in Ecclesia militante, est peruersa introductio istorum novorum ordinum contra Christum.
units.tr: The cause of all evil in the militant Church is the perverse introduction of these new orders against Christ.

units.la: Hypocrisis est fundamentum istis quatuor sectis, & ideo sic loquitur Esaias. Et erunt qui beatificant, & qui beatificantur præcipitati, & perdet Dominus ab Israel cauda cum capite, intelligendo per caput Rom. pontificem, & per caudas sectas fratrum.
units.tr: Hypocrisy is the foundation of these four sects, and so Isaiah speaks: "Those who call this people blessed lead them astray, and those who are called blessed are cast down"; and "the Lord will cut off from Israel head and tail together". By the head he means the Roman pontiff, and by the tails the sects of the friars.

units.la: Cum fratres sint alieni à secta Christi: probabile est quod sua merita non plus valent, quàm opera paganorum.
units.tr: Since the friars are alien to the sect of Christ, it is probable that their merits are worth no more than the works of pagans.

units.la: Globus fratrum sicut non habet fundamentu à Domino, sed ei opponitur, sic trahit fratres ad poenam non modicam.
units.tr: The whole body of friars, just as it has no foundation from the Lord but is opposed to him, so it draws the friars to no small punishment.

units.la: Sectæ fratrum non fundantur ex lege Domini, sed ascendut aliunde tanquā fures et latrones.
units.tr: The sects of the friars are not founded on the law of the Lord, but climb in from elsewhere like thieves and robbers.

units.la: Diabolus nō solū defraudat simplices, per hos fratres, sed per sectas infundabiliter introductas ut sunt monachi, canonici cū Cæsario clero, qui auferūt dominia, quæ haberet domini seculares.
units.tr: The devil deceives not only simple folk, through these friars, but also through sects introduced without foundation, such as the monks and canons with the Caesarean clergy, who take away the lordships which secular lords would otherwise have.

units.la: Introducentes & suo perpetuo desponsantes novas sectas, nimis ingratè recusant sectam libe-ram Iesu Christi, innuentes ipsi quòd ipsa ex im-perfectione sui autoris fuerat completa.
units.tr: Those who introduce new sects and betroth themselves to them for ever most ungratefully refuse the free sect of Jesus Christ, implying that it was completed by the imperfection of its author.

units.la: Intrantes novas sectas, de hoc non poenitent, sed lætantur usq; ad mortem cum male fecerint, & hæc ratio quare tam sæpe inueximus contra eos, ut de hæresi resipiscant, & ad meliorem se-ctam redeant Iesu Christi.
units.tr: Those who enter new sects do not repent of it, but rejoice until death even when they have done evil. This is the reason why we have so often inveighed against them: that they may repent of their heresy and return to the better sect of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Damnabilis esse videtur cōsecratio istarū quā-tuor sectarū, qua peruertūtur fideles de simpli-ci secta Christi ad sectam friuolam Antichristi.
units.tr: The consecration of these four sects seems damnable, by which the faithful are perverted from the simple sect of Christ to the frivolous sect of Antichrist.

units.la: Saraceni sunt graviter increpādi ex hoc quòd non tollunt iugum Christi super se, sed ambulant per sectas alias ad infernu, sed sectae istae quatuor inter Christianos sunt amplius increpadae.
units.tr: The Saracens are to be severely rebuked because they do not take Christ's yoke upon themselves but walk through other sects to hell; but these four sects among Christians are to be rebuked even more severely.

units.la: Nemo haberet conscientia omnes illas sectas fri uolas relinquere, imo infidelitatis signu foret licentia papae et alterius de hoc petere, quia in hoc uideretur quis petere de illo licetia ab antichristo quod generaliter concediture discipulis Iesu Christi.
units.tr: No one would have a clear conscience in leaving all those frivolous sects. Indeed, it would be a sign of unbelief to seek permission about this from the pope or anyone else, since in doing so one would seem to ask Antichrist for permission for what is generally granted to the disciples of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Religiosi fideles debent ex uerbis Christi col ligere quod constanter exeant suos priuatos ordines, cum Paulus exierit ordinem Pharisaicum, et cum Dominus ex sua communi gratia concedit fidelibus suis ut potiora eligant et renunciant minus bona.
units.tr: Faithful religious ought to gather from the words of Christ that they should constantly go out from their private orders, just as Paul left the Pharisaic order; and because the Lord, in his common grace, grants to his faithful that they choose the better things and renounce the less good.

units.la: Domini temporales debent abstrahere a uiris ecclesiasticis seculare dominium, ad damnum suae animae contra fidem scripturae stolide occupatu.
units.tr: Secular lords ought to withdraw secular lordship from churchmen, which they have foolishly seized against the faith of Scripture, to the damage of their own souls.

units.la: Sepulcra mortuorum sunt tripliciter illusionis obiecta. lapides enim politi sunt obiectum primum. aurum et argentum incrustata super istos lapides sunt secundu. et lapides preciosi cu alijs bracteis sunt tertium illusionis obiectum. ut patet de sepulchris rouiter canonizatoru a Romana ecclesia.
units.tr: Tombs of the dead are an object of illusion in three ways. The polished stones are the first object; gold and silver encrusted over these stones are the second; and precious stones with other gilded plates are the third object of illusion. This is evident in the tombs of those canonised by the Roman Church.

units.la: Ratio necessitat quod fideles credant plus nimis operibus sanctoru, quam mortuis illusionibus, quae fiunt communiter per diabolum in presentia talium sepulcrorum.
units.tr: Reason compels us to conclude that the faithful believe far too much in the works of the saints, and not enough in the dead illusions which are commonly performed by the devil in the presence of such tombs.

units.la: Religiosi nostri praeter ordinationem Domi-ni introducti, habent obseruantias hypocriticas, ut cantum in medijs noctibus, & ieiunium in ele-ctis temporibus, & alia talia quae non sonant in religione Domini nostri Iesu Christi. Tractatu 2. de sermone Domini in monte, capite 16.
units.tr: Our religious orders, introduced beyond the ordinance of the Lord, have hypocritical observances, such as singing in the middle of the night, fasting at chosen times, and other such things which do not accord with the religion of our Lord Jesus Christ. Tractate 2 on the Sermon on the Mount, chapter 16.

units.la: Confessio uocalis facta sacerdoti introducta per Innocentium tertium, non est tam necessaria homini, ut diffinit. quia si quis solu cogitatu, uer-bo, uel opere offendit fratrem suum, solum cogi-tatu, uerbo uel opere sufficit poenitere.
units.tr: Vocal confession made to a priest, introduced by Innocent III, is not so necessary for a man as he defines. For if anyone offends his brother by thought alone, by word or by deed, it is enough to repent by thought, word or deed alone.

units.la: Papa latinus erubescere debet de ista moder-na poenitentia fine fundatione per omnia, cum non liceat mortalibus etiam Apostolis difficulta-re legeDomini ultra hoc, quod ipsemet limitauit.
units.tr: The Latin pope ought to blush at this modern penance, which has no foundation in every respect, since it is not lawful for mortals, not even Apostles, to burden the law of the Lord beyond what he himself has limited.

units.la: Diuina sapientia Hebraeorum & Graecorum deridet istam stultitiam latinorum.
units.tr: The divine wisdom of the Hebrews and the Greeks mocks this foolishness of the Latins.

units.la: Graue est & infundabile presbiterum audire confessiones populi modo quo latini utuntur.
units.tr: It is a grievous and unfounded practice for a presbyter to hear the confessions of the people in the way the Latins do.

units.la: Sicut Christus iniunxit adulterae quod non- lit amplius peccare: ita uidetur confessores iniun-gere debere poenitentiam confitenti, quia nulla est ars poenitentiaria a qua potest capi certior poenitentia iniungenda.
units.tr: Just as Christ enjoined on the adulteress that she should sin no more, so it seems confessors ought to enjoin penance on the one confessing, since there is no penitential art from which a more certain penance could be drawn to enjoin.

units.la: Quia tam graciosus est Dominus, & alliga-tionem astringentem homines tantum exosus, sieût fuit in primitiua Ecclesiam dicât fideles no stris sacrarijs, dirumpamus uincula eorum &c.
units.tr: Because the Lord is so gracious, and so hostile to the bonds that fasten men, as was the case in the primitive Church, let our faithful say in our sacred places: "Let us break their bonds asunder", etc.

units.la: In hijs uerbis, uos mundi estis sed non omnes: posuit diabolus pedicam infidelem, in qua pedem caperet Christiani, introduxit enim confessionem priuatam & infundabilem, et postquam illa confessori nota fuerit: in lege statuit quod non prodatur propter populi maliciam sic confessi.
units.tr: In these words, "You are clean, but not all", the devil set a faithless snare in which he might catch the Christian's foot. For he introduced private and unfounded confession, and after it had become known to the confessor, he decreed in law that the confessed should not be betrayed because of the malice of the people.

units.la: Christus in baptismo suo non chrisma huiusmodi, sed aquam simplicem requisiuit.
units.tr: Christ in his baptism did not require such chrism, but plain water.

units.la: Experimēto cognoscimus quod papa uel mortuo, uel deposito, cum suis cardinalibus, & prælatis cæsarijs non minus, sed amplius prosperare tur Ecclesia. Nam quantum ad sacramentum confirmationis, cum sacramento ordinis, & benedictione chrismatis, cū Ecclesijs dedicādis, quæ appropriatur episcopis, uidetur quod Christus perpendiculariter residens in cœlis super iustos presbyteros, daret illis, potestatem talia faciendi.
units.tr: By experience we know that the Church is not less but more prosperous when the pope is either dead or deposed, along with his cardinals and Caesarean prelates. For as regards the sacrament of confirmation, together with the sacrament of order, the blessing of chrism, and the dedication of churches, which is appropriated to bishops, it seems that Christ, sitting directly in heaven over the just presbyters, would give them the power to do such things.

units.la: Cum mendacium hæreticum de hostia consecrā ta inter singula teneat principatum, ut ipsa ab Ecclesia extirpetur: secure denūcio modernis hæreticis, quod non possunt declarare, nec intelligere accidens sine subiecto, & ideo omnes istæ hæreticæ sectæ sunt in capitulo ignorantum. Ioannis 4. Nos adoramus quod scimus, &c.
units.tr: Since the heretical lie about the consecrated host holds the first place among all the others, so that it may be rooted out of the Church, I confidently declare to modern heretics that they cannot state or understand an accident without a subject. Therefore all these heretical sects are in the chapter of the ignorant. John 4: "We worship what we know", etc.

units.la: Moueret fideles principes atque regna, quod dum talia capita sunt hæretica & ex errore pro prio uel consensu in materia de hostia consecra tamen sunt actualiter membra Iesu Christi Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: It would move the faithful princes and kingdoms that, while such heads are heretical and through their own error or consent in the matter of the consecrated host, they are nonetheless actually members of the Church of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Non dubium quin Christus suffragabitur fidelibus pie laborantibus in ista materia, cum nulla fuerit materia martirij laudabilior.
units.tr: There is no doubt that Christ will support the faithful who labour devoutly in this matter, since no martyrdom is more praiseworthy.

units.la: Fratres isti qui ex defectu suæ fundationis, à fidelibus recipiendi non essent: sunt hæretici recentes, plusquam multi quàm mures, cum dicunt quod ipsi comedunt accidens, sine subiecto.
units.tr: Those brothers who, because of the defect of their foundation, are not to be received by the faithful, are recent heretics, more numerous than mice, when they say that they eat an accident without a subject.

units.la: Quidam prognosticant probabiliter quod regna non erunt in pace sine perturbatione notabili, dum ista hæresis venenosa taliter fuerit dominata.
units.tr: Some reasonably predict that the kingdoms will not be at peace without notable disturbance, while this poisonous heresy has such dominion.

units.la: Audacter pronostico omnibus istis sectis & suis complicibus, quod non defendent fidelibus quod sacramentum sit accidens sine subiecto, antequam Christus & tota triumphans Ecclesia venerit equitans in finali iudicio super flatum Angeli Gabrielis.
units.tr: I boldly predict to all these sects and their accomplices that they will not persuade the faithful that the sacrament is an accident without a subject, before Christ and the whole triumphant Church come riding at the final judgment on the breath of the angel Gabriel.

units.la: Quando fidelis communicandus panem postulat: moderni hæretici, secundum suam falsam fictionem, ei porrigùt peius quàm lapidem, quia accidens sine subiecto.
units.tr: When the faithful man asks for the bread to be communicated, the modern heretics, according to their false fiction, offer him something worse than a stone, namely an accident without a subject.

units.la: A principio millenarij diaboli usq; hodie, regna gnauit hæresis de hostia consecrata, ut legenti epistolas decretales patet, cum suis glossationibus & sectis, pertinaciter consentientibus huic hæresi, postquam Diabolus ipsam introduxit.
units.tr: From the beginning of the thousand years of the devil down to today, this heresy about the consecrated host has reigned over the kingdoms, as is plain to anyone who reads the decretal letters, with their glosses and their sects, which persistently agree with this heresy since the devil introduced it.

units.la: Sicut Christus est simul Deus & homo: sic hostia consecrata est simul corpus Christi, & verus panis, quia est corpus Christi ad minimum in figura, & verus panis in natura. vel quod idem sonat verus panis realiter, & corpus Christi figuraliter.
units.tr: Just as Christ is at once God and man, so the consecrated host is at once the body of Christ and true bread: for it is the body of Christ at least in figure, and true bread in nature. Or, what amounts to the same thing, it is true bread really and the body of Christ figuratively.

units.la: Praetermissa probatione materiali & formali, oportet catholicum probationes habitudinales concedere in scripturis, ut Genesis 41. septem boves septem anni sunt, & ad Corinthios, Petra autem erat Christus, & Matth. 11. Si uultis scire, ipse, scilicet Baptista, est Helias, sic dicit catholicus, quod panis sacramentalis est corpus Domini, & unum in calice, est eius sanguis.
units.tr: Setting aside material and formal proof, the Catholic must concede relational proofs in the Scriptures, such as Genesis 41: "The seven cows are seven years," and 1 Corinthians: "The rock was Christ," and Matthew 11: "If you wish to know, he, namely the Baptist, is Elijah." So the Catholic says that the sacramental bread is the body of the Lord, and the one in the cup is his blood.

units.la: Quum plus credi debeat operibus, quam alementó, & chartis episcopi, magis est operibus presbiteri attendendum, qua scripturæ episcopi ordinantur: Et ideo nullæ tales literæ testimoniales darent fidem fidelibus quod quis foret sacerdos, siue Episcopus, sed juxta Euangelica hoc probaret. Secunda parte de sermone Domini in monte cap. 69.
units.tr: Since more credit ought to be given to deeds than to words, and to the letters of a bishop, more attention must be paid to the works of a presbyter, by which the Scriptures ordain bishops. And therefore no such testimonial letters would give the faithful assurance that someone is a priest or bishop, but he should prove it according to the Gospel. Second part, on the Lord's sermon on the mount, chapter 69.

units.la: Non ex testificatione hominis ordinantis, sed ex iustificatione operis capienda est probabilis euidentia talis status. Deus enim potest sine talι instrumento digno uel indigno personam aliam in tali statu constituere, nec est probabilior euidentia quam ex uita, ideo habita uita sancta et doctrina catholica satis est Ecclesiae militanti. Ibidem.
units.tr: The probable evidence of such a state is to be taken not from the testimony of the man who ordains, but from the justification of the work. For God can appoint another person to such a state without such an instrument, whether worthy or unworthy, and there is no more probable evidence than from life. Therefore, a holy life and sound Catholic teaching are enough for the militant Church. Ibidem.

units.la: Dubitare habent fideles si moderni haeretici conficiunt, uel rite ordinant, uel ministrant alia sacramenta, quia non est euidentia, quod Christus adsistit tali pontifici, propter hoc quod tam male super illam hostiam mentitur, et in sua conuersatione dicit contrarium uitae Christi. Eiusdem sermonis cap. 48.
units.tr: The faithful have reason to doubt whether, if modern heretics consecrate, or ordain duly, or administer the other sacraments, Christ is present with such a prelate, because it is not evident, since he lies so wickedly over that host, and in his conduct says the opposite of the life of Christ. Of the same sermon, chapter 48.

units.la: Domini temporales possunt licite auferre temporalia ab Ecclesia delinquente, nec oportet istis expectare decretum Romani pontificis, ideo absit quod fallacia antichristi seducat mundi principes, ne ex defectu sui, unanimes uadant praecipites in infernum.
units.tr: Temporal lords may lawfully take away temporal goods from a Church that offends, and they need not wait for a decree of the Roman pontiff. Far be it that the deceit of Antichrist should lead the princes of the world astray, so that through their own defect, all together they rush headlong into hell.

units.la: Ex proprietate uiuentes ut fratres, sunt haeretici, qui in suis praedicationibus, exhortationibus, uel confessionibus in praedicta quauis materia obmutescunt.
units.tr: Those who live in private ownership like brothers are heretics, who in their preaching, exhortations or confessions keep silent on any of the aforesaid matters.

units.la: Domini seculares sunt haeresiarchae qui in ista materia tacent contra iuramentum factum Ecclesiæ, atq; suum officium limitatum à Deo:
units.tr: Secular lords are heresiarchs who keep silent on this matter, against the oath made to the Church and against their office, which God has limited.

units.la: Omnia bona istorum possessionatorum hæreticorum confiscurrentibus principibus qui hæresi ipsorum detraherent, & omnia eorum immobilia, ut redditus, prædia, & prædicta quibus dotati sunt: redirent ad manus secularium, ut primo.
units.tr: All the goods of these heretical possessioners should be confiscated by the princes who take away their heresy, and all their immovable property, such as revenues, estates, and the things with which they are endowed, should return into the hands of the secular powers, as at first.

units.la: Licet progenitores superstitum priuauerunt se, uero Dominio talium prædiorum, & reddituum, quo ad Deum: tamen posteri contriti de sui & suorum progenitorum stultitia, acquirerent, corrigendo errores, titulum iustitiæ quo ad Deum, & quo ad homines, qui quidem titulus fore longe iustior, quàm titulus gladij, ex conquestu.
units.tr: Although their ancestors deprived themselves, before God, of the true dominion over such estates and revenues, nevertheless their descendants, grieved at the folly of themselves and their ancestors, would acquire, by correcting the errors, a title of justice both before God and before men. This title would be far more just than the title of the sword, arising from conquest.

units.la: Stante dotatione Ecclesiæ, quæ est mater & fotrix hæresis symoniacæ, miraculum foret insolitum quòd hæresis symoniaca foret extincta.
units.tr: So long as the endowment of the Church stands, which is the mother and nurse of simoniacal heresy, it would be an unusual miracle if simoniacal heresy were extinguished.

units.la: Intoxicata & excommunicata sunt regna per prælatos hæreticos in omni genere sacerdotum defectantur, namque copiosa habere ad iactantiam temporalium, ut largius ministretur egentibus est studiose appetere officium laicale.
units.tr: Kingdoms are poisoned and excommunicated by heretical prelates, and there is a shortage of priests of every kind; for to have many temporal goods for display, so that they may be distributed more freely to the needy, is to seek a lay office eagerly.

units.la: Populus conduceret tales prælatos ne benedicant, uel ministrent Ecclesiæ sacramenta, quia eorum benedictiones, maledictiones sunt, secundum illud. Maledicam bened. &c.
units.tr: The people should refuse to hire such prelates, lest they bless or administer the sacraments of the Church, because their blessings are curses, according to that saying: "I will curse their blessings," etc.

units.la: Conuersa est cleri religio à Christiana in Cæsaream, & dimisso titulo recipiendi à populo ædificato, eleemosinas gratis datas, statuuntur quædam leges Antichristianæ ad pecunias extorquendas.
units.tr: The religion of the clergy has been turned from Christian to Caesarean, and, with the title of receiving from the people, which was built up, alms freely given are dismissed, and certain Antichristian laws are enacted to extort money.

units.la: Siue clericus uadat, siue mittat etiam in uoculis studiorum ad Papam pro beneficijs Ecclesiasticis, ut sic seipsum ad Dei ministerium exaltet, Deest, nescio quid.
units.tr: Whether a cleric goes, or even sends, in the vocal studies of the schools, to the Pope for ecclesiastical benefices, so that he may exalt himself to the ministry of God, ... Something is missing, I know not what.

units.la: Periculosum est quodcunque diuinum patronatum Ecclesiæ occupare, quia nisi persona plus humili, & prudenti illud intenderit: damnabiliter cadit à diuino patronatu.
units.tr: It is dangerous to seize any divine patronage of the Church, because unless a person who is more humble and prudent has intended it, he falls damnably from divine patronage.

units.la: Apostoli quoque laborabant manibus, ac parcè susceperunt eleemosinas à populo præcise quantum fuerat eis necessarium, & utile populo ad spirituale ministerium recipiendum, unde uidetur mihi indubie quod quicunque clericus intentione alia & mensura à populo benedictionem receperit: symoniacus est censendus.
units.tr: The apostles also laboured with their hands, and received alms from the people sparingly, precisely as much as was necessary for them, and useful to the people for receiving the spiritual ministry. Hence it seems to me beyond doubt that any cleric who receives a blessing from the people with another intention and measure should be judged a simoniac.

units.la: Leges multæ papales sunt hæreticæ, ut patet de lege Bonifacij 8. in titulo de Rescriptis. capitulo. Si duobus, & alijs huiusmodi.
units.tr: Many papal laws are heretical, as is plain from the law of Boniface VIII, in the title on Rescripts, chapter "If to two," and others of this kind.

units.la: Quantum ad leges singulas de raptoribus & spoliatoribus ecclesiarum æditas, credo quòd intelligitur per has leges, quòd illi qui spoliant ecclesiam, quæ est homines inexcellentia status & virtutum per dotationes cæcas, instinctu d' abo‐li, extortas, sunt sacrilegi, & à triumph. ntecc‐clesia maledicti.
units.tr: As for the individual laws on robbers and plunderers of churches that have been issued, I believe that they are understood to mean that those who despoil the Church, which is men eminent in status and virtues, by blind endowments extorted at the instigation of the devil, are sacrilegious, and are cursed by the triumphant Church.

units.la: Deficit humana regula de eligendo prapositos, apostolo enim deficiente, reuelatione elegerunt Mathiam per sortem, sed factum eorum debet in isto, esse euidentius quam sequens dictu, uel factum Romani pontificis, quare adhuc debet Ecclesia intendere huic formæ.
units.tr: Human rule is deficient about choosing prelates. For when the apostle failed, they chose Matthias by lot through revelation. But their deed ought in this matter to be more evident than any later saying or deed of the Roman pontiff; therefore the Church ought still to attend to this form.

units.la: Implicans se electionibus secundum traditiones humanas, ubi posset secundu legem Dei procedere: peccat grauiter, et sic uidetur mihi quòd omnes adinuentiones hominũ præter fidem scripturæ, sunt secundum plus uel minus culpabiles.
units.tr: Whoever entangles himself in elections according to human traditions, where he could proceed according to the law of God, sins gravely. And so it seems to me that all human inventions apart from the faith of Scripture are more or less culpable.

units.la: Quantum ad consecrationes locorũ, dicitur quod episcopi consecrantes, capiunt quinq; marcas, sed longè minus malum foret celebrare sub dio, quàm in loco taliter benedicto. Lepra enim spiritualis inficit parietes & loca d' stantia, cum Deus pro leuiori peccato subuerterit Sodomam & Gomorram.
units.tr: As for the consecrations of places, it is said that the bishops who consecrate take five marks; but it would be far less evil to celebrate under the open sky than in a place so blessed.
