For spiritual leprosy infects the walls and the places standing near, since God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah for a lighter sin.

units.la: Talis consecratio nõ est uera consecratio, sed execratio & maledicta, retardans fideles à misterio debito Deo suo: Non occurrit ex scriptu-ra, quare sanctus laicus, vel quilibet sacerdos non possit taliter benedicere, & sacrare.
units.tr: Such a consecration is not a true consecration, but a cursing and a curse, hindering the faithful from the due service owed to their God. Scripture does not show why a holy layman, or any priest, could not bless and consecrate in this way.

units.la: Subtrahat populus decimas, oblationes, & alias privatas eleemosinas ab indigenis antichristi discipulis, cum hoc facere debeant de lege Dei, nec est timenda sed gaudenter acceptanda maledictio, vel censura quam inferunt discipuli antichristi.
units.tr: Let the people withhold tithes, offerings and other private alms from the hirelings of Antichrist, since they ought to do so by the law of God; nor should the curse or censure which the disciples of Antichrist bring be feared, but rather gladly accepted.

units.la: Ex principijs fidei est per se notum, quod quicquid homo in mortali peccato fecerit, peccat mortaliter.
units.tr: It is known in itself from the principles of faith that whatever a man does in mortal sin, he sins mortally.

units.la: Deficientibus praelatis ut cifris antichristi, Christus ordinat quemcunque, quomodocunque & quocunque voluerit, sequatur igitur in moribus, et secure potest de ipso confidere, quod deficiente praelato caesario, sit a Christo legitime ordinatus.
units.tr: When the prelates fail, like the cyphers of Antichrist, Christ ordains whomever, however and wherever he wills. Let one therefore follow in conduct, and securely trust that a prelate who is Caesarean in failing has been lawfully ordained by Christ.

units.la: Dominus papa, episcopi, omnes religiosi, vel pueri clerici titulo perpetuae possessionis dotati, debent renunciare illis in manus brachij secularis, quod si pertinaciter noluerint: per seculares Dominos debent cogi.
units.tr: The lord pope, bishops, all religious, or clerics endowed with the title of perpetual possession, ought to renounce these things into the hands of the secular arm; and if they stubbornly refuse, they must be compelled by the secular lords.

units.la: Religio privata est religio praeter religionem Domini expressam in evangelio, adinuenta, & illa privatur omni fundatione laudabili.
units.tr: Private religion is a religion invented apart from the religion of the Lord expressed in the gospel, and it is deprived of every laudable foundation.

units.la: Omnis religio pr.u.ta sapit in eo imperfectionem item & peccatum quo homo impeditur ad Deum liberè seruiendum.
units.tr: Every private and perverse religion smacks of imperfection and of sin, insofar as a man is hindered from serving God freely.

units.la: Cuncti patroni illorum ordinum peccaue-rut, licet isti ordines occasionaliter faciant multa bona.
units.tr: All the patrons of those orders have sinned, although those orders occasionally do many good things.

units.la: Quis excusare poterit istas sectas fratrum quin demisso Christi ordine blasphemè eligant minus bonum, imò tota sua religio blasphemia est permixta.
units.tr: Who will be able to excuse those sects of friars, which, by setting aside the order of Christ, blasphemously choose the lesser good? Indeed their whole religion is mixed with blasphemy.

units.la: Inter omnia monstra quæ unquam intraue-runt ecclesiam: monstrum horum fratrum est maximè seductiuum, infundabile, & à veritate & charitate distans.
units.tr: Among all the monsters that have ever entered the Church, the monster of these friars is most seductive, indefensible, and far removed from truth and charity.

units.la: Ritus sensibilis ad quem religiosi priuati ex suo ordine obligantur: est traditionum suarum obseruatio ultra mandata decalogi, et Iesu Christi Domini nostri, & traditio ista necessitat ipsos esse hypocritas, & infringere mandatum Domini.
units.tr: The outward rite to which private religious are bound by their order is the observance of their own traditions beyond the commandments of the Decalogue and of Jesus Christ our Lord. This tradition necessarily makes them hypocrites and breaks the command of the Lord.

units.la: Si secundum prophetiam Ezechielis pecca-tum Sodomæ quadruplex fuit iniquitas: quanto patentius aggregatio ex ijs priuatis traditionibus ac priuilegijs est colligatio impietatis, qui subetur dissolui.
units.tr: If, according to the prophecy of Ezekiel, the sin of Sodom was fourfold in iniquity, how much more openly does the association formed by those private traditions and privileges constitute a bond of impiety, which must be dissolved.

units.la: Cum Dominus dicit per prophetas, dis-solue colligationes impietatis, solue fasciculos deprimentes, Dimitte eos qui confracti sunt liberos, & omne onus dirumpere uidetur, tales ordines priuatos praecipiendo soluere.
units.tr: When the Lord says through the prophets, "Dissolve the bonds of impiety, loosen the heavy burdens, let go those who are broken and free, and break every yoke" (cf. Isa. 58), it seems to command that such private orders be dissolved.

units.la: Si ceremoniae legis ueteris propter suam gra‐uitudinem & multitudinem cessare debuerant in lege gratiae, quanto magis tales traditiones ho‐minum quae sunt infundabiliter fictae, isto tempo‐re legis gratiae debent solui.
units.tr: If the ceremonies of the old law had to cease in the law of grace on account of their heaviness and multitude, how much more must such traditions of men, which are invented without any foundation, be dissolved in this time of the law of grace.

units.la: Coniectura probabilis est, quod talis qui rite uiuit, diaconus est, uel sacerdos, sicut enim cogno‐sco quod iste est Ioannes, sic probabili coniectu‐ra cognosco quod ille sic uiuendo constitutus est a Deo in tali officio, siue statu.
units.tr: It is a probable conjecture that one who lives rightly is a deacon or a priest. For just as I know that this man is John, so by a probable conjecture I know that the man who lives thus has been appointed by God to such an office or station.

units.la: Videtur sanctis doctoribus, quod in sacramento ordinis superfluum est ponere plures q duos gra‐dus scil. diaconus, uel leuitas, uel presbyteros, siue episcopos, nam illi duo gradus suffecerat in lege ueteri: ubi multiplicius fuit ministerium cleri Dei.
units.tr: It seems to the holy teachers that in the sacrament of orders it is superfluous to posit more than two grades, namely deacon and Levite, or elder or bishop; for those two grades sufficed under the old law, when the ministry of God's clergy was more manifold.

units.la: Ad quid oportet ponere alios tres gradus, sci licet clericu prima tonsurae, accolitu & subdia‐conum, cum nec ratio ministerij, nec autoritas fa‐ciat euidentiam, quod in statu clerici isti tres gra‐dus clerici sint distincti.
units.tr: Why is it necessary to posit three other grades, namely the first tonsure of the clergy, the acolyte, and the subdeacon, since neither the nature of the ministry nor authority makes it evident that these three grades are distinct within the state of the clergy?

units.la: Videtur irrationale & infundabile, q ecclesia militans sit cum tribus istis ordinibus onerata.
units.tr: It seems irrational and indefensible that the militant Church should be burdened with these three orders.

units.la: Mostrosa uidetur ordinis noui conglobatio per hoc quod diabolus ditat, & onerat uocatum falsè clerum Domini, cum talis globatio non sit honoris, sed oneribus, nec institutioni Christi consona, sed contraria.
units.tr: The clustering of a new order seems monstrous, in that the devil enriches and burdens the falsely called clergy of the Lord; for such a clustering belongs not to honour but to burdens, and is consonant not with the institution of Christ but contrary to it.

units.la: Sicut non sequitur Petrus fuit uocatus à Christo singulariter sathanas, ergo Petrus fuit cunctis abiectior, ita non sequitur, Petrus habuit singulariter haec priuilegia ut sibi diceretur, Tibi dabo claues, et Rogaui pro te ut no deficiat, etc. ergo Petrus debuit post ascensionem esse papa, & sic caput ecclesiae militantis.
units.tr: Just as it does not follow that because Christ called Peter alone Satan, Peter was therefore the most abject of all, so it does not follow that because Peter alone had these privileges, namely that it was said to him, "I will give you the keys," and "I have prayed for you that your faith may not fail," etc., Peter therefore had to be pope after the ascension, and so the head of the militant Church.

units.la: Certū uidetur ex chronicis quod non à Christo, sed à Caesare Constantino Romanus episcopus accepit, uel usurpauit potestatem.
units.tr: It is clear from the chronicles that the Roman bishop received or usurped his power not from Christ but from the emperor Constantine.

units.la: Quod ex fide Euangelij ista papalis praemi-nentia coepit ortum, est aeque falsum, sicut quod ex pura ueritate error quilibet est exortus.
units.tr: That this papal pre-eminence began from the faith of the gospel is just as false as that any error arose from pure truth.

units.la: Ex isto textu. Sinō abiero, elicitur, quod fuit ut-expediens Christum ascendere, & non perpetuo cum sua Ecclesia conuersari, sed multo magis repu-gnat legi & ordinationi Christi, quod sit unus talis fictus uicarius illicitè in ecclesia introductus.
units.tr: From this text, "If I do not go away" (John 16:7), it is inferred that it was expedient for Christ to ascend and not to remain always with his Church. Much more does it oppose the law and ordinance of Christ that some such feigned vicar should have been unlawfully introduced into the Church.

units.la: Nullus potest fundare quod talis uicarius in-trauit ecclesiam per hostium, sed quod secular-ter ex cautela diaboli ascenderat aliunde.
units.tr: No one can establish that such a vicar entered the Church by the door, but rather that he climbed up secularly by a trick of the devil from elsewhere.

units.la: Videtur q; nullus Christianus debet obedire ta-li uicario, siue praepositio, nisi obedientia resistiua.
units.tr: It seems that no Christian ought to obey such a vicar or prelate, except with a resisting obedience.

units.la: Circumcisio et cerimonia ueteris legis non sunt à fidelibus obseruanda, et multo magis hodiernæ cerimoniæ præter nouam et ueterem legem introductæ.
units.tr: Circumcision and the ceremonies of the old law are not to be observed by the faithful, and much less the present ceremonies introduced beside the new and old law.

units.la: Substantia panis manet in altari post consecrationem, et non definit esse panis, hoc est loquendo de pane materiali.
units.tr: The substance of bread remains on the altar after consecration, and does not cease to be bread; this is said of material bread.

units.la: Sicut Ioannes fuit figuraliter, et non personaliter Helias, sic panis in altari figuraliter est corpus Christi, et absq; omni ambiguitate, hæc est figuratiua locutio, hoc est corpus meum: sicut ipse Ioannes ipse est Helias.
units.tr: Just as John was figuratively, and not personally, Elijah, so the bread on the altar is figuratively the body of Christ, and without any ambiguity; "This is my body" is a figurative mode of speech, just as John himself is Elijah.

units.la: In capitulo Ego beringarius. Romana curia determinauit quod sacramentum Eucharistiæ est naturaliter uerus panis: loquendo de pane materiali albo et rotundo.
units.tr: In the chapter "Ego Berengarius," the Roman curia determined that the sacrament of the Eucharist is naturally true bread, speaking of material bread, white and round.

units.la: Diffinientes paruulos fidelium sine sacramentali baptismo decedentes non fore saluandos: sunt in hoc stolidi et præsumptuosi.
units.tr: Those who define that the infants of believers who die without sacramental baptism will not be saved are foolish and presumptuous in this.

units.la: In tempore Pauli sufficiebant ecclesiæ duo ordines clericorum, sacerdos et diaconus, quia certum est quod superbia cæsaria alios adinuenit.
units.tr: In Paul's time two orders of clergy sufficed for the Church, the priest and the deacon, because it is certain that Caesarean pride devised the others.

units.la: Leuis et breuis confirmatio episcoporum cum adiectis ritibus solennitatis, est ex motione diaboli introducta, ut populus in fide ecclesiæ illudatur, et episcoporum solennitas aut necessitas plus credatur.
units.tr: The light and brief confirmation of bishops, with the added rites of solemnity, was introduced by the prompting of the devil, so that the people might be deceived in the faith of the Church and more credence given to the solemnity or necessity of the bishops.

units.la: Quantum ad oleum quo episcopi ungunt pueros, & peplum lineum quod complexum est capiti: videtur quod est ritus levis infundabilis ex scriptura, & quod ista confirmatio introducta supra Apostolos blasphemat in Deum.
units.tr: As for the oil with which bishops anoint children, and the linen cloth that is wrapped around the head: it seems to be a light and indefensible rite without warrant in Scripture, and this confirmation, introduced above the Apostles, blasphemes against God.

units.la: Collatio sacramenti confirmationis, non est episcopis reservata.
units.tr: The conferring of the sacrament of confirmation is not reserved to bishops.

units.la: Antiqui qui ex cupiditate temporalium, exspectant mortuorum, aut ex causa excusandae libidinis, licet desperent de prole, copulantur adinuicem: non vere matrimonialiter copulantur.
units.tr: The ancients who, from desire for temporal goods, wait for the dead, or for the sake of excusing lust, couple with one another even though they despair of offspring, are not truly joined in matrimony.

units.la: Causa diuortij ratione affinitatis, vel consanguinitatis, est infundabiliter humanitus ordinata.
units.tr: A divorce on account of affinity or consanguinity is ordained by men without any warrant.

units.la: Haec verba, Accipiam te in uxorem, eligibiliora sunt in contractu matrimoniali quam ista verba, Accipio te in uxorem, & quod contrahendo cum una per haec verba de futuro, & post cum alia per verba de praesenti, non debet frustrari per verba secundaria.
units.tr: The words "I will take you as wife" are more fitting in the contract of marriage than the words "I take you as wife." And one who contracts with one woman by words of the future tense, and afterwards with another by words of the present tense, ought not to be defeated by the secondary words.

units.la: Duodecim sunt procuratores & discipuli Antichristi, papa, cardinales, patriarchi, archiepiscopi, episcopi, archidiaconi, officiales, decani, monachi, bifurcati canonici, pseudofratres introducti iam ultimo, & quaestores.
units.tr: The twelve procurators and disciples of Antichrist are: the pope, cardinals, patriarchs, archbishops, bishops, archdeacons, officials, deans, monks, forked canons, the pseudo-friars introduced most recently, and the questors.

units.la: Praecipitur simpliciter negatiue, q; nec sacer dotes Aaronitæ nec Leuitæ haberet partem hæreditatis cum aliis tribubus, sed quod pure uiuat de decimis & oblationibus.
units.tr: It is commanded simply in the negative that neither the Aaronite priests nor the Levites should have a share of the inheritance with the other tribes, but that they should live purely on tithes and offerings.

units.la: Non est maior hæreticus uel antichristus quàm ille clericus qui docet quod licitum est sacerdotibus & leuitis legis gratiæ dotari in possessionibus temporalibus. Et si sunt aliqui hæretici uel blasphemi, sunt illi clerici qui hoc docent.
units.tr: There is no greater heretic or antichrist than that cleric who teaches that it is lawful for the priests and Levites of the law of grace to be endowed with temporal possessions. And if there are any heretics or blasphemers, they are those clerics who teach this.

units.la: Non solum possunt Domini temporales auferre bona fortunæ ab ecclesia habitualiter delinquente, nec solum hoc eis licet, sed debet hoc facere sub poena damnationis æternæ.
units.tr: Temporal lords may not only take away the goods of fortune from a Church that persistently offends, nor is this merely permitted to them; they ought to do so under pain of eternal damnation.

units.la: Si corporalis unctio foret sacramentum ut mo bo fingitur, Christus & eius apostoli, eius promulgationem non tacuissent.
units.tr: If bodily anointing were a sacrament, as is falsely imagined, Christ and his apostles would not have kept silent about its promulgation.

units.la: Quicunque humilior est ecclesiæ minister, et in amore Christi quo ad suam ecclesiam, feruentior ille est in ecclesia militante maior, & in ecclesia proximus Christi uicarius.
units.tr: Whoever is the humbler minister of the Church, and the more fervent in love of Christ towards his Church, he is the greater in the militant Church, and in the Church the nearest vicar of Christ.

units.la: Ad uerum seculare dominium requiritur uera iustitia dominantis, sic quod nullus existens in peccato mortali, est uerus Dominus alicuius rei.
units.tr: True secular dominion requires the true justice of the ruler, so that no one who exists in mortal sin is the true lord of anything.

units.la: Omniaquæ eueniet absolutè, necessario eueniet.
units.tr: Everything that will happen absolutely will happen necessarily.

units.la: Quicquid Papa uel cardinales sciunt ex sacra scriptura deducere, istud dùtaxat est credendum, & quicquid ultra præsumpserint, tanquam hæreticum est contemnendum.
units.tr: Whatever the Pope or the cardinals can deduce from Holy Scripture, that alone is to be believed; and whatever they presume beyond this is to be despised as heretical.

units.la: Cum clerus non debeat seculariter dominari, sed esse pauper simulis statui innocentiae instar Christi: manifestum uidetur quod clerus qui tam pertinaciter in temporali dominio obuiat legi Dei, est haereticus maledictus.
units.tr: Since the clergy ought not to rule in secular matters, but to be poor and simple in the condition of innocence after the pattern of Christ, it seems manifest that the clergy who so obstinately resist the law of God in temporal dominion are cursed heretics.

units.la: Patet ex facto quod Romana curia dogmatizans in opere tam pertinaciter & falso dictae sententiae contrarium, est haeretica manifeste, & eo patentius quo publicat haeresim de cleri dominio per Ecclesiam militantem.
units.tr: It is evident from the fact that the Roman curia, by its work, teaches dogmatically the opposite of this sentence, so obstinately and falsely stated, that it is manifestly heretical, and the more openly so in that it publishes the heresy of clerical dominion throughout the militant Church.

units.la: Non est potior antichristus quam qui huic fidei de praedicta pauperie cleri Christiani est contrarius tam opere quam sermone, nec solum isti praelati antichristi, sed mundani domini consentientes isti facinori: sunt capitales inimici Domini Christi Iesu.
units.tr: There is no greater Antichrist than the one who opposes this faith about the aforesaid poverty of the Christian clergy, both by deed and by word. Not only those prelates who are Antichrist, but also the worldly lords who consent to this crime, are the chief enemies of the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Curia romana est minus dispositia ad conuincendum aliquos super haeretica prauitate, illud tamen praesumit temere, quia ad sensum nusticum, est castellum quod est contra Christi Apostolos. In speculo militantis Ecclesiae, capite 5.
units.tr: The Roman curia is least fitted to convict anyone of heretical depravity, yet it presumes this rashly, since to the rustic understanding it is a castle set against the Apostles of Christ. In the Mirror of the Militant Church, chapter 5.

units.la: Quantum ad chartas & concessiones seculariu dominiorum: patet quod clerus erubesceret inniti tam culpabili fundamento, quia in nullo ualet humana concessio nisi praehabita licentia a domino capitali, & cum non possunt docere quod Domini ad hoc habeant licentiam à Christo: paſtet quod tam lege humana quàm diuina est talis ſmulta donatio ſentienda, illicita, & à catholicis ſpueſpenda.
units.tr: As for the charters and grants of secular dominions, it is clear that the clergy should be ashamed to rest on so culpable a foundation. Human grant is worth nothing unless licence has first been obtained from the chief Lord. Since they cannot show that the lords have licence from Christ for this, it is clear that such a worldly endowment must be judged unlawful by both human and divine law, and spurned by Catholics.

units.la: Quantum ad leges & bullas papales, patet quod ſunt confirmatio criminis, quia cum non ſint in Christo est & non, patet, quod impoſsibi le est, ratione, uel ſcriptura traditiones iſtas papales uel leges hominum in hac materia de do tatione Ecclesiæ ſtabiliri.
units.tr: As for papal laws and bulls, it is clear that they confirm crime. Since they are in Christ and not in Christ, it is clear that it is impossible, by reason or by Scripture, for these papal traditions or human laws on the endowment of the Church to be established.

units.la: Qua maior infidelitas, quam approbare eleſtiones cardinalium, qui ex dubio nobis ſunt dia boli incarnati, hæc autem hæresis à loco fortis Apoſtolorum qui elegerunt, per diabolum inſtroducta, ponit zizannia ad catholicos ut in fide catholica diſcordent, medicina, ergo foret, taſles electiones cum non Apoſtolicæ, refutare.
units.tr: What greater unfaithfulness is there than to approve the elections of cardinals, who are, beyond doubt, devils incarnate to us? This heresy, introduced by the devil from the place of the strong Apostles who elected, sows tares among Catholics so that they quarrel over the Catholic faith. The remedy, therefore, would be to refute such elections as not apostolic.

units.la: Si fiat obiectio contra impugnantes dotatioſnem Ecclesiæ de beatis, Benedicto, Gregorio et Bernardo, qui pauca temporalia in pauperie poſsidebant, dicitur quod de illis finaliter poſnitebat. Si iterum obijcias, quod fingo iſtos ſanſctos de ista declinatione à Lege Domini finaliſter poenitere: doce tu quod ſunt ſancti, & ego docebo quod finaliter poenitebant.
units.tr: If an objection is made against those who oppose the endowment of the Church, citing the blessed Benedict, Gregory and Bernard, who possessed few temporal goods in poverty, it is said that they finally repented of it. If you again object that I feign that those saints finally repented of this departure from the Lord's law, then you teach that they are saints, and I will teach that they finally repented.

units.la: Sicut ſub duo influentia cœleſtis liberius eſt xecepta: sic religionis oratio penetrat liberium coelum sub diuo, quàm uenit ad aures Domini inclaustris.
units.tr: As the heavenly influence is received more freely under the open sky, so the prayer of religious life penetrates the freer heaven under the open sky more readily than when it comes to the ears of the Lord in cloisters.

units.la: Quantum ad priuilegia & indulgentias Ecclesiae ac regulatione in lege noua: patet quòd soret expediens toti Ecclesiae, quòd omnes no-uitates huiusmodi sint sopitae, omnia enim talia uidentur esse phantasmata, nec fundata rationi-bus, nec scriptura.
units.tr: As for the privileges and indulgences of the Church and the regulations of the new law, it would be expedient for the whole Church that all novelties of this kind were quashed, for all such things seem to be phantasms, founded neither on reasons nor on Scripture.

units.la: Omnes operationes cōcernentes sacerdotes Casarios, inquantum tamen tales, nonproficiunt, dire-cte ad beatitudinem sed impediunt, uel retardant, et ita est de tribus dignitatibus uel officijsquae e-piscopus sibi reseruat, quaesunt, iuuenū confirma-tio, clericorum ordinatio, et locorū cōsecratio.
units.tr: All operations concerning Caesarean priests, insofar as they are such, do not advance us directly toward blessedness but hinder or retard it. So it is with the three dignities or offices which the bishop reserves to himself: the confirmation of young people, the ordination of clergy, and the consecration of places.

units.la: Cum Christus non ordinauit istas uniuersitates atq; collegia: manifestum uidetur, quòd sicut graduationes in illis sunt uana gentilitas intro-ducta: sic dicta & obiecta contra secularia do-minia clericorum & appropriationes Ecclesia-rum sunt uiuaciter contra eos.
units.tr: Since Christ did not ordain these universities and colleges, it seems manifest that just as the gradations within them are a vain worldliness introduced, so the things said and objected against the secular dominions of clerics and the appropriations of churches are vigorously against them.

units.la: Paulus pharifeus quondam propter melio-rem sectam Christi, ex eius licentia sectam illam dereliquit, & hæc est ratio quare claustrales quacunque fuerint obligatione aut quocunque iuramento stulto astricti: debent libere ex mandato Christi exire ista uincula, & induere liberam sectam Christi.
units.tr: Paul the Pharisee once, for the sake of the better sect of Christ, with its permission, abandoned that other sect. This is the reason why monks, however bound by any obligation or any foolish oath, ought freely, by the command of Christ, to go out from those chains and put on the free sect of Christ.

units.la: Omnes censuræ antichristi non sunt nisi falsæ umbræ à uia Domini deterrentes.
units.tr: All the censures of Antichrist are nothing but false shadows that deter us from the way of the Lord.

units.la: Vnum est solacium fideli, quòd excommunicatio, suspensio, & omnes tales censuræ non sunt in Christo, & in lege sua fundatæ, sed ab antichristo callidè machinatæ.
units.tr: One consolation for the faithful is that excommunication, suspension and all such censures are not in Christ or founded on his law, but cunningly devised by Antichrist.

units.la: Quælibet essentia siue corporea siue incorporea est communis tribus suppositis, & omnibus illis communiter, proprietates, accidentia & operationes.
units.tr: Any essence, whether corporeal or incorporeal, is common to the three supposits, and to all of them in common: properties, accidents and operations.

units.la: Contradictionem includit, aliquam essentiam creatam excedere, uel deficere à ternario suppositorum parium, quo ad omnia, in quibus communicant.
units.tr: It involves a contradiction for some created essence to exceed or fall short of the threefold number of equal supposits in all the things in which they share.

units.la: Deus non est alicuius potentiæ intensiue.
units.tr: God is not of any intensive power.

units.la: Nullum accidens, potest esse aliquid per se existens.
units.tr: No accident can be something existing per se.

units.la: Si albedo posset per se existere: tunc ipsius unio ad subiectum foret accidens quo subiectum fieret accidentatum immediate formaliter, & non illa albedo, & talis unio esset qualitas, & non albedo data.
units.tr: If whiteness could exist per se, then its union with the subject would be an accident by which the subject would immediately and formally become accidented, and not that whiteness; and such a union would be a quality, and not whiteness given.

units.la: Nihil agit proprie nisi essentia absoluta, cuiusmodi est substantia, habens propriam inclinationem
units.tr: Nothing acts properly except an absolute essence, such as substance, having its own natural inclination,

units.la: tiones tionem naturalem, à qua procedit actio extrinse-ca, quod alienum est ab accidente quocunque.
units.tr: from which an extrinsic action proceeds; this is alien to any accident whatever.

units.la: Quælibet essentia habet unum suppositum secundum quod producit aliud suppositum par priori, & ista est actio immanens perfectissima possibilis naturæ.
units.tr: Any essence has one supposit insofar as it produces another supposit equal to the first, and this is the most perfect immanent action possible for a nature.

units.la: Impossibile est multa puncta vel substantias punctuales esse simul in eodem situ indiuisibili, ponendo situm & puncta mathematica, ergo non est possibile duo corpora coexistere.
units.tr: It is impossible for many points, or punctual substances, to be at the same time in the same indivisible situation; positing situation and mathematical points, therefore it is not possible for two bodies to coexist.

units.la: Omnis pars mundi corporea continuatur cum alia, cum mundus sit nimia creatura possibilis, moles magna constans ex impossibili materia, sub iecta sitque tempori, & cæteris accidentibus.
units.tr: Every corporeal part of the world is continuous with another, since the world is a possible creature of excessive size, a great mass consisting of impossible matter, subject to time and other accidents.

units.la: Impossibile est, duas substantias corporeas coexistere, unam continere quiescentem localiter, et aliam corpus quiescens continue penetrantem.
units.tr: It is impossible for two corporeal substances to coexist, one resting locally and containing, and the other body resting while continually penetrating.

units.la: Imaginandum est unam essentiam corpoream in principio productam esse ex indiuisibilibus compositam, & occupare omnem locum possibilem.
units.tr: One must imagine that one corporeal essence, produced at the beginning, was composed of indivisibles and occupies every possible place.

units.la: In Eucharistia manet unum corpus subiectans accidentia panis, quod uoco corpus mathematicum, & abstractum, sicut enim substantia panis prius natura est corpus, quam panis, sic idem esse, quod panis plus manet corpus sub illo gradu quidditatis generalis.
units.tr: In the Eucharist there remains one body underlying the accidents of the bread, which I call the mathematical and abstract body. For just as the substance of bread is by nature a body prior to being bread, so the same being which is bread remains more body under that grade of general quiddity.

units.la: Altaris sacramentu sensibile non est accidens, sicut quaelibet creatura, sed est substantia quae per se illis accidentibus, quae videmus, est subiecta.
units.tr: The sensible sacrament of the altar is not an accident, as is any creature, but is a substance which per se underlies those accidents which we see.

units.la: V biq; omne ens est, cum omne ens sit Deus.
units.tr: Everywhere every being is, since every being is God.

units.la: Impossibile est Deum multiplicare corpus per diversa loca.
units.tr: It is impossible for God to multiply a body through diverse places.

units.la: Quamvis nec tempus nec accidens aliquod possit agere: poterit tamen facere multa bona
units.tr: Although neither time nor any accident can act, it will nevertheless be able to do many good things.

units.la: Linea aliqua mathematica continua componitur ex duobus, vel tribus, vel quatuor punctis immediatis, aut solum ex punctis simpliciter finitis, vel tempus est, vel fuit, vel erit, compositum ex instantibus immediatis.
units.tr: Some continuous mathematical line is composed of two, or three, or four immediate points, or only of simply finite points; time is, or was, or will be, composed of immediate instants.

units.la: Nos non debemus aliquid praestare, vel donare aliquid peccatori dum cognoscimus ipsum esse talem, quia sic essemus fautores proditorum Domini nostri, vel foveremus proditorem Domini nostri. de Dominio civili cap. 2.
units.tr: We ought not to grant or give anything to a sinner while we know him to be such, because thus we would be favourers of the traitors of our Lord, or would foster the traitor of our Lord. On civil dominion, chapter 2.

units.la: Peccator sicut nec pro tunc meretur beatitudinem: sic nec meretur ut alius mereatur sibi gratiam, nec bonum aliquod temporale.
units.tr: A sinner, just as he does not at that time merit blessedness, so neither does he merit that another should earn grace for him, nor any temporal good.

units.la: Nec testium dispositio nec iudicis sententiatio, nec corporalis possessio, sicut descensus hereditarius, nec humana commutatio sive donatio confert homini sine gratia Domini, ut ius ad aliquid vel omnia ista simul.
units.tr: Neither the testimony of witnesses, nor the sentence of a judge, nor corporeal possession such as hereditary descent, nor human exchange or donation confers on a man, without the grace of the Lord, a right to anything, or to all these things together.

units.la: Si Deus det homini bono quemcunque statum dum ipso abutitur, deficit sibi iusta uendicatio ex titulo donationis Christi. Et reuera si titulus ille deficiat nescio quis ualebit.
units.tr: If God gives a good man any status whatever while he abuses it, the just claim arising from the title of Christ's donation fails him. And indeed, if that title fails, I do not know who will be able to stand.

units.la: Omnis iniustus occupans bonū Domini, quod cunq; capit rapina, furto, uel latrocinio aliena. de Dominio ciuili. cap. 14.
units.tr: Every unjust man who occupies the Lord's good, whatever he seizes by robbery, theft or brigandage from what belongs to others. On civil dominion, chapter 14.

units.la: Successio hereditaria est impertinens ad tale dominiū, nisi forte pater meruerit filio gratiam sequendi eum in omnibus.
units.tr: Hereditary succession is irrelevant to such dominion, unless perhaps the father has merited for the son the grace of following him in all things.

units.la: Virtus praecellens in rege est praecipua regnan di ciuiliter, ipsa enim per se sufficit ad regnan-dum Euangelice, & est sufficiens cum approba-tione populi ad regnandum ciuiliter.
units.tr: Pre-eminent virtue in a king is the chief thing for ruling civilly; for it alone is sufficient for ruling in the Gospel manner, and with the approval of the people it is sufficient for ruling civilly.

units.la: Non est possibile ordinare quod ubi quis ex seruo seruili processerit, tunc fiat seruus ciuilis.
units.tr: It is not possible to ordain that where someone has come from a servile slave, he thereby becomes a civil slave.

units.la: Si dominus ciuilis tractet seruum suum non ea dem mensura, qua debet sibi metiri uelle, in casu consimili: excidit à charitate, & per consequens à ciuili dominio, & ex consequente seruus excī-dit respectu illius à seruitute ciuili.
units.tr: If a civil lord treats his servant not by the same measure by which he ought to wish to be measured himself in a like case, he falls from charity and, consequently, from civil dominion; and in consequence the servant, with respect to that lord, falls from civil servitude.

units.la: Titulus hereditariae successionis non sufficit ad fundandum uerum dominium, sed per se ti-tulus charitatis.
units.tr: The title of hereditary succession is not enough to found true dominion; charity alone is the true title.

units.la: Deus non potest dare homini, per se, & suis heredibus, imperpetuum ciuile dominium. de ciuili dominio, cap. 35. est ibi secunda veritas:
units.tr: God cannot give civil dominion in perpetuity to a man and his heirs by himself. On civil dominion, chap. 35; there the second truth is this:

units.la: Nisi aßit lex charitatis intrinsecus nemo propter chartas, vel bullas habet habilitatem, vel iustitiam plus vel minus.
units.tr: Unless the law of charity is inwardly present, no one has the ability or the justice, more or less, through charters or bulls.

units.la: Quacunque communitate vel persona ecclesiastica habitualiter abutente diutius, Domini temporales possunt legitime et valde meritorie, ipsas auferre, etiam quantiscunque traditionibus humanis fuerint confirmatae, de Dominio ciuili. cap. 37.
units.tr: Whatever community or ecclesiastical person persistently abuses its position for a long time, temporal lords may lawfully and very meritoriously strip of civil dominion, however firmly it has been confirmed by human traditions. Chap. 37.

units.la: Si scripturae et rationi debemus credere patet quod Discipuli Christi non habent potestatem coactione exigendi temporalia per censuras, sed hoc tentantes sunt filij hely, filij belial.
units.tr: If we ought to believe Scripture and reason, it is plain that the disciples of Christ have no power to demand temporal goods by coercion through censures; those who attempt this are sons of Eli, sons of Belial.

units.la: Credere debet catholicus, quod nec imperator, nec universalis Ecclesia, nec Dominus de potentia absoluta ordinare potest, pro eo quod quis succedit post Petrum uocatus in facie Ecclesiae Romanus episcopus vel papa eo ipso sit caput Ecclesiae, vel pars eius cui obediendum est.
units.tr: A Catholic must believe that neither the emperor, nor the universal Church, nor the Lord by his absolute power can ordain that whoever succeeds Peter, called Roman bishop or pope before the face of the Church, is by that very fact the head of the Church, or the part of it to which obedience must be given.

units.la: Omnes humanae traditiones quas lex Euangelica non docet facere, sunt superfluae et iniquae.
units.tr: All human traditions that the Gospel law does not teach us to observe are superfluous and unjust.

units.la: Solam legem Christi licet practizare, discere, vel docere, et quicunque practissaueritlegem aliquam quo non dirigit directe ad beatitudinem ex dimem ex praxi facit seipsum damnabilem.
units.tr: It is lawful to practise, learn, or teach only the law of Christ; whoever practises some law that does not lead directly to blessedness makes himself damnable by that practice.

units.la: Non promisit Dominus, quod quicunq; in officio pastorali, Petro Romæ successerit, gaudebit dignitate ut sit caput ecclesiæ.
units.tr: The Lord did not promise that whoever succeeds Peter at Rome in the pastoral office will enjoy the dignity of being head of the Church.

units.la: Nimis abusiue et pharisaice uocantur temporalia ecclesiastica appropriata uel mortificata, ut sint Domino consecrata.
units.tr: Temporal goods of the Church that are appropriated or mortified so as to be consecrated to the Lord are called so in an abusive and Pharisaical way.

units.la: Ex Doctrina Christi qui præcepit suis discipulis habere omnia communia, possunt seculares conuincere, quomodo possessionatorum bona, non timendo uocabulum sacrilegij, possunt merito-rie pauperibus ministrare.
units.tr: From the teaching of Christ, who commanded his disciples to hold all things in common, secular men can prove that the goods of possessioners may be ministered to the poor meritoriously, without fearing the name of sacrilege.

units.la: In adulterio, hæresi, et quolibet tali crimine, possunt iudices seculares sine confusione iurisdi-ctionum cognoscere.
units.tr: In adultery, heresy, and any such crime, secular judges can take cognizance without confusion of jurisdictions.

units.la: Sicut rex, princeps uel dominus, tempore quo est in peccato mortali, non sortitur nomen illius officij, nisi nominetenus & satis æquiuocè, sic nec papa, episcopus, uel sacerdos dum lapsus fue-rit in mortali.
units.tr: Just as a king, prince, or lord, while in mortal sin, does not obtain the name of that office except by name and quite equivocally, so neither does a pope, bishop, or priest once he has fallen into mortal sin.

units.la: Omnis homo in peccato mortali caret quocunq; dominio, et usu licito, operis etiā boni de genere
units.tr: Every man in mortal sin lacks every dominion and lawful use, even of a good work of any kind.

units.la: Cum Christus legē euangelicā non tradidit diuiti, uidetur quod de sensu Christi sit, nullum discipulum suum, pro aliquo bono fortunæ debere contendere.
units.tr: Since Christ did not hand the evangelical law down to the rich man, it seems to accord with the mind of Christ that he would have no disciple contend for any good of fortune.

units.la: Non licet Christiano pastori exercere iudicium, nisi in causa ecclesiæ, quia omnis causa extrinseca est prophana.
units.tr: A Christian minister may not exercise judgment except in a matter of the Church, because every external cause is profane.

units.la: Adueniente debellatione patriæ etiam per barbaros: uia securior foret iniurias pati humiliter, quàm resistere & debellare uiriliter.
units.tr: If the country is overrun, even by barbarians, it would be safer to suffer injuries humbly than to resist and fight back manfully.

units.la: Deus non approbat usum ecclesiasticum domi-nari ciuiliter, uel ciuiliter iudicare.
units.tr: God does not approve of the Church's exercising civil lordship or judging in civil matters.

units.la: Omnes puré clerici debet esse pauperes euan-gelici in specie altissimæ paupertatis, quia debent renunciare omni proprietati & ciuili suo perpetuo.
units.tr: All clergy who are purely clergy ought to be evangelical poor, in the form of the highest poverty, because they must renounce all property and their civil rights for life.

units.la: Omnes Christiani sacerdotes tenentur imitari Christum in specie altissimæ paupertatis, & per consequens omnem dominationem pro suo perpetuo abdicare.
units.tr: All Christian priests are bound to imitate Christ in the form of the highest poverty, and consequently to renounce all lordship for life.

units.la: Chartæ clericis possessionatis superfluunt, cū chartæ charitatis per se sufficiunt. Chartæ enim humanæ sunt femina litium, et faciunt homines præsumere, quòd titulus humanus sufficit sine titulo charitatis.
units.tr: Charters for possessioner clergy are superfluous, since charters of charity suffice by themselves. Human charters are the mother of lawsuits, and make men presume that a human title is enough without the title of charity.

units.la: Videtur mihi impossibile secundum leges humanas, uel diuinas, dotationem cleri in temporalibus, quo ad ciuilitatē perpetuam uel instanea, stabiliri ut patet. Tu primo ex incapacitate illicita in clericis, Tu secundo, quia cadendo à gratia non obstantibus omnibus munimentis possessionalibus: cadit à possessione & dominio.
units.tr: It seems to me impossible, by human or divine law, to establish the endowment of the clergy in temporal goods, as regards civil right, either perpetually or for the present, as is plain. First, from the unlawful incapacity of clerics; second, because by falling from grace, despite all possessional safeguards, one falls from possession and dominion.

units.la: Nec in proprio, nec in communi, debet clerici ciuiliter dominari.
units.tr: Clerics ought not to exercise civil lordship, either individually or in common.

units.la: Quando clericus repetit in foro cötentiosō, vel facit aliquid cōtra contra Christi consilia, ex certa scientia: peccat mortaliter.
units.tr: When a cleric engages in a contentious lawsuit, or does anything against the counsels of Christ, knowingly, he sins mortally.

units.la: Loqui uerbum otiosum ex certa scientia: est peccatum mortale.
units.tr: To speak an idle word knowingly is a mortal sin.

units.la: Ira quantumlibet leuis ex passione animi nō pia intentione colendi Deum & ædificandi proximum, est peccatum mortale.
units.tr: Anger, however slight, arising from a disturbance of the mind and not from the pious intention of worshipping God and edifying the neighbour, is a mortal sin.

units.la: Baptismus delet omne peccatū originale uel actuale, mortale, aut ueniale quod inuenit.
units.tr: Baptism removes every original or actual sin it finds, whether mortal or venial.

units.la: Inutile est ut plurimum, cōdere testamētum.
units.tr: It is generally useless to make a will.

units.la: Omnes existentes in purgatorio, cōmunicati ue participant meritaecclesiæ proportionaliter secundum suā capacitatē, sic quòd qui decessit in maiori gratia, magis participat, et citius liberatur. Et ideo diuites mundi errāt, putantes habere de bonis ab executoribus suis appropriate suffragium, contigit enim pauperes executoribus illis incognitos plus illis participare ex quo apud Deum fuerunt Domini ueriores.
units.tr: All who are in purgatory, whether in communion or not, share in the merits of the Church in proportion to their capacity, so that whoever died in greater grace shares more and is freed more quickly. Hence the rich of the world are mistaken in thinking that they have a suffrage secured for them by their executors out of their goods; for it happens that poor people, unknown to those executors, share more in it, since they were the truer lords before God.

units.la: Prælato quem subditi improbum iudicant, probabiliter ex vita sua, non debent retribuere honores mundanos solitos, nec temporalia tanquam debita, nec tanquam redditus aut proventus, sed debet talia subtrahere, ne offendat Christum. Conversatio mala prælati subtrahit acceptionem ordinum, & aliorum sacramentorum a subditis, qui tamen necessitate urgente possunt hoc ab eis capere, supponendo, pie, quod Deus supplet per ministros suos diabolos, opus vel finem officij, ad quod iuuant.
units.tr: A prelate whom his subjects judge wicked, probably from his life, ought not to be paid the customary worldly honours, nor temporal goods as debts, nor as revenues or incomes; rather they ought to withhold such things, lest they offend Christ. A prelate's evil conduct withdraws from his subjects the reception of orders and of the other sacraments; yet in pressing necessity they may take these from him, piously supposing that God, through his ministers the devils, supplies the work or the end of the office to which they contribute.

units.la: A tempore quo curia Romana declinauit a Christi sequela, est demonstrabile, quod Curia Romana ex nuda autoritate sua, hoc asserit.
units.tr: From the time when the Roman court departed from the following of Christ, it can be shown that the Roman court asserts this from its bare authority.

units.la: Qui peccat, & forde aliqua est maculatus, non potest de ecclesia appellari.
units.tr: He who sins and is stained with some filth cannot be appealed from the Church. [Obscura.]

units.la: Laruati diaboli ex nova simulata religione domesticari non possunt in filios lucis, cum necessario sint filij diaboli.
units.tr: Devils in disguise cannot be tamed into sons of light by a new, feigned religion, since they are necessarily sons of the devil.

units.la: Quatuor ordines mendicantium sunt dispositi naturaliter ut incurrant magnitudinem nimiam, seu peccatum.
units.tr: The four orders of mendicants are by nature disposed to incur excessive greatness, or sin.

units.la: Ista secta volunt aduersari voluntati Dei, quia nolunt de secta Christi contentari & eius regula: sed unam novam friuolam & legi Christi contrariam machinantur.
units.tr: These sects wish to oppose the will of God, because they are unwilling to be content with the sect of Christ and his rule, but devise a new, frivolous one contrary to the law of Christ.

units.la: Papa fingit mendaciter quod est summus vicarius Iesu Christi in terris, sed benedictus Deus qui istud caput Ecclesiæ in parte contriuit, & di uisit in partes contrarias huiusmodi caput male‑dictum. In supplemento triali cap. 5.
units.tr: The pope falsely pretends to be the chief vicar of Jesus Christ on earth. But blessed God, who has in part crushed this head of the Church and divided it into opposing parts, has cursed this head. In the Supplement to the Trialogus, chap. 5.

units.la: Debemus credere quod nullus Papa Cæsari‑us est per ordinem Christi, sed per cautelam dia‑boli in ecclesiam introductus.
units.tr: We must believe that no Caesarean pope is so by the order of Christ; he was introduced into the Church by the devil's cunning.

units.la: Principes & potestates debent potenter iu‑uare, quòd non sit talis papa cæsarius, & nullo modo expensis vel laboribus souere talem diabo‑lum, vel iuuare.
units.tr: Princes and powers ought vigorously to help ensure that there is no such Caesarean pope, and in no way to nourish or aid such a devil with expenses or labours.

units.la: Quid aliud quam obedientiam faciendâ huic diabolo sonat illa lex ipsius. Omnis utriusque sexus, & sic de multis legibus lucifrinis ei si‑milibus.
units.tr: What else does that law of his sound like, but an order to obey this devil: "Every one of either sex..."? And so with many other Luciferian laws similar to it.

units.la: In mendicitatem inciderent sacerdotes, ante‑quam pro temporalibus satisfacerent. In supple‑mento triali cap. 4. 8. de ecclesia & membris.
units.tr: Priests would fall into beggary before they made satisfaction for temporal things. In the Supplement to the Trialogus, chaps. 4 and 8, on the Church and its members.

units.la: Religiosi & clerici possessionati, ex dotatio‑ne quam contra Christi legem suscipiunt & de‑sendunt, sunt meridianum dæmonium, & ad da‑mnum ecclesiæ diaboli indurati.
units.tr: Religious and possessioner clergy, by the endowment they undertake and defend contrary to Christ's law, are a noonday demon, hardened into devils to the damage of the Church.

units.la: Religio, siue regula priuata sapit præsum‑ptionem, blasphemiam, & arrogantiam supra Deum, & religiosi talium ordinum per hypo‑crifim defensionis suæ religionis præsumunt se supra apostolos exaltare.
units.tr: A religion or private rule savours of presumption, blasphemy, and arrogance against God; and religious of such orders, under the hypocrisy of defending their religion, presume to exalt themselves above the apostles.

units.la: In orationibus suis longis non stat profectus ecclesiae, plusquam in Ethnicis.
units.tr: The progress of the Church does not depend on their long prayers any more than it did among the heathen.

units.la: Non sonat in perfectionem religiosorum quod castrantur, vel incarceratur in claustris suis materialibus, vel quod habeant priores qui debent ipsos regere & docere, nec hoc consonat rationi.
units.tr: It is no sign of the perfection of religious that they are castrated or shut up in their material cloisters, or that they have priors who are to rule and teach them; nor does this agree with reason.

units.la: Christus in scriptura non docet aliquam speciem ordinis, & ideo non suo beneplacito est, quod sunt tales de capitulo antichristi, & capitulum continet duodecim species, quae sunt Papa, cardinales, patriarchi, archiepiscopi, episcopi, officiales, decani, fratres, canonici, & quae sunt tores.
units.tr: Christ in Scripture teaches no species of order; therefore it is not by his good pleasure that such men belong to the chapter of Antichrist. That chapter contains twelve species: the pope, cardinals, patriarchs, archbishops, bishops, officials, deans, friars, canons, and rectors (reading "tores" as obscure).

units.la: Ecclesia Christi stare debet in limitibus legis, sic, quod quicquid papa, vel sui cardinales sciuerint ex scriptura clare deducere, illud duntaxat est credendum, vel ad sua monita faciendum: & quicquid ultra praesumpserint, est tanquam haereticum contemnendum.
units.tr: The Church of Christ ought to stand within the limits of the law, so that whatever the pope or his cardinals can clearly deduce from Scripture is alone to be believed or obeyed as their admonition; and whatever they presume beyond that is to be rejected as heretical.

units.la: Non propter electionem cardinalium est quis Christi vicarius, vel membrum Ecclesiae magis quam propter garritum auium vel signum quan Papa apo- tumcunque impertinens quod contingit, & idem stema eccle est iudicium de quibuscunque electionibus hodie sia. celebratis. De Ecclesia & membris cap. 9.
units.tr: It is not by the election of cardinals that anyone is Christ's vicar or a member of the Church, any more than by the chirping of birds or any irrelevant sign that happens to occur. The same holds for any judgment about the elections held today. From "On the Church and Its Members," ch. 9.

units.la: Deus non finens apostema illud, scil. papam in Ecclesia amplius perdurare, soluebat illam pu-tredinem in nido isto diabolico congregatam: et diuisit in duo capita, ut melius pateat sanies & uirulentia antichristi.
units.tr: God, not allowing that abscess, the pope, to remain any longer in the Church, drained that pus gathered in this diabolical nest and divided it into two heads, so that the gore and virulence of Antichrist might be more plainly seen.

units.la: Hostia consecrata est naturaliter uerus pa-nis, & sacramentaliter corpus Christi.
units.tr: The consecrated host is naturally true bread, and sacramentally the body of Christ.

units.la: Cum uia ponens panem manere, sit plus con-sona scripturæ, rationi & sensui, quam uia sin-gens accidens manere sine subiecto: Deus uerax non est autor huius noui operis somniati.
units.tr: Since the view that bread remains is more consonant with Scripture, reason and the senses than the view that accidents remain without a subject, God, who is true, is not the author of this newly dreamed-up work.

units.la: Quod papa sit summus pontifex, est ridicu-lum, & Christus nec in Petro, nec in alio talem approbat dignitatem.
units.tr: That the pope is the highest pontiff is ridiculous, and Christ approves no such dignity either in Peter or in anyone else.

units.la: Ex fide & operibus quatuor sectarum qui sunt clerus cæsarius, uarius monachus, uarius ca-nonicus atq; fratres, euidenter elicio quod nulla persona istarum est membrum Christi in sancto-rum catalogo, nisi in fine dierū deseruerint tam stolidam suam sectam.
units.tr: From the faith and works of the four sects, namely the secular clergy, the various monks, the various canons and the friars, I clearly infer that none of these persons is a member of Christ in the catalogue of the saints, unless at the end of their days they abandon their so foolish sect.

units.la: Augustinus et Hieronymus cū cæteris deserue-runt sectas istas, & sic religiosi nostri possent re-ligionem suā mendosam deserere, & Christi reli-gione, relicta sua apostasia, sapienter accipere.
units.tr: Augustine and Jerome, along with the others, abandoned those sects. So our religious could abandon their faulty religion and, leaving behind their apostasy, wisely embrace the religion of Christ.

units.la: A probabili creditur q; uacata beneficia ab episcopis uocatis et rectoribus forēt omnino su-spensa, et gratis euangelizantes haberet strictæ uitæ necessaria suspensis omnibus traditionibus an ti christi.
units.tr: It is believed, on probable grounds, that benefices left vacant by the bishops, the called ministers and the rectors would be entirely suspended, and that those who preach the gospel freely would have what a strict life requires; with all the traditions of Antichrist suspended.

units.la: Puræ & perpetuæ eleëmosinæ sunt præsumptiones stolidæ, per artem diaboli usurpatæ, imò nomen puræ & perpetuæ eleëmosinæ est sophisticate diaboli, adinuentum.
units.tr: Pure and perpetual alms are foolish presumptions, usurped through the devil's craft; indeed, the name "pure and perpetual alms" is a sophistry of the devil, invented for the purpose.

units.la: Papa non habet potestatem condendi hanc legem. Omnis utriusq; sexus, &c.
units.tr: The pope has no power to enact this law. Every person of either sex, etc.

units.la: Panis ille qui corpus Christi est, & vinum quod est sanguis Domini, quandoq; fit mucidus & acidum.
units.tr: That bread which is the body of Christ, and the wine which is the blood of the Lord, sometimes becomes mouldy and sour.

units.la: Papa, prælati, & quicunq; nominant se Christianos, contrarij dictæ fidei, de quidditate hostiæ consecratæ, dum pertinaciter illud defenderint, sunt hæretici manifesti.
units.tr: The pope, the prelates, and whoever call themselves Christians but oppose the said faith concerning the quiddity of the consecrated host, as long as they stubbornly defend it, are manifest heretics.

units.la: Sicut Deus necessitat futuritionem instantiū, sic necessitat omnes euentus qui in illis sunt futuri.
units.tr: Just as God necessitates the futurition of things about to happen, so he necessitates all the events that are to be in them.

units.la: Vtile foret ecclesiæ poni in pristina libertate, & sic cessarent missarum solennia superaddita rum, & orationes cum horis canonicis adinuentæ, licet enim istæ tres adinuentiones humanæ per accidens prosint ecclesiæ, non tantū quantum peccatum diaboli.
units.tr: It would be useful for the Church to be restored to its former liberty, and then the solemn masses added on, and the prayers with the canonical hours, invented by men, would cease. For although these three human inventions benefit the Church incidentally, they do not benefit it nearly as much as the sin of the devil harms it.

units.la: Nescio excusare peccata sanctorum, qui traditiones istas inuenerunt, cum melius occuparetur paretur Ecclesia & devotius Deum coleret, libere seruando consuetudines Apostolicas: licet non fuerit cum humanis ritibus desponsata.
units.tr: I cannot excuse the sins of the saints who devised these traditions, since the Church would have been better occupied and would have worshipped God more devoutly by freely keeping the apostolic customs, which were never wedded to human rites.

units.la: Multa sunt licita, & meritoria, quorum dispensatio & obligationis fundatio est peccatum, sicut est de istis traditionibus hominum adinuentis, & sic est sentiendum de ieiunijs per Ecclesiam institutis, &c.
units.tr: Many things are lawful and meritorious, but the dispensing of them and the founding of obligation upon them is sin. This is the case with these human traditions that have been invented, and so one should judge the fasts instituted by the Church, etc.

units.la: Euidentius foret ad euidentiam Ecclesiae quod Basilicarum sumptuosarum structurae, & sectae nouorum ordinum, sicut in die iudicij iam cessarent. Et ita multae festiuitates sub fuco hypocrisis introductae, ad utilitatem et liberationem Ecclesiae delerentur.
units.tr: It would be more evident to the Church's advantage if the building of sumptuous basilicas and the sects of new orders were now to cease, as they will on the day of judgment. And so many feasts, introduced under the cloak of hypocrisy, would be abolished for the Church's benefit and deliverance.

units.la: Vtile foret Ecclesiae quod non esset papa uel praelatus Caesarius, & decens foret & utile sicut erit post diem iudicij, quod Ecclesia foret ab eorum traditionibus expurgata. Ibidem.
units.tr: It would be useful for the Church if there were no pope or Caesarean prelate, and it would be fitting and useful, as it will be after the day of judgment, that the Church be purged of their traditions. Ibidem.

units.la: Corpus Christi non est substantialiter in sacramento altaris, attendedo ad corpus Christi secundum naturam suam, sed est ibi substantialiter, corporaliter & dimentionaliter attendendo ad modum hostiae secundum naturam suam.
units.tr: The body of Christ is not substantially in the sacrament of the altar when considered according to its own nature; but it is there substantially, bodily and dimensionally when considered according to the mode of the host, according to the host's own nature.

units.la: Sacramentum altaris est naturaliter panis et uinu & sacramentaliter corpus Christi, quanuis alij fingunt ipsum esse accidens sine substantia subiecta.
units.tr: The sacrament of the altar is naturally bread and wine, and sacramentally the body of Christ, although others feign that it is an accident without an underlying substance.

units.la: Oportet deponere infundabile blasphemiam de fictis miraculis accidentis.
units.tr: The unfoundable blasphemy concerning the fictitious miracles of accidents must be put away.

units.la: Fructus illius dementiae qua fingitur accidens sine subiecto foret blasphemare in Deum, scanda lisare sanctos, & illudere Ecclesiae per mendacia accidentis.
units.tr: The fruit of that madness by which an accident without a subject is feigned would be to blaspheme God, to scandalize the saints, and to mock the Church with the lies of accidents.

units.la: Cum pertinet ad Imperatorem, & alios reges, qui contra legem Dei Ecclesiam, stulte dederunt, sibi satisfacere: videtur quod ad illos pertinet bona potestatiue restituere brachio seculari, cū propter hanc causam gladiu suum portent.
units.tr: Since it belongs to the Emperor and the other kings, who foolishly gave to the Church against the law of God, to make satisfaction to themselves, it seems that it belongs to them to restore by their power those goods to the secular arm, since they bear the sword for this very cause.

units.la: Videtur quod quicunque papa vel praelatus Ecclesiae, isti restitutioni restiterit: est manifestus haereticus, legi Christi contrarius, & per consequens tanquam perturbator pacis Ecclesiae, a fidelibus remouendus.
units.tr: It seems that any pope or prelate of the Church who resists this restitution is a manifest heretic, contrary to the law of Christ, and consequently, as a disturber of the Church's peace, is to be removed by the faithful.

units.la: Non videtur magna prudentia eleemosinatis dare eleemosinam diuturniorem, quam sit tempus quod Deus donauerit ad merendum.
units.tr: It does not seem great prudence for almsgivers to give alms that last longer than the time God has granted for earning merit.

units.la: Cum Deus aeternus limitet ad panem quotidianum dandum hodie: non debet quis secundum rationem eleemosinae perpetuae recipere quicquam ab homine.
units.tr: Since the eternal God limits the giving of daily bread to today, one should not, on the reasoning of perpetual alms, receive anything at all from a man.

units.la: Quaestiones extractae per Vualdenum.
units.tr: Questions extracted by Waldensis.

units.la: Clerus magis intoxicatus fuit per dotationem huiusmodi quam fuisset ex licentia data coniugibus {·}utendi, cum non tam expresse fuit clero inhibitum sic habere uxores eo quod Petrus, & alij Apostoli uxores proprias, & non possessiones proprias licite habuerunt.
units.tr: The clergy were more intoxicated by such endowment than they would have been by the licence given to married people to use wives, since it was not so expressly forbidden to the clergy to keep wives in this way, because Peter and the other Apostles lawfully had their own wives but not their own possessions.

units.la: Christus omnino à tali dominio se seruauit, sicut & eius Apostoli, quare ergo non nos eorum uicarij, cum tam expressum mandatum ad hoc habemus in lege Domini, non autem ad continendum nos ab opere coniugali? Ideo timendum est nobis ne pharisaice excolamus culicem, & deglucamus camelum.
units.tr: Christ kept himself entirely free of such lordship, as did his Apostles. Why then are we not their vicars, since we have so express a command for this in the law of the Lord, but none for restraining ourselves from the conjugal act? Therefore we must take care that we do not Pharisaically strain out a gnat and swallow a camel.

units.la: Postquam hypocritæ plus magnificarūt traditiones hominū, quàm legę scripturæ: horrebant desponsatione præsbyteri ut uenenū, sed fornicationem etiam secundum species turpissimas acceptarunt, fides tamen scripturæ desponsationem sacerdotis non prohibet, & fornicationem prohibet generaliter in quolibet seculari.
units.tr: Since hypocrites have magnified the traditions of men more than the law of Scripture, they shrank from a priest's marriage as from poison, yet they accepted fornication even in its most shameful forms. The faith of Scripture, however, does not forbid a priest's marriage, and it forbids fornication in general for any layman.

units.la: Renunciatio temporalium titulo seculariter pof fidedi cuicunq; clerico debet competere, & qui sen tit se minus dispositum ad sic viuendum, de parte Domini abstineat ab officio clericali. Nec videó quomodo repugnaret legi diuinæ, quod clericus sentiens se inhabilè ad illud officiū, ad seculum recedat, quod licet temeritate quadam deliquerit, sed non tantum quantum fungens officio clericali
units.tr: Renunciation of temporal goods, which by secular title ought to belong to any cleric who holds property, should be made by whoever feels himself less fit to live in this way; let him withdraw from the Lord's portion and abstain from the clerical office. Nor do I see how it would be contrary to the divine law for a cleric who feels himself unfit for that office to return to the world. Though he may have offended by some rashness, he has not offended as much as one who discharges the clerical office while unfit for it.

units.la: COLLECTANEA QVAEDAM EX Reginaldi Pecoki Episcopi Ciceftrenfis opusculis exustis conseruata, et ex antiquo psegmate transcripta.
units.tr: A Certain Collection Preserved from the Booklets of Reginald Pecock, Bishop of Chichester, Which Were Burned, and Transcribed from an Old Copy

units.la: SI dicitis mihi quòd uirtus est in imagine, quia est in aqua benedicta uirtus Spiritus sancti, unde Ambrosius lib. de offic. Et Presbiter in sanctificando fontem, sic orat, descendat uirtus Spiritus sancti in pleni-tudinem fontis. Respondeo, Ambrosius fuit deceptus in illo, & plu-res alij antiqui Doctores. Vbi fun-dant se super ratione, uel scriptura, tenendi sunt, Aliter non. Sic de Ec-clesia dici potest admittendo idem officiū, quod non est merę fidei, sed opinionis, quia non est inconuenien-s tenere, quòd Ecclesia potest falli, & decipi: Vel potest dici quòd intelle-ctus Ambrosij, & Ecclesię est quòd Spiritus sanctus erit assistens aquæ sanctificatæ, & operans in ipsa aqua, uirtutę personæ baptizatæ, quæ uir-tus, tus, erit gratia, uel ipsa uirtus quæ dicitur uirtus Spiritus sancti, non est aliud, quàm concessio Spiritus sancti, quia promisit assistere & iuuare aquâ fontis quâdo puer baptizatur, et ipsa concessio Spiritus sancti, non est res permanes in aqua, sic nec uirtus Spiritus sancti (de qua Ambrosius, & Ecclesia loquitur) est permanes in aqua, sed permanet in Spiritu sancto. Hoc in lib. suo de signis Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: If you tell me that there is power in the image because the power of the Holy Spirit is in holy water, as Ambrose says in his book On the Duties (De officiis), and the priest, in consecrating the font, prays thus: "Let the power of the Holy Spirit descend into the fullness of the font." I answer that Ambrose was deceived in this, as were several other ancient doctors. Where they rest their view on reason or Scripture, they are to be held; otherwise not. So it may be said of the Church, while granting the same point, that this is not a matter of pure faith but of opinion, since it is not inconsistent to hold that the Church can err and be deceived. Or it may be said that the meaning of Ambrose and of the Church is this: the Holy Spirit will be present to the sanctified water and will work in the water itself, the power of the person baptized, and this power will be grace. Or the power called the power of the Holy Spirit is nothing other than the grant of the Holy Spirit, because he promised to be present and to help the water of the font when the child is baptized. And that grant of the Holy Spirit is not a thing that remains in the water; so neither is the power of the Holy Spirit (of which Ambrose and the Church speak) remaining in the water, but it remains in the Holy Spirit. This is in his book On the Signs of the Church.

units.la: Videtur quòd Moses ex informatione, qua ex inspiratione, fecit Pentateuchum, &c. non est, in ipso casu, recurrere ad miraculum, sicut temere & inconsulte facit Gregorius super Ezechielem. Item quia de Iudæis erant aliqui boni, uidetur quod semper habuerūt fidem in scriptis: Ideo dicere, sicut multi Doctores dicunt, cum magistris historiarū, quod Esdras per inspirationē reparat libros legis, sine copia, est quid fictitium, quia est sine euidentia
units.tr: It seems that Moses wrote the Pentateuch from information, or from inspiration, etc. In this case it is not necessary to have recourse to a miracle, as Gregory does rashly and inconsiderately in his commentary on Ezekiel. Likewise, since there were some good men among the Jews, it seems they always had the faith in writings. Therefore to say, as many doctors say with the masters of histories, that Ezra by inspiration restored the books of the law without a copy, is something fictitious, because it is without evidence.

units.la: Hinc quæritur an tota Ecclesia in terra potest facere de nouo, aliquem articulum esse fidem qui non fuerit ante in se fides. Dico quod fides uno modo dicitur cognitio, qua cognoscitur uerus articulus, & sic fides sumitur proprie. Secundo modo sumitur pro articulo scilicet cognito tamen improprie, tum sic primo igitur sumedo fidem quæ est cognitio, qua consentimus articulo supra capacitatem nostræ rationis, scilicet quia Deus affirmat. Tum rursus secundo sumendo fidem, pro uerita te sic cognita, Et neutrū istius fidei potest Ecclesia de nouo facere ad uo luntatem propriam, quia non est in potestate Ecclesiæ uniuersalis, facere uerum uel falsum, quod Maria concepit filium. Quia in istis Ecclesia tantum testificatur, quod talis articulus est fides. Et Ecclesiæ est, determinare, quis articulus debet sumi pro fide; Et maioris fortitudinis no uideo determinationem Ecclesiae esse, sed potius credere per Ecclesiam quod hic dies est ieiunabilis, uel dies festiuus &c.
units.tr: Hence the question arises whether the whole Church on earth can newly make some article to be of faith which before was not of faith in itself. I say that faith is taken in one way for knowledge, by which a true article is known, and in this sense faith is taken properly. In a second way it is taken for the article itself as known, though improperly. Taking faith first as knowledge, by which we assent to an article beyond the capacity of our reason, namely because God affirms it; then again, taking faith secondly for the truth so known, neither kind of faith can the Church newly make at its own will. For it is not in the power of the universal Church to make true or false that Mary conceived the Son. In these matters the Church only testifies that such an article is faith. And it belongs to the Church to determine which article ought to be taken as faith. I do not see the Church's determination to be of greater strength in this, but rather that through the Church we believe that this day is a fast day, or a feast day, and so on.

units.la: Item Ecclesia non determinauit scripta quatuor doctorum esse uera, sed admisit sumi in studio legentium cum libertate iudicandi, sicut te- uidentiae possunt mouere. Quae scripta non fuissent sic in reuerētia sumpta nisi fuissent admissa, sicut repudiauit scripta haereticorum.
units.tr: Likewise the Church did not determine that the writings of the four doctors are true, but admitted that they be taken up in the study of readers, with freedom of judgment, as the evidences may move them. Those writings would not have been held in such reverence unless they had been admitted, just as it rejected the writings of heretics.

units.la: Item non est idem credere sanctam Ecclesiam catholicam esse, & credere sanctae Ecclesiae catholicae. Quia per id quod ponitur in symbolo (Credo sanctam Ecclesiam) uirtute uerborum istorum non plus sentitur, quam Credo sanctam Ecclesiam catholicam esse, & remissionem peccatorum esse, & non quicquid uniuersalis Ecclesia dicit est uerum, quia statim post Apostolos, haeretici dixerunt, diuersas Ecclesias esse, ideo ponebatur, Credo sanctam Ecclesiam catholicam, quod idem est, quod uniuersalem orthodoxam, & gloriosam: Ideo quaelibet Ecclesia dicitur orthodoxa, quamuis non catholica. Nam Ecclesia sic statuit in symbolo, Credo in Deum Patrem, in Filium, in Spiritum sanctum. Sed non dicit, Credo in sanctam Ecclesiam catholicam, sed Credo sanctam Ecclesiam id est generalem Ecclesiam esse.
units.tr: It is not the same to believe that the holy Catholic Church is, and to believe in the holy Catholic Church. By what is placed in the creed ("I believe the holy Church"), the force of these words conveys no more than "I believe the holy Catholic Church is, and the remission of sins is," and not that whatever the universal Church says is true. For immediately after the Apostles, heretics said that there were various churches; therefore it was set down, "I believe the holy Catholic Church," which means the same as "the universal, orthodox and glorious" Church. Thus any church is called orthodox, though not catholic. For the Church thus lays down in the creed: "I believe in God the Father, in the Son, in the Holy Spirit." But it does not say, "I believe in the holy Catholic Church," but "I believe the holy Church," that is, that the Church is general.

units.la: Item Ecclesia non potest esse fundamentum uel regula fidei Ecclesiae, quia determinatio est effectus cleri, uel Ecclesiae, & potuit non fieri. Igitur non potest esse fundamentum suae Ecclesiae, quia sentitur, quod clerus sic determinans non capit fidem ab illa determinatione.
units.tr: Likewise the Church cannot be the foundation or rule of faith of the Church, because a determination is an effect of the clergy or of the Church, and it could have not been made. Therefore it cannot be the foundation of its own Church, because it is felt that the clergy making such a determination does not take its faith from that determination.

units.la: Item quandocunque Ecclesia determinauit articulum esse fidem, prius uidit ipsum articulum esse fidem, aliter determinasset ipsum articulum sine uisu quo determinasset, quia serì titur quòd ecclesia fuit in fide illius articuli, antequam determinauit ipsum articulum non potuit habuisse fidem sine fundamento ipsius fidei; & cum determinatio est posteri or, non potest esse fundamentum prioris: nec effectus fundat causam: tamen laici debent obedire determinationi ecclesiæ, nisi sciant improbare sic denunciantem uel testificante ipsum articulum esse fidem.
units.tr: Whenever the Church has determined an article to be faith, it first saw that the article itself was faith; otherwise it would have determined the article without the sight by which it made the determination. For it is agreed that the Church was in the faith of that article before it determined the article. It could not have had faith without the foundation of that faith; and since a determination comes later, it cannot be the foundation of what came before, nor can an effect found its cause. Nevertheless, laymen ought to obey the Church's determination, unless they know that the one announcing it is wrong, or that the article itself is not faith.

units.la: Item sacra scriptura in sensu litera li intellecta secundum uerum iudicium rationis, est sufficiēs regula fidei ecclesiæ, tamen laicis determinatio est secunda regula uel particularis. Nam si in istis uerbis, Credo ecclesiam catholicam, intelligeretur quasi dicat credo esse uerum quicquid ecclesia determinat, tunc sequeretur quòd sicut intelligeretur idem, credo sanctorum communionem, idem esset, quasi credo uerum esse
units.tr: Likewise, Holy Scripture, understood in the literal sense according to the true judgment of reason, is a sufficient rule of faith for the Church; yet for laymen the determination is a second or particular rule. For if in these words, "I believe the Catholic Church," it were understood as if it said, "I believe it true whatever the Church determines," then it would follow that, just as the same thing would be understood by "I believe the communion of saints," it would amount to "I believe it true
